2593.blurb: Rodgers spent the majority of last offseason pondering his NFL future before landing in Pittsburgh on a one-year deal with Mike Tomlin. In classic Steelers fashion, Rodgers did enough to help them stay competitive and make the playoffs, but they ultimately fell short in the Wild Card Round. Back with the Steelers again, at this point in his career, the vet isn't really on the radar for fantasy outside of 2QB formats.
2593.dyn: Now 42 years old, Rodgers and the Steelers seemed like a one-year fling, but they hired his old coach, Mike McCarthy, to replace Tomlin. In dynasty, you are constantly guessing on the next plot twist in the reality show known as Aaron Rodgers.

9038.blurb: It was an all-time season for the future Hall of Famer, becoming one of six QBs ever with 4700 passing yards & 46 TDs in a season. It wasn’t just stat-padding, as his nine top-6 finishes were the most among all QBs. 33 of his 46 TDs were inside the red zone, by far the most in the league. We caution going all-in on non-mobile QBs coming off a year where his TD rate went to the moon. Stafford will likely settle into low-end QB1 territory, but you have an opportunity to scoop him up as your team’s QB2 to pair with another.
9038.dyn: Is this a chance for one last ride? Every year, we ask that question, knowing the 38-year-old has one final year under contract with the Rams. With $408 million in career earnings, Stafford has made more money than any other player in NFL history. It is probably best just to ride off into the dynasty sunset with him.

tags.bust: Scared of regression? Listen, we get it: it is tough to repeat 46 passing TDs and an MVP season. Let this stat put his career into context: through 17(!) seasons, Stafford has never put up back-to-back seasons of 27+ TDs ever. Those goal-line TDs we were so used to seeing for Davante Adams could easily shift in 2026 as McVay puts his offensive imagination to the test. We do not consider him an every week start and thus not someone we are leaving our drafts with unless he is paired with another QB.

14252.blurb: After two middling years in Atlanta, Cousins signed a “five-year” contract with Las Vegas, but only $11.3 million was guaranteed. He reunites with Klint Kubiak, who was his play-caller during his time in Minnesota. Expect Captain Kirk to potentially start the beginning of the season before giving way to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. In other words, Cousins is a first-round pick in your “QB-mentors-only” leagues but off the radar for fantasy in any other format.
14252.dyn: Uncle Kirk is loaded! With $321 million in career earnings, Cousins trails only Tom Brady and Matthew Stafford in his quest to somehow earn more money than any other player in NFL history. In dynasty, he has a limited opportunity to start at the beginning of the year before Mendoza takes over.

14895.blurb: You cannot make this stuff up - the Jets traded for Geno Smith, coming full circle on a player they once took in the second round of the NFL Draft way back in 2013! He was a shell of himself last year in Las Vegas, ranking dead last among all QBs in sack rate (10.6%) and INTs (17). For fantasy purposes, Geno is off the radar, but we would be satisfied if he gives Garrett Wilson 200 targets. At some point, expect the Jets to eventually replace him with fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik for a few starts as they look to 2027’s QB class.
14895.dyn: Consider him a bridge-type QB as they likely attack the position aggressively in the 2027 NFL Draft. It is wild to think Geno has been around since 2013.

15048.blurb: Quietly the TE4 in 2025, Kelce finished as the TE8 or better every year as a starter, reminding us he is a true fantasy football legend. Louder for the people in the back! He had a solid 851 yards receiving (TE4) with 584 routes run (TE2), and you can continue to expect to see him on the field as Patrick Mahomes’ good ole security blanket. We would like to see that TD total go up a bit - Kelce had five last year - but to be fair, no one on the team caught more than that number. He is a solid later-round pick if you wait on the TE position, knowing this is his latest ADP in more than a decade. Respect your elders.
15048.dyn: The “will-he-or-won’t-he” retire shenanigans continued in the off-season, as Swifties watched to see if Travis would return for one last ride. He signed a one-year, fully guaranteed $12 million deal in March, so expect him to give it his all. That won’t necessarily equate to high-end fantasy success as you ride off into the sunset with the all-timer.

15076.blurb: "Unc" still has it! The 34-year-old signed a one-year deal with the Colts in mid-August to link up with his former OC, Shane Steichen. The vet was quietly productive last year in Los Angeles leading the team with 81 receptions. Obviously, his best days are behind him but the savvy veteran still knows the nuances of getting open in zone coverage in the short area of the field. With Alec Pierce likely starting the year slowly recovering from his injury, old man Keenan could have some WR3/FLEX weeks in full PPR leagues. The key for fantasy is going to be figuring out how this affects his new teammates as he and Josh Downs are both best when playing out of the slot.
15076.dyn: If you're a contender and need some depth, Keenan probably won't cost more than a 3rd round rookie pick via trade. Obviously, at age 34 with just one year on his contract there's no long term value, but he's a fine bench stash in full PPR leagues. He is 48 receptions away from vaulting to 3rd all-time among NFL WRs in catches securing his status as one of the true GOATs. Respect this man!

16470.blurb: Adams is coming off arguably the best season ever for a WR inside-the-five as he became the team’s “goal-line WR”. He saw the most targets (16) inside the 5-yard line since targets became a stat (1992). Nevertheless, the warning signs are there as he totaled just 789 receiving yards and now enters his age-33 season. When we couple that with Matthew Stafford’s outlier TD season, it is hard to be bullish on Adams repeating as a WR1 for fantasy. We view him more as a WR3, as his price tag in drafts is a bit too rich for us.
16470.dyn: Adams enters his final year under contract and his 13th season in the NFL. He could be someone at your league’s trade deadline you flip to a contending team searching for WR help. Our research shows that the greatest decline in fantasy production for aging WRs is between the age 32 and 33 seasons, right where Adams is for 2026.

16597.blurb: For the first time in his career, Mike Evans won’t be wearing a Bucs uniform. Weird! He is now in San Francisco as he chases another ring with the Niners. Historically speaking, there is an increased risk with veterans changing teams at this stage of their career. It was a tough 2025 season for the elder statesman, who missed a ton of time with hamstring and collarbone injuries. He will be 33 this season, so be mindful of his ADP throughout the summer. If he gets steamed up, we are hesitant to chase him up the board, but if he falls, there is double-digit TD upside with Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan, especially with George Kittle coming off a torn Achilles and Ricky Pearsall out for the year
16597.dyn: San Fran essentially signed Evans to a year-to-year contract, so we are not exactly sure how long he will play. At 33 years old with a significant injury history, the dynasty value is all but gone. If you are a contender, you are just riding it out at this point with the future Hall of Famer.

16906.blurb: After one season in New England paired with Drake Maye, the veteran WR finds himself in Washington with Jayden Daniels, another young star QB. Despite being one of the oldest starting WRs in the league, Diggs was quietly very productive with 85 receptions and over 1,000 yards on a league-leading 85% catch rate. His per-route metrics (2.53 YPRR) behind-the-scenes also suggest he is not quite done. He forms a solid old man receiving duo with Terry McLaurin and should step right into a 20+ % target share on a Commanders team desperate for pass-catchers. Consider Diggs a discounted FLEX option at your drafts on an offense that could be in a ton of shootouts.
16906.dyn: Leading into his age-33 season, Diggs clearly has something left in the tank. He was targeted on 25% of his routes and continues to buoy his dynasty life well past the normal WR age curve. He is a short-term PPR option at best.

16964.blurb: The Wallerus is back - GOO GOO GAJOO! He had his moments at times last year with the Dolphins, but he was never a full time player and missed time yet again with another injury. Entering his age 34 season, we're not particularly jazzed about a declining player on what should be a low-volume pass offense, but he reminded us last year that he can still be a red zone weapon in the right matchup. Perhaps he'll fine his way into a waiver wire show at some point this season, but for now, you don't need to be drafting him in redraft formats.
16964.dyn: If he's on the waiver wire in your league, feel free to scoop him up and see what happens, but we're keeping our expectations in check. Waller is only in Carolina on a one-year deal.

17922.blurb: Impress your friends by letting them know the only QBs to finish inside the top-10 at the position each of the last four years: Josh Allen, Jalen Hurts, and… drumroll… Jared Goff. The first half was middling with just one top-12 finish, but he responded when things mattered for fantasy, averaging 20.3 fantasy points per game from Weeks 10-16. He imploded in Week 17 at Minnesota (two INTs, three fumbles, five sacks), but that is the game you play with Goff. He offers nothing in the run game, keeping his ceiling around that QB10 mark. The Lions are favored in 14 of their first 15 games, including a juicy Week 1 matchup at home against the Saints. We know what Goff is at this point: a streaky s
17922.dyn: Goff is the perfect QB2 in dynasty attached to a high-powered offense, yet likely undervalued by your league mates. He is signed through 2028 and somehow still only 31 years old.

17959.blurb: You can tell your grandkids you lived through the glory years known as "Derrick Henry SZN". He is an absolute fantasy legend finishing 2025 with his eighth straight season of double-digit rushing TDs. He saw the most carries inside the 5-yard line of his career and ranked third among all RBs in yards per carry. “Father Time” is usually undefeated when it comes to 30+ year old RBs, but Henry has kicked him outside the wrestling ring the last couple of years. Our projections still have him ranked as a low-end RB1 with a slight deduction in full PPR leagues.
17959.dyn: The future Hall of Famer is under contract for two more years as he carries a team-friendly $5.5 million cap hit in 2026 that balloons to $16.2 in 2027.  It is worth noting that since 2010, only one 32+ year old RB has had a double-digit TD season: DeAngelo Williams (PIT) in 2015 had 11 rushing TDs. If you have Henry in dynasty, you could entertain offers or just ride this man into the sunset!

tags.value: Ageists have been trying to sink the King for years, and yet it feels like he grows stronger and stronger. Maybe the hate fuels him! As the lead back on a team projected for a league-leading 11.5 wins, why is Derrick Henry so low in ADP this year? Anyone want a shot at double-digit TDs in the third round? Our projections for the 32-year-old remain strong as he remains one of the great outliers of fantasy football.

17975.blurb: Henry was quietly the TE6 on a team where he was second in targets with 87, just behind Stefon Diggs with 102. The problem with Henry was that you never seemed to know when to start him, as he surpassed eight fantasy points per game in less than half of his games (47%). Henry’s weekly uncertainty might not improve much with the addition of AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs. Henry seems to consistently be undervalued in drafts, making him an easy trigger to pull at the end or a pickup off waivers as your second TE on a deep roster.
17975.dyn: Henry signed a 2-year extension in August to remain the Patriots top TE option. He will be playing his 10th season in 2026, so you probably won’t get much in a trade for him. Hold on and see if you can use him in prime matchups.

18018.blurb: Where’s the Beef? Brissett was cookin’ last year for fantasy purposes, averaging over 40 pass attempts per game in his starts. His nine consecutive top-12 fantasy finishes were the most of 2025, thanks in large part to the team trailing on 73% of his dropbacks. Despite the fact that the Cardinals went 1-11 in his starts, he remains the incumbent veteran starter with Kyler Murray now donning Viking purple. He remains on the streaming radar, although we expect the passing volume to slightly decrease with new head coach Mike LaFleur calling the shots.
18018.dyn: You need to be counting your blessings in a SuperFlex dynasty league that the 33-year-old Brissett continues to be relevant as a QB2. The window of his opportunity will be closing as the Cardinals look forward to finding a new franchise QB.

18055.blurb: Another year and another opportunity for fantasy managers to disrespect the Dallas franchise QB. His ten top-10 weekly finishes tied Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford for most among QBs as he led the NFL in completions and set career highs in passing yards and attempts. He did have massive splits in Cowboys wins (24.0 ppg) and losses (12.7), the largest gap of any QB in 2025. Blessed with a historically bad defense, Cowboys games averaged 58 combined points, always giving Dak and company a chance to jump into a shootout.  We love us some Dak.
18055.dyn: His age (almost 33) keeps his dynasty value at bay, but he is under contract for another three years. In SuperFlex leagues, he is the type of QB2 we love trying to work a deal for during the lulls of the off-season.

tags.value: The Rodney Dangerfield of fantasy football continues to be disrespected by fantasy managers. The passing volume is consistent, and the team throws inside the red zone, as evidenced by his 13 passing TDs inside the 5-yard line. If you pass on the elite QBs early in your drafts, let your league mates spend mid-round draft capital knowing Dak is available in the later rounds as a “backstop” for your team. Dak finished as a top-12 QB every single full season of his career, and we expect that trend to continue again in 2026.

18422.blurb: Raymond had a bit role with the Lions as an undersized slot receiver who primarily contributed on special teams. Ironically, he is now reunited with Ben Johnson in Chicago, so he should have no issues carving out a nice little role for the Bears. We do not expect that role to be fantasy relevant.
18422.dyn: Raymond should not be on a dynasty roster at this point in time…or ever.

18857.blurb: This is a tricky situation in Cleveland. We have not seen Watson be meaningful in fantasy since (checks… rechecks) 2020! Seriously, he averaged 13.2 fantasy points per game in 18 starts over multiple years, dealing with injuries and the scrutiny of NFL fans and the media. The Browns have named Watson as their Week 1 starter, but he is nowhere near consideration for fantasy outside of deeper 2QB leagues. We expect Shedeur Sanders to make starts at some point this season.
18857.dyn: The Browns converted nearly $45 million of his salary into a signing bonus for the third year in a row, kicking the can down the road for arguably the worst sports contract of all-time. He is in the final year of his deal, but in dynasty, he is basically worthless as a potential short-term QB3.

18876.blurb: Njoku is joining the Chargers on a one-year deal, and he joins a room with the new hotness, Oronde Gadsden, and blocking TE Charlie Kolar. Njoku was quickly usurped by rookie Harold Fannin Jr. in Cleveland last season, so it is unclear how he will be used in Mike McDaniel’s offense. You need to keep an eye on how the team functions and read the tea leaves in case you need to grab him from waivers early in the season.
18876.dyn: Njoku turns 30 this year and is coming off a knee injury that robbed him of the final four games of the 2025 season. If someone is offering up something for him trade-wise after he has a decent game, it might be time to send Njoku away with a thank-you note and a box of chocolates.

18877.blurb: This is the stuff fantasy dreams are made of. If you called your shot with CMC in 2025, oh baby, were you living large while the rest of your league mates cowered in fear due to “he’s gonna get injured” fears. The RB1 was a consistency monster as essentially two players in one for fantasy. Using only his receiving stats, he would have been the WR11 in half-point leagues or the WR8 in full PPR. He tied Amon-Ra St. Brown for the league lead in red zone receptions while totaling a whopping 413 touches, the most by a fantasy RB since DeMarco Murray in 2014. Whew! That type of workload suggests some regression is coming for the 30-year-old, but we still have him ranked as a top-5 RB. He is him, a
18877.dyn: CMC is an all-timer for fantasy football. If you have ever had the opportunity to experience and inhabit a CMC #1 overall season, you likely won your league. However, we are not here to pat your back, but instead offer a word of caution. Since 2020, 11 RBs saw 330+ touches in a regular season; ALL of them saw a decrease of 45+ touches the following year, and only two played a full season. He can still be awesome for 2026, but we would advise shopping him in your league to get an absolute haul. T

18878.blurb: From his rookie year in 2017 until 2024, only Derrick Henry scored more fantasy points than Alvin Kamara. He was truly a generational fantasy back and arguably the most dependable pass-catcher at the RB position. He hit a fantasy wall in 2025, averaging the fewest yards per carry (3.6) of his career while scoring one total TD and bowing out to an injury in Week 12. With the signing of Travis Etienne Jr., it remains to be seen what type of role he will have in this offense in 2026. You might see the name in your player pool, but remind yourself that the good ole days are gone. On top of Kamara's decline as a player, he's now dealing with a sprained MCL that is expected to sideline him for the
18878.dyn: Kamara's time in New Orleans looked like it was coming to a close, but they curiously extended him in 2024 and now are paying for it. He has one year remaining on his deal with a $10 million cap hit and several void years of kicking his contract down the road further. For dynasty purposes, if you can get anything for him, congratulations. If not, remember the good times.

18880.blurb: Can we go into Madden and turn off injuries here? Before that nasty ankle fracture-dislocation in 2024, Godwin was putting up some unreal numbers, but ever since that injury, his efficiency has taken a hit, with his yards per reception declining in three straight seasons. Mike Evans’ departure theoretically opens up a world where Godwin can bounce back, so we do not mind adding him in drafts as a WR3/4 for your squad, but the upside we have seen in the past is unlikely to repeat at this stage of his career. He certainly gets a small boost in full PPR leagues.
18880.dyn: Godwin has been a dynasty stalwart for years, but those days are long gone, mostly because of injury and age. Rod God is now 30 years old, and he is coming off back-to-back injury-affected seasons while averaging just 3.7 catches per game. Sadly, we view him as an expiring asset, even if he is able to have a solid 2026 campaign.

tags.value: Godwin is not the sexiest name to click in your drafts. However, with Emeka Egbuka battling a toe issue, it would not shock us if Godwin is the clear target leader at the beginning of the season and a weekly PPR start. He will be the starting slot receiver for Baker Mayfield and a reliable FLEX option if you are looking for WR depth later in your draft.

18882.blurb: We will always remember the good times, Coop. The former Fantasy MVP has slowly morphed into a role player at this stage of his career, but ya know what? This man just won another Super Bowl, so he is probably doing okay! We will always love you, CoopaKuppaCoffee, but sadly, your days as a fantasy starter are long gone. We view Kupp as a potential injury fill-in should JSN or Rashid Shaheed miss time.
18882.dyn: The time to cash in on Kupp in dynasty was about three years ago. So, at this point, you are just holding and using him in your lineup a couple of times per year when the injury bug bites or the bye weeks kick in.

18890.blurb: After a year in which the Chiefs failed to make the playoffs, and Mahomes tore his left ACL in Week 15, we have to reassess the aura surrounding the Kansas City QB. It is going to be really fascinating to track his recovery all offseason as he comes off the ACL plus LCL surgery. For fantasy, it is highly unlikely we will see the rushing production we saw in 2025, when Mahomes set career highs in per-game rushing attempts, yards, and TDs. The Chiefs are gifted with a “third-place” schedule and a core group willing to go for one more title run. The addition of Kenneth Walker III could take some pressure off Mahomes trying to Superman this thing every week. For fantasy purposes, he is a low-end
18890.dyn: Mahomes is the dude in KC. Forever and always...he is under contract through 2031. However, the star has lost some of his shine as we would consider him a solid but unspectacular top-10 QB in dynasty. Listen, we would love to have him on our rosters, but he is certainly not an “untouchable” in SuperFlex leagues.

tags.bust: This one hurts. We love Mahomes. Who doesn’t?! He is still viewed as one of, if not the, best QBs in the league, but for the game we play, 2026 may not be the year for Mahomes to be a difference-making fantasy QB. He is coming off a multi-ligament ACL injury, and the Chiefs did very little to add to their pass-catching corps. With Travis Kelce another year older and Kenneth Walker now in town to take the load off Mahomes, we don’t see him separating in a meaningful way for fantasy, especially if he is not going to scramble the way he did a year ago, coming off this serious knee injury. There is a chance his name value keeps his ADP too high for our liking.

18912.blurb: When Engram went to Denver in 2025, fantasy managers were hopeful that Sean Payton might have found his new Joker, but the role never really panned out. Engram set a career low in 2025 with 28.8 yards per game and finished the season with only one receiving TD, leaving us wondering if the TE6 and TE2 finishes of a few years prior were the outliers. Do not get your hopes up too much – the team traded for Jaylen Waddle in the offseason, added rookie Justin Joly in the draft, and, the most important part of the puzzle, they still have Adam Trautman. Targets will be even tougher to command, and you will never know when to start him - just remember the good times.
18912.dyn: Engram signed a two-year, $16.5 million guaranteed contract with Denver in 2025, giving his dynasty managers a spark of hope, but after his disappointing season, his value in dynasty has dropped drastically. The man turns 32 this year, so anything he gives you from here on out will be a delightful surprise.

18983.blurb: It has been a wonderful run for Conner, but it seems he finally will fade into the fantasy background. After four straight years as a top-20 RB and the engine of the Arizona offense, the 31-year-old missed the majority of 2025 with a right foot injury and will begin on injured reserve. It seems he will be buried on the depth chart behind Tyler Allgeier and rookie Jeremiyah Love.
18983.dyn: Conner is under contract for one more year. Rather than moving on from the 31-year-old and saving over $7 million against the cap, the team decided to restructure his deal to keep him on the roster for 2026.

18993.blurb: Old man Samaje Perine is in his final year under contract solely to annoy Chase Brown managers. He averaged seven opportunities per game last season, thanks to running more routes and catching more balls on third down than Brown. For redraft purposes, he is off our boards.
18993.dyn: It is a miracle the “Painbot” still lives on in the NFL. He enters his 10th year in the NFL and is a fringe bench player in dynasty.

19023.blurb: If your league awards points for aura, Mack Daddy is the 1.01. The shoeless wonder is a weekly must-see for his interesting stadium entrances. He was a solid player for New England on their Super Bowl run a year ago, but with AJ Brown joining the squad, he is not on the radar for fantasy.
19023.dyn: We are huge fans of Hollins’ Instagram account, where he shares all sorts of useful info for everyday tasks labeled #MackHacks. Oh, you came here for his dynasty value? It does not exist. But seriously, give the guy a follow on IG, and thank us later.

19045.blurb: After averaging 4.9 yards per carry for the first eight seasons of his career, Aaron Jones finally hit a wall in Year 9, setting career lows in yards per carry (4.2), rushing TDs (2), and yards after contact per attempt (2.67). He remains under contract for one more year in Minnesota, sharing the backfield with Jordan Mason. The Vikings begin the season with a rough three-week stretch (GB, @ CHI, @ TB) before things open up. We have him ranked as a low-end FLEX option with unknowns at the QB and betting that the wheels finally fall off of his insanely efficient career on a per-touch basis.
19045.dyn: Jones is hitting that RB age cliff (31 years old) and only has one more year on his deal. You likely will get nothing of value in a trade, so we recommend holding in hopes he bounces back in the TD department and the Minnesota offense returns to its norm with Kyler Murray under center.

19063.blurb: Oh, George. Times are tough. It is hard to get behind an almost 33-year-old TE heading into his 10th NFL season who is coming off an Achilles injury. If anyone can do it, you know it is Kittle; he has given us six seasons where he has finished as the TE5 or higher! The physical freak who has publicly said he is targeting an early-season return could be a value in fantasy drafts, if he drops far enough. Pair him with a vanilla-reliable TE that you can use confidently in the first half of your season, knowing you can pop Kittle on your IR. If he comes back even close to his past form late in the season, you have some options in your playoff push. We don’t suggest even entertaining the option u
19063.dyn: If you have Kittle in dynasty, you are holding as you would only be getting pennies on the dollar if you trade him. You might get lucky to obtain another solid year from him in 2027 post-Achilles, and after that, it might just be a “thank you so much for your service” farewell.

19318.blurb: Bourne will randomly pop up for monster games as he did in Weeks 5 and 6 last year. He hit 142 receiving yards exactly in back-to-back games and then (get this) averaged 18 receiving yards per game the rest of the year. Impress your buddies at your draft, saying “oh yeah, that guy is a Cardinal” before crossing him off your draft list.
19318.dyn: It feels like Bourne has lived 38 different lives in the NFL. This life he will be living as part of the Arizona Cardinals is not one you want to be part of.

19766.blurb: Coming off a legendary 2024 campaign and Super Bowl run, there were warning signs about regression coming across the board for Saquon and the Eagles' offense. He bottomed out in a number of areas, including plummeting from 17 runs of 20+ yards to only four in 2025. He also shockingly converted only one of his 13 carries inside the 5-yard line into a TD, but still volumed his way to finishing as the RB13. With an offensive coordinator change, we expect Saquon to bounce back in 2026 at a discounted price in the second round of your drafts. Your league mates might bring up the fact he was a “bust,” but we are willing to forgive and forget.
19766.dyn: Entering his age-29 season, this is the time to make a decision on Saquon based on your team’s competitive window. If you are a contender, you can expect one more year of elite production, but rebuilds should consider shopping him for at least a first-round pick and another young piece. He is under contract for two more seasons, but we are not valuing him as an elite asset beyond 2026.

19781.blurb: For the first three weeks of the season, it was vintage Lamar, averaging 27.6 fantasy points on the back of three passing TDs and 39 rushing yards per game. Unfortunately, a back injury altered his season and the future of the Baltimore Ravens. After returning in Week 9, he never quite looked like himself, averaging just 13.5 fantasy points, 1.2 passing TDs, and 20 rushing yards per game. With John Harbaugh out, it feels like a different era in Baltimore. Lamar’s raw pass attempts remain low yet continue to be the most valuable in fantasy: 40% were 10+ air yards (second highest in NFL) and 9% were “end-zone” attempts, the highest rate in the NFL. He remains in the annual top-5 QB conversatio
19781.dyn: At 29 years old, we still are in prime territory for a run of multiple dominant fantasy seasons. He is our consensus QB5 in startups. Don’t be the idiot sandwich in your league who got too cute trading away Lamar because you thought the “value” was too good to pass up.

19790.blurb: In Weeks 1-8, the magic we saw from “Laser” Mayfield in 2024 looked like it was here to stay. He was in the MVP conversation on the back of a 13:2 TD-to-INT ratio with the team eyeing the postseason. However, after the bye, Baker stumbled, throwing nine INTs while struggling to get there for fantasy. He battled through some injuries, his OL was banged up, and his pass-catchers never quite felt in sync. With Mike Evans gone, there are some question marks with the offense that now employs its fifth different play-caller in five years. Baker is another late-round QB that should only be drafted in 1QB leagues if you buy into Tampa Bay’s early season schedule.
19790.dyn: We are still believers in Mayfield, but Tampa does have some key decisions on their hands as he is in the final year of his current deal and entering his age-31 season. His 7.2% TD rate in 2024 looks a bit fluky, so instead of having a locked-in QB1, we have him more as a mid-tier QB2.

19800.blurb: Sutton’s target share is likely to take a hit with Jaylen Waddle now on the team. Shoot, there were even moments last season where Sutton was losing targets to guys like Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant. For context, he only averaged 7.3 targets per game for a 21.3% market share. If that comes down at all because of Waddle, Sutton could become TD dependent in 2026.
19800.dyn: Sutton has strung together some nice fantasy seasons in recent years, but the dynasty window could be closing somewhat quickly. He will turn 31 later this season, and now Jaylen Waddle is in town. The Broncos signed him to a big extension not that long ago, but that doesn’t necessarily mean he will continue to post great fantasy numbers. If you are a contender, you can likely hold and get multiple WR2 weeks, but we expect his dynasty value to take a pretty significant hit over the next two seaso

tags.bust: Sutton has been a great value in drafts in back-to-back seasons, finishing as the WR13 in both 2024 and 2025. Unfortunately, the numbers and the changing situation suggest that is probably not repeatable. Denver traded for Jaylen Waddle before the NFL Draft, and he is certainly going to steal some volume. That is a scary proposition for Sutton, who could become a TD-or-bust option in 2026. The veteran also turns 31 later this year, and that is usually around the age where we start to see non-elite WRs trend down in terms of their efficiency.

19801.blurb: He is him. While technically Allen finished with his lowest fantasy points per game average since 2019, he continued his streak of being the QB1 or QB2 for the sixth consecutive season. In 2024, Allen became the first top-5 fantasy QB without a top-36 scoring WR or top-12 TE. In 2025, he did it again. Same exact thing. Yes, he is now 30 years old, and the Bills mixed things up, firing HC Sean McDermott. The offense should remain the same, with the WR corps hopefully upgraded with the addition of DJ Moore. Allen is our unquestioned QB1 and the first pick in 2QB/SuperFlex leagues. However, in 1QB leagues, we caution taking him at the end of Round 2 and would prefer to load up on RBs or WRs.
19801.dyn: Allen is the all-time leader in fantasy points per game and career rushing TDs (79) for a QB… and we are only entering Year 9 in the NFL. Bask in his greatness and remind your league mates that Allen is him.

19802.blurb: Ridley broke his fibula in Week 11 last year and is still working back. On a Titans offense still trying to find their identity, Ridley likely will not have a large part.
19802.dyn: At age 31, on a restructured deal, and injuries at the forefront, it is time to move on from him in dynasty.

19803.blurb: With Isaiah Likely signing with the New York Giants, all of a sudden, Mark Andrews has life again. The TE19 finish of last season was far from extraordinary, especially as he bottomed out over the final month of the season. Expected TD regression came as well, dropping from 11 to five. Woof. The Ravens didn’t add any huge names TE-wise in the draft - apologies, Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas - so the runway exists for Andrews to have a bounce-back season, especially if he can keep up with his red zone target share. He was close to 30% last season.
19803.dyn: The Ravens pulled the wool over our eyes last season, teasing the departure of Andrews and opening up the path for Likely’s usage. Snip, snap! Gotcha! It was Likely who was gone from the roster and Andrews who signed a three-year, $39 million extension in December 2025. Andrews looks to still have value on your dynasty squad, whether for a “win now” team, or as trade value if you are rebuilding.

19812.blurb: Oh, the tales we get to tell our grandchildren about Sam Darnold resurrecting from the fantasy grave! The Super Bowl Champion has 60(!) passing TDs over the last two seasons (tied for fifth most in the NFL) with the second-best yards per pass attempt (8.2) in that span. His passing volume declined down the stretch as Seattle came up with a winning formula, leaning on the run and a play-action-based offense that hyper-targeted Jaxon Smith-Njigba. We are happy for the man Darnold, but he still belongs only in the streaming fantasy category despite his success.
19812.dyn: Hindsight is always 20/20, but hat tip to this front office and coaching staff for that Geno deal (sorry, Raider fans). Sam Darnold signed a three-year deal with $55 (!!) million guaranteed last offseason, so we know he is the dude for the foreseeable future after finally getting the monkey off his back and taking his team to the Super Bowl. For fantasy, Darnold profiles as more of a dynasty QB2 as he only averaged about 14 fantasy PPG, but this recent success solidifies him as a locked-in start

19815.blurb: A journeyman of sorts, Kirk lands with his fourth team, entering his ninth season in the league. He has given us two usable fantasy seasons before, and TBH, what’s not to say he becomes the WR1 in San Francisco in a matter of weeks due to their injury luck? Just kidding. Or am I…Just be ready to head to your waiver wire if this happens, but otherwise, he shouldn’t be on your redraft radar, especially considering he's beginning the season on IR because of a calf injury.
19815.dyn: The man is almost 30 and on a one-year deal in San Francisco. If you are lucky, he might have a good matchup on a week you need a bye week fill-in.

19844.blurb: It is not difficult to get excited about one of Josh Allen’s top weapons. We do see a world where Moore has a nice season in Buffalo if he can command WR1 usage. That said, in 2024, Allen became the first top-5 fantasy QB without a top-36 scoring WR or top-12 TE. In 2025, he did it again. Joe Brady’s offense can function without hyper-targeting a single WR. Moore’s efficiency marks dropped off in 2025 (just 1.33 YPRR), so we are not exactly sure if he is the same guy he was a few years back. Perhaps a change of scenery will serve him well, but there is a wide range of outcomes here.
19844.dyn: Moore has been on the Hitman’s Dynasty Trade Away list all off-season. Will he be productive for Josh Allen and the Bills this year? Yes. However, the time to capitalize in the trade market is right now, before the bottom falls out. Moore is already 29 years old, and generally speaking, this is right about the age where veteran players start to decline. If you can sell on the hype of Josh Allen’s WR1, we are doing that now as we see Moore’s value taking a big hit in 2027 and beyond.

tags.bust: Is there a world where Josh Allen unlocks DJ Moore for one more elite fantasy season? Of course, it’s certainly possible, but this Bills offense has been great without having one WR make a difference for fantasy, as they generally spread things out in the pass game and feed James Cook in the red zone. Perhaps that changes with the trade of Moore, but there are also some warning signs on Moore as a player at this stage of his career. Historically speaking, 29-year-old WRs changing teams have not been a great bet in fantasy, and Moore is coming off career lows in receptions, receiving yards, yards per route run, and missed tackles forced. The allure of Josh Allen’s WR1 probably keeps his ADP at a range where we’re fine passing in drafts this year.

19853.blurb: Remember those magical “Sticky Gesicki” weeks a few seasons back? Never forget. Gesicki’s great weeks in 2024 primarily made their appearances when Tee Higgins was out of the lineup, and then in 2025, things got even more confusing with QB Joe Burrow missing nine weeks. Gesicki only had a 9.4% target share last season and will always be left battling on that front with talents like Ja’Marr Chase and Higgins on the field. If he is on your roster, you are only entertaining starting him if one of those WRs is out, and for a guy who only had two receiving TDs in 2025, you don’t need that nonsense.
19853.dyn: There is so much that has to go a certain way for Gesicki to be relevant in dynasty. Sure, he might be the guy to start on the third Sunday of October when the moon is in its waning phase, and the wind is blowing at exactly 2.2 mph, but c’mon, who has the time for that? The team has more youth on their side with Erick All Jr. (25) and rookie Jack Endries (22), making it even easier to leave Gesicki on your bench.

19863.blurb: The TE3(!) in 2025 returns to Philly with the talented rookie Eli Stowers breathing down his neck. After a league-leading 11 TDs last season - the same as Trey McBride, on half as many receiving yards (591) - we can expect some TD regression. It will be tough to start him every week in redraft, especially with all of the offensive options in Philly.
19863.dyn: Goedert signed a one-year extension in the off-season, and with the addition of Stowers, we can see a world where the team moves on after 2026. We can hope for a landing spot where he is featured near the goal line so we can squeak out another year or two in dynasty. He should go off draft boards in the early 20-something range in start-ups.

19867.blurb: Gallup took a year off to experience life as a retired 28-year-old and realized, “Hey, I can still play!” He lands with the up-and-coming Commanders' offense as a rotational deep threat that possibly could get axed when the roster cuts commence.
19867.dyn: If you are scouring your league’s dynasty waiver wire in hopes of mining out Michael Gallup’s dynasty value, stop it! You have a problem, and it is called fantasy football. No shame there. Just thought we would point it out.

19920.blurb: “Dr. Schultz” definitely took some sabbatical weeks in 2025 - clocking eight weeks where he finished as the TE20 or worse. Ick. But then he also had some weeks where he was the dude, slicing and dicing in the operating room, finishing as the TE11 or better seven times. It was tough to anticipate what version of Schultz we were going to get in 2025, making starting him every week a scary decision. A lot will ride on whether Stroud can return to that magical rookie season production. He has had at least 85 targets in the past six seasons, but TDs have never seemed to be his thing. Schultz is a low-ceiling, later-round option in redraft this season.
19920.dyn: The man signed a one-year extension in March of this year. He will turn 30 this year and will just be a boring, vanilla TE2 sitting on your dynasty roster, reminding you once in a while that he can find the end zone.

20753.blurb: Noah Fant’s fantasy trajectory has pointed solidly down for years. As a Bengal in 2025, he finished with only 34 receptions and 288 yards in a full rotation. He signed a two-year deal with New Orleans in the off-season, landing behind incumbent starter Juwan Johnson. The team also drafted third-rounder Oscar Delp, making Fant no more than a backup.
20753.dyn: Fant was not signed to replace anyone in New Orleans, and his deal was nothing special. The team looks like they are thinking Delp could be their TE of the future. It is a wild fall for a player once taken 20th overall in the NFL Draft in 2019 out of Iowa, aka TE University.

20802.blurb: Hill averaged 5.2 yards per carry in limited work before suffering a neck injury in Week 12 and not returning to the field in 2025. He continues to be a “better in real life football” back as a valuable third-down pass protector. This is a new regime in Baltimore, so Hill’s playing time in 2026 could certainly dip. He does not sniff FLEX-worthy territory even in full PPR leagues.
20802.dyn: Hill is a fringe dynasty bench asset with incoming competition behind Derrick Henry from rookie Adam Randall. The 28-year-old is in his final year under contract.

20805.blurb: After three TE4 or better finishes in three out of four years, Hockenson fell and fell hard. He saw 66 mostly forgettable targets in 2025. He was unstartable almost every week until he tapped out for the final two weeks of the season due to a shoulder injury. The Vikings’ offense will look different this season with either Kyler or “Nine” under center, and with Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison still there, it is hard to consider him in redraft this season, at least until you see how the usage pans out.
20805.dyn: Hockenson used to be a fantastic dynasty asset as recently as a couple of years back, but oh, how quickly the tides turn! He is almost 29, and even though there is no one threatening him in the depth chart, he seems to have lost his shine. If Kyler can bring him back to his former glory, consider yourself lucky.

20824.blurb: It looked like Jacobs was going to repeat as a certifiable RB1 for fantasy, averaging 22 opportunities and 1.2 rushing TDs per game through the first ten weeks of the season. He hit a major wall down the stretch, dealing with a knee injury and averaging just 10.5 fantasy points from Week 13 on. We know what he is: a TD monster with a league-leading 24 rushing TDs inside the 10-yard line over the last two seasons. If he is on the field, the workload should be there.... but now he's got a serious legal situation. Jacobs was formally charged with two misdemeanors related to his May arrest and was recently placed on the commissioner's exemption list. He Is now a risky pick in drafts given the of
20824.dyn: While his contract says he has two more years left in Lambeau, there is language that would allow the Packers to get out after this year if he falters. It is also possible the team wants to cut ties after 2026 because of the legal problems. Either way, at age 28, he fits the bill as someone moving along the age curve, and it is better to get out before his dynasty lifecycle is over.

20837.blurb: Johnson will always mean more to the Buffalo Bills than your fantasy teams. He ranked fifth among all RBs in the NFL in routes run on third down and did see an annoyingly high 23 opportunities inside the red zone. His biggest contribution to fantasy will be watching the TV and screaming that your RB target went to “Johnson” instead of “Cook”. Even in the deepest of PPR leagues, Ty is just a guy.
20837.dyn: The Bills must love this guy, as they continually deploy in their game plans to poke fun at fantasy managers. Johnson is under contract for one more year and figures to see a quarter of the RB snaps.

20841.blurb: For the first eight weeks of the season, Jones was the QB6, averaging 20.5 fantasy points per game and a scintillating 71% completion percentage. The Colts were 8-2 heading into their Week 11 bye, and then the world came crashing down with a brutal season-ending Achilles tear. Our injury timeline suggests he will be limited throughout the off-season and could be compromised early in the 2026 season, especially as a runner.
20841.dyn: The Colts brought back the 30-year-old Jones on a two-year deal worth up to $100 million. The front office and coaching staff are essentially betting their jobs on Jones returning to form. We would make the opposite bet for fantasy, willing to sell last season’s high if someone in your league thinks they are finding a solution at QB for SuperFlex leagues.

20850.blurb: It is super cool being tied to Josh Allen and a high-flying offense, but neither is enough to push Knox into the draftable range in redraft. It has been a good long while since his TE8 season of 2021. Never forget.
20850.dyn: You can’t drop that guy because you know what happens if one or two guys go down to injury ahead of him. Find him a cozy corner on your bench, knowing Knox is under contract for two more years in Buffalo as Josh Allen’s best bud.

20873.blurb: After being one of the most valuable WRs in fantasy in 2024, Scary Terry’s 2025 was a year to forget. Not only did McLaurin deal with injury throughout the season, but the Commanders also lost Jayden Daniels for a significant chunk of the year. To no one’s surprise, the Commanders’ offense was stuck in the mud in what was essentially a lost season. Now, looking forward to 2026, McLaurin has a chance to bounce back in a big way. The depth chart here behind McLaurin is barren, so it wouldn’t be surprising at all to see Terry push for a healthy target share and 8-10 TDs if things break right.
20873.dyn: McLaurin got a new deal from Washington last year, but he is entering the stage of his career where you should expect some gradual decline over the next couple of seasons. He will be 31 later this year, so if you are not a contender, it is time to shop him to the rest of your league. If you are a top team in your league, we are fine riding it out and taking the production in 2026.

tags.value: After five wins and a lost season for the Commanders, McLaurin’s ADP is being punished in 2026 despite the fact that we saw only three total games where he played with Jayden Daniels. Remember how electric that combo was the previous year, and now see that you are receiving a whole round discount from what you paid last year. Our UDK stats have Terry as the clear target lead for a Washington team that sportsbooks project to have the sixth-highest average game total (48.1) in the NFL. Expect a ton of shootouts and expect Terry to recoup his cost as a draft-day value.

20875.blurb: Pittsburgh traded for Metcalf, then signed him to a huge deal…only to target him 99 times. What? Why? Needless to say, it was a very frustrating 2025 for Metcalf managers last season in that Arthur Smith/Aaron Rodgers offense. On one hand, Mike McCarthy’s offense should be much more throw-heavy in 2026, but on the other hand, Metcalf is now competing with Michael Pittman for targets and still has Aaron Rodgers or an inexperienced youngster as his QB. Could Metcalf rebound and regain WR2 form? It is possible, but we do not see league-winning upside with Metcalf in this offense.
20875.dyn: Metcalf burned bright for a few years there in Seattle, but things have trended downwards in recent seasons. Now 28 years old, Metcalf still has some good years left in the NFL, but expecting him to return to what we saw early in his career is pretty unlikely. He is a solid piece to have if you are a contender, but if you have your eyes on the 2027 season, we like moving Metcalf now before the bottom falls out.

20876.blurb: Meyers’ 2025 was a tale of two seasons. In Las Vegas, it was forgettable to say the least. He posted just one week inside the top-36 from Weeks 1-9. However, after the trade to Jacksonville, Meyers averaged about seven targets and 9.6 fantasy points per game. It is worth noting that most of that production came after Travis Hunter went down for the year, so we cannot really copy and paste his production for 2026 if Hunter happens to play more receiver than corner. Even still, the financial commitment from the team suggests Jakobi will have a real role here. He doesn’t scream “upside,” but if you are in a league that starts three WRs, Meyers can fill in as your third option as a higher- floor
20876.dyn: Meyers is the perfect depth piece to have if you are looking to make a run at a title in your dynasty league. He will never win you your league, but he should have the opportunity to post WR3/FLEX-type numbers for the next couple of years after the Jags signed him to a three-year, $60 million extension.

20882.blurb: The Texans must have a type: past-their-prime early down runners who can be effective scoring TDs in bunches. Montgomery's value received a major boost when he was traded from Detroit to Houston as the team was desperately searching for an answer inside the red zone. The team converted a league-worst 17% of their attempts inside the 5-yard line into TDs, with the league-average being 39%. Monty should see 18+ touches a game and return low-end RB2 value for a team that wants to win by running the ball and leaning on their defense.
20882.dyn: Monty has two more years left under contract until his age-30 season. While that might be too far to consider in dynasty, he remains an undervalued asset for win-now teams. He is a hold for now, knowing his value could rise for RB-needy teams as you draw closer to your league’s trade deadline.

20889.blurb: The Kyler Murray era in Arizona officially came to a close with the Cardinals releasing the former No. 1 overall pick in early March. Still just 28 years old, Kyler will look to get his career back on track in Minnesota, perhaps following the path of guys like Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold. Expect the team to frame this as a QB competition throughout the summer, but if you watched JJ "Nine" McCarthy play NFL football in 2025, you likely know where this is headed in terms of the Week 1 starter. We are still keeping the light on for Kyler to return to being a top-10 fantasy QB.
20889.dyn: This move makes all the sense in the world for Kyler and Kevin O'Connell's team. They are short on cash this year in terms of cap space, and with Arizona picking up the vast majority of his salary this year, they were able to sign him for the vet minimum. Kyler is looking to parlay a year of starting in Minnesota into another long-term starting gig, ala Sam Darnold. He is a high upside swing in SuperFlex if you think his rushing upside and change of scenery can restore him to QB1 status.

20912.blurb: Pollard might have been the most boring fantasy selection at RB in 2025. The first 13 weeks were utter garbage as he averaged 15+ touches per game while turning that volume into a measly 7.9 fantasy points per game. Woof. He did save the best for last, turning it on in the final month of the fantasy season with four top-20 finishes in a row while averaging 113 rushing yards per game. The 29-year-old is hitting the crashing point in the lifecycle of an NFL RB and enters the final year of his Titans contract as the lead back on an offense that hopefully takes a step forward under new OC Brian Daboll. If dirty, dirty RB volume is your thing, Pollard can be a FLEX for your team for one last ride
20912.dyn: We are a long way from the high-impact, efficiency monster he was behind Zeke in Dallas. He enters the final season of his free agent deal, sputtering to the finish line. The Titans are favored in just one of their first six games, so pray Pollard falls into the end zone.

20932.blurb: He's back! After one season in Washington, Deebo returns to the Bay to reunite with Kyle Shanahan, George Kittle, CMC, and Brock Purdy. Ricky Pearsall is battling a recurring knee injury, and veteran Christian Kirk is on the roster bubble (while also dealing with a calf injury), so the signing of Deebo makes perfect sense for a team that is trying to compete for a division title. We expect Mike Evans and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling to work on the outside with Deebo doing his thing over the middle of the field. Now 30 years old, Samuel's best football is probably behind him, but he is still a solid chain mover on a great offense, which could have WR3/FLEX viability in the right matchups.
20932.dyn: Samuel's dynasty value is all but gone at this stage of his career. He is now on the wrong side of 30, and he's only under contract for one year with the Niners. His peripheral metrics are not what they were a couple of years ago, suggesting he is already on the decline. If you are a contender and want to hold for depth, that is viable, but if not, this is probably the last call to get anything for him via trade before the bottom really falls out.

20941.blurb: Entering the final year of his free agent deal with the Giants, “Singlecarry” was surpassed on the depth chart by both Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy while seeing career lows in receptions and yards per carry. It’s not the way you want things to trend entering your age-29 season. Consider this man D-O-N-E.
20941.dyn: “Dingleberry” was a Daboll guy, so it wouldn't be surprising to see him completely phased out of the offense with Skatt and Tracy dominating touches. He is a fringe bench name who likely will be on dynasty waiver wires heading into 2027.

20943.blurb: If you would have told us Darius Slayton was still a Giant after all these years, we would have called you a liar. The team seemed to want to move on for years, and then finally paid him only to draft Malachi Fields and sign Darnell Mooney who do the exact same thing he does - stretch the field. If this were a Facebook relationship, we would give it the “It’s complicated” label. Expect Slayton to be on the field early in the year as Malik Nabers is eased in off his ACL surgery.
20943.dyn: Slayton is kind of the worst type of player for dynasty leagues. He is just good enough that you can talk yourself into rostering him, yet you are not actually going to start him on a consistent basis. If you look up “Roster clogger” in the dictionary, you will see Mr. Slayton’s picture.

21042.blurb: You heard about it for months and it finally happened... A.J. Brown is now a Patriot.  As for the player himself, last year probably felt frustrating as Philly’s offense sputtered and he finished with career lows in yards per reception (12.9). Even in a “down” year, Brown still finished as fantasy’s WR10 and an efficient 2+ yards per route run for his 7th consecutive season. He remains one of the league's best in man coverage as an absolute bully in one-on-one situations. Perhaps a change of scenery with Drake Maye could unlock Brown for another WR1 finish in 2026.
21042.dyn: We have had Brown as a trade-away candidate in the Dynasty Pass. It is not because we think he will have a bad season in 2026, but rather, we would prefer to maximize value after his NFL trade in the dynasty trade market a year early. You can likely still get a young WR plus a first-round rookie pick if you are willing to move off the soon-to-be 29-year-old vet.

21045.blurb: HOLLYWOOOOOOD is still fun to say on the podcast, but honestly, do you have any memory of what Brown did in the 2025 season? Apart from a Week 1 surprise when he saw 16 targets with Rashee Rice out, it was mostly forgettable despite leading all Chiefs WRs in receiving yards (587). Your league mates might be surprised to learn he is on the Eagles' roster in 2026. Apart from having a player named HOLLYWOOD on your roster, it will be impossible to ever start this guy.
21045.dyn: Hollywood’s dynasty value evaporated over the last two years. The former first-round pick signed a one-year deal worth up to $6.5 million. He feels like “fancy Tutu Atwell."

21142.blurb: The wee little man signed a two-year deal with the Falcons in free agency, and if you have been following the NFL long enough, that probably sounds familiar. He actually began his career with Atlanta as a UDFA back in 2019, so we have a bit of a reunion situation going on here. Quite honestly, there is a chance he sees some playing time given the state of the depth chart behind Drake London. That said, we don’t anticipate him being fantasy relevant as he has been in the league for seven years and has never averaged more than 5.5 fantasy PPG.
21142.dyn: The fact that this man has survived in the NFL for 7+ years as a former UDFA should be celebrated. The “How is he still in the league?” Footie will be in the mail shortly…

21674.blurb: Poor J.K… can this guy catch a break? Through the first ten weeks of the season, he was the RB18, averaging 16.7 opportunities per game ahead of the more hyped RJ Harvey. An unfortunate “hip-drop” tackle ended his season yet again, as he now has appeared in just 38% of possible games over the last five years. He signed a two-year deal worth up to $20 million to run it back with the Broncos. While we still expect Harvey to see high-value looks in the pass game, Dobbins should have FLEX-worthy weeks in the right matchup while running behind one of the best offensive lines in football.
21674.dyn: Dobbins keeps picking up “extra lives,” proving these last two years that he can still contribute as a fantasy RB2 in a timeshare. He is a hold in dynasty, knowing the sun will be setting soon for a player plagued with injuries.

tags.value: It feels like we are in "de ja vu" again as the Broncos backfield remains an ADP mystery like it was in 2025. Dobbins was re-signed to a 2-year extension this off-season and yet here we are again with question marks surrounding his stranglehold on the backfield. RJ Harvey will certainly mix in on passing downs but Dobbins projects as the lead ball carrier behind the NFL's best offensive line. The fact you can get a starting RB for a team coming off a 14-win season this late in your drafts screams value!

21677.blurb: Tua’s time in Miami came to a crashing end as he was cut for an NFL-record $99.2 million in dead cap money. The Falcons, scooping up every known left-handed QB in the universe, signed him for the veteran minimum ($1 million) to pair with Michael Penix Jr., who is returning from a season-ending ACL injury. Tua’s yards per attempt declined in three straight seasons (8.9 > 8.3 > 7.2 > 6.9), signaling that the former fifth overall pick’s best days are likely behind him. Nevertheless, he could begin the season as Atlanta’s starter, but is irrelevant to the fantasy conversation.
21677.dyn: After signing a four-year $212 million deal in July of 2024, Tua went 12-13 and finished as a top-12 QB in just a quarter of those starts. The 28-year-old is a QB3 at best in SuperFlex but likely will be supplanted by Penix at some point in 2026.

21679.blurb: Lamb had a good season in 2025, but it didn’t feel great considering you likely had to take him in the first round last year. He missed a few games because of the high ankle sprain, and he only scored three TDs. In the game we play, that is just not going to get it done. However, he is coming off a career high 14.4 yards per reception and has now finished with 1,000+ yards in five straight seasons. If that TD variance swings back in his direction, CeeDee can absolutely finish as a top-5 WR in 2026.
21679.dyn: Lamb remains one of the most valuable WRs in all of dynasty, but it is at least worth considering that he is 27 years old. He will remain ultra-productive for the next couple of years, so if you have him, keep taking that top-tier production. Just have it on your radar for the next two years that the trade window might close more quickly than you think. We aren’t saying he will fall off any time soon, but we generally prefer to be a year early in order to maximize returns in the trade market.

21681.blurb: It is a miracle Big Herbs is still alive. After losing both starting All-Pro tackles, he took a career-high number of hits and was sacked 54 times, easily the most of his career. Even with all that, he managed to bank a QB9 finish, thanks mostly to career highs in rush attempts (83) and rushing yards (498). If that part of his game can stick around and his line can stay healthy, the weapons are there for Herbert to have one of the best seasons of his career in 2026. Mike McDaniel is one of the most creative play-callers in the league, so we are bullish on Herbert if you can get him late in your drafts.
21681.dyn: Herbert became the first QB since 2018 (Deshaun Watson) to lead the league in % of drop backs pressured (43%) and make the NFL playoffs. That type of NFL life isn’t sustainable for the 28-year-old QB, but we expect 2026 to be much better. Big Herbs is a top-10 dynasty QB in our book.

21682.blurb: Oh man, those first 10 weeks of JTT were legendary! His five 30+ fantasy point games were tied with 2000 Marshall Faulk and 2006 LaDanian Tomlinson for the most ever through the first ten weeks of a season. As a receiver, he was more involved than ever, setting career highs in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Unfortunately, the Colts’ offense tanked down the stretch with Philip Rivers & Riley Leonard under center. Taylor’s production essentially was cut in half, nosediving from 23.3 fantasy points per game with Daniel Jones to 11.8 over those final five games. JTT is still a locked-in RB1 for us, although the first month of the season is a brutal stretch for the Colts.
21682.dyn: Taylor signed a 3-year extension in early August, and he is one of four RBs since 2000 to average 90+ rushing yards per game through his first six seasons! Despite being 27 years old, he remains an elite RB1 for dynasty and a building block for contending dynasty teams.

21684.blurb: Over the last six years, only two RBs finished inside the top 24 at the position every year: Derrick Henry and D'Andre Swift. Yep, it isn’t always the sexiest outcomes, but Swift is the clear lead back for a Chicago offense we want pieces of in fantasy. He set career highs in rushing yards, rushing TDs, and rush success rate behind a much- improved Bears offensive line. Over the back half of the season, he did cede work to Kyle Monangai, but we still view Swift as the lead guy in a 60-40 backfield. Does he make it seven years in a row as an RB2? Our projections certainly think so.
21684.dyn: The 27-year-old has one more year under contract, but dynasty managers could look to flip him to RB-needy teams if they are looking to profit.

tags.value: Daaaaa Bears! Year 1 of the Ben Johnson era was a smashing success with Chicago ranking ninth in both points per game and yards per play en route to their first double-digit win season since 2018! D'Andre Swift is coming off a 2025 campaign in which he set career highs in rushing yards (1,087) and rushing TDs (9) behind one of the better offensive lines in football, and the Bears didn't add any competition to the backfield. Kyle Monangai will see some work, but Swift should lead the backfield yet again for a team that should win plenty of games and put up plenty of points. He's finished as a top-24 fantasy RB in six straight seasons, making him a rock solid pick as your RB2 in fantasy drafts.

21685.blurb: JJetts disappointed fantasy managers who grabbed him early in drafts last season, but was it really his fault? I mean, I think we all know who to blame here…“Nine” was one of the worst starting QBs in football, and you may forget, but Carson Wentz (yes, that guy) started five games while Max Brosmer attempted to play football in the NFL. Spoiler: It did not go well. Basically, we are completely ignoring Jefferson’s 2025 season. He is still one of the best in the game, and while Kyler is not a top-five QB, he is certainly an upgrade on whatever the heck the Vikings were doing in 2025. He is one of fantasy’s most obvious bounce-back players for 2026 and is well worth a look in Round 1 of draft
21685.dyn: Jefferson is still one of the most valuable WRs in dynasty formats despite his down 2025 campaign, and we are confidently taking him in the first round of startup drafts.

21687.blurb: Smitty has always been a great talent at the WR position, but his fantasy value has been held in check with AJ Brown on the roster. With Brown gone, expect "Slim Reaper" to be one of the hottest names in fantasy. Smith will have a chance to set career highs in targets, receptions, and yards as the Eagles’ new WR1. His ADP will probably skyrocket, but the excitement is warranted for a guy who’s averaged 14.5 PPR points per game without Brown in the lineup going back to 2022.
21687.dyn: Smith has always had the talent to produce like a WR1, but he has been pigeon-holed as the second option in Philly ever since the Eagles traded for AJ Brown. That should change in a big way in 2026. Expect Smith’s dynasty value to skyrocket, but just be aware that he is already turning 28 years old later this year. He is still in his prime for now, but the window is probably closing faster than you might realize.

21690.blurb: Blurb- “Meat Higgins,” as he is known around Fantasy Footballers HQ, has now finished as a top-24 fantasy WR in four of the last five years as the Robin to Ja’Marr Chase’s Batman. As long as Joe Burrow stays healthy, we expect both guys to eat this year, with Higgins the more volatile option of the two Cincy WRs. We are fine with Higgins as a pick where he goes as a WR2 for your squad, but he has always got that sneaky WR1 upside if Chase happens to miss time.
21690.dyn: Higgins still has three more years left on the contract extension that he signed before the 2025 season, and he is still just 27 years old. He likely has at least two to three more great seasons in him before we talk about a potential decline. Keep riding this thing out, especially if you are a contender.

21691.blurb: The 27-year-old Chuba finds himself as the presumed lead back in Carolina a year after taking a backseat to Rico Dowdle. The efficiency numbers weren’t pretty, averaging a paltry 3.8 yards per carry with only 6% of his runs gaining 10+ yards, the fourth lowest rate among qualifying RBs. Hubbard will face some competition from former second-round pick Jonathon Brooks, and now he's dealing with a hamstring injury in training camp. Initially, our projections had Hubbard seeing the lion's share of the work for the Panthers, but that projection could change if Brooks keeps showing out in camp.
21691.dyn: Chuba is a hold right now for RB-needy teams. Keep in mind, he failed to have a single run of 15+ yards on the season, so this is purely a volume-based play. He enters his age-27 season as the presumed lead back and is under contract for three more seasons. However, perhaps Jonathon Brooks begins working more in the rotation.

tags.bust: There were a couple of alarming truths that emerge after we reviewed Chuba's 2025 season. He was usurped by Rico Dowdle, he had one total carry inside the 5-yard line and no runs of 15+ yards on the season. Yikes! Jonathon Brooks' rise over the summer is certainly making us nervous about selecting the 27-year-old as the Panthers' RB1 in our drafts. He could begin the year as the lead in the backfield but there are routes where he ends up in a full timeshare or is surpassed on the depth chart at some point. That is not a profile we want to bet on in the 7th round on a team projected for just 6.5 wins on the season.

21692.blurb: Is Jeudy a capable NFL WR? Sure. Is he frustrating to watch due to the inconsistency? Yep. Is he a fun click in fantasy? Nope! Judge Jeudy had that magical stretch with Jameis Winston in 2024 (#JameisForever), but outside of that small sample, he has largely been irrelevant for fantasy since he arrived in Cleveland. The Browns took multiple rookie WRs in this draft, so his playing time isn’t a guarantee moving forward, especially with a new coaching staff in town.
21692.dyn: Jeudy’s dynasty value was already in free fall before the Browns double-dipped in the NFL Draft with KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Jeudy comes from the previous regime, so Todd Monken may prefer to get a look at the young guns. That leaves Jeudy in no man’s land when it comes to his future outlook. He is under contract through 2027, but it wouldn’t be surprising to see his name in trade rumors.

21693.blurb: Through six seasons as Cincy’s signal-caller, Burrow has three elite fantasy seasons and three injury-plagued disappointments. In 2025, he went down in Week 2 and did not return until Week 13. Those final six weeks were vintage Burrow as he put together a 17-game pace of 4500+ passing yards and 43 passing TDs. It also helps that the Cincy defense has a ton of holes, forcing shootouts and more passing volume Burrow’s way. While we don’t love living and dying with TD rates from pocket passers, Burrow runs just enough to ignore that rule. They throw enough inside the red zone to justify his ADP.
21693.dyn: With Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins locked up for at least the next three years, you have to be cackling to yourself if you are a Burrow manager. He is a weekly threat to finish as QB1, and at only 29 years old, he feels so safe as a top-5 dynasty QB in startups. Now if only the Bengals could help improve his .389 winning percentage in September…

21696.blurb: After Jacksonville’s Week 8 bye, Etienne turned into a fantasy force, averaging 17.5 fantasy points per game as the RB7. He was a wild outlier as a pass-catcher, becoming the third RB over the last 25 years to score 6+ rec TDs on fewer than 40 receptions. The main headline for the man formerly known as Travis Etienne Jr. was the four-year free agent deal he signed to come home to New Orleans and be crowned Travis “Aychane” Jr. With Alvin Kamara phasing out of the team’s plans, Etienne will be given every opportunity to be a workhorse for this Kellen Moore-designed offense. While the Saint’s weekly TD expectation might be low, he should end up a solid RB2 on volume alone.
21696.dyn: The finer details of Etienne’s deal need to be discussed, as his four-year contract sneakily is a “two-year” deal, as he carries a $0 dead cap hit in 2028. In the short term, the 27-year-old should hold RB2 value as the main workhorse for the Saints’ running game. We are not banking on anything of significant value after these first two years of the contract.

21717.blurb: Jauan “Jennayings” (IYKYK) signed with the Vikings late in free agency, inking a one-year deal worth up to $13 million. With Jefferson dominating targets and Jordan Addison one of the better WR2s in the league, we are not super excited about Jennings’ fantasy outlook as Kyler’s WR3. He is likely to help the Vikings more than he helps our fantasy rosters. That said, if JJetts or Addison happen to miss time because of injury, we know Jauan is a serviceable fantasy WR who can be a plug-and-play option off the waiver wire.
21717.dyn: Jennings doesn’t have a long-term contract and is now entering his age-29 season. We expect his dynasty value to continue to take a hit over the next 12 months, so at this point, he is not really anything more than a bench piece for a contender.

21738.blurb: There have been whispers in the bushes every year about a potential Juwan Johnson breakout season, and we finally got it in 2025! His TE10 finish was the best of his career on the back of 529 routes run, the fifth most for the position. It was the rapport with QB Tyler Shough that really greased the gears, and they should be ready to come out firing to start the season. The team added offensive weapons with eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson, Travis Etienne Jr., and TEs Oscar Delp and Noah Fant, which likely eats into his target volume. Going off draft boards past TE15 territory means you can shoot your shot with the former basketballer if you had a fun ride last year.
21738.dyn: We do not usually suggest targeting almost 30-year-old TEs with a classic sixth-year breakout. The team restructured Johnson’s contract this spring, giving themselves an out after 2027. Add in the drafting of Georgia’s Oscar Delp, and it suggests that the team is preparing for a world without Juwan-son as a Saint. If you can capitalize on a strong 2025 and trade him to a TE-needy team, we don’t think it is a bad decision. If no takers, you are holding and hoping.

21739.blurb: “Have you seen this WR depth chart behind Terry McLaurin? Someone could see a big opportunity here!” you explain to your friend. Listen up, bud: Van Jeff will be entering his seventh season in the NFL as a certifiable “Cardio King”. He runs the routes, he knows the plays, and yet his 10% career target share reminds you he should not be allowed on a fantasy roster. He has not scored ten fantasy points in a game since 2022!
21739.dyn: Remember when Sean McVay took this guy in the second round of the NFL Draft? On his fourth team in four years, you likely will not gain fantasy points for “being in the right place” and “being a glue guy in the locker room”. Ok, if you want bonus points for reading this VAN JEFFERSON(!) dynasty blurb, text someone you love, let them know how you truly feel, and finally throw in the fact his birth name is Vanchii Lashawn Jefferson Jr.

21744.blurb: Michael Pittman in Pittsburgh? We did it! Pitty City…but for real. Indy’s possession receiver over the last handful of years, Pittman should operate in a similar role in Pittsburgh and offers a nice compliment to the more explosive DK Metcalf. Given the state of the QB room (an inexperienced younger guy or an aging Aaron Rodgers), we are skeptical of the ceiling here, but Pittman projects as a high-floor WR3/FLEX option for 2026 given his target-earning ability.
21744.dyn: Pittman has been a solid WR for years in the NFL, but in dynasty circles, his name no longer carries a ton of value as he is set to enter his age-29 season. Despite Pittsburgh signing him to a brand new contract this offseason, we are not thrilled with this team’s outlook in the short or long term, given the lack of stability at the QB position. He is a nice depth piece if you are a contender, but you are not winning your dynasty league because of Pitty City.

21756.blurb: Even with C.J. Stroud disappointing more often than not from a real-life NFL perspective, Collins continues to post WR1 numbers on a per-game basis. He is just that dude in this offense, and with Tank Dell recovering from a major injury and last year’s rookies, Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel, unproven commodities, Collins’ elite target share remains locked in. He is on the short list of players who are capable of finishing as a top-five fantasy WR in 2026.
21756.dyn: Nico is now 27 years old, so he has a couple more seasons in his prime. If you are a contender, you are obviously riding this out and taking the production, but if you are a rebuilding team, we do not mind putting him on the trade block and getting a haul. Our philosophy in dynasty is that we would generally prefer to be a year early rather than a year late.

21768.blurb: The veteran back signed with the Giants as a late camp addition but seems to be gaining the trust of the coaching staff. He is way past the good ole days when he was a workhorse for fantasy but it should not be shocking if he eats into Cam Skattebo's workload. Consider Najee either a stash in deeper leagues or a waiver name to monitor over the first few weeks.
21768.dyn: The former first round NFL Draft pick is still only 28 years old. Whoop-de-doo! Dynasty fantasy football is a cruel game. In the "what have you done for me lately” world we live in, Najee is just a backup… a free fall from a guy who was the 1.01(!) in rookie drafts back in 2021.

21772.blurb: The offensive weapons in Chicago are plenty, and Kmet tried desperately to contribute in 2025. Unfortunately, the 347 receiving yards on 48 targets - although helpful for the NFL team - were not helpful for our fantasy squads. We all know that Colston Loveland is the present and future for this franchise, so any hope of using Kmet in redraft is out the window, barring an injury. And don’t you dare put that into the universe!
21772.dyn: There was dynasty chatter about Kmet heading into the 2024 season, coming off the heels of back-to-back TE7 finishes. We know those days are over. With Mr. Loveland at the TE helm, Chicago added rookie Sam Roush in the third round so we could see Kmet heading to a new home soon. You can hold on to him to see if he lands on a team that can reignite his offensive spark. He is only 27.

21785.blurb: As much as we like to admit that Travis Kelce will never retire, the man is cake tasting and choosing floral arrangements. The end is near, but is Gray the next man up? Mahomes has never trusted Gray enough to give him more than one season of 49 targets. He will pop up for a TD here and there, but even in the deepest of TE premium leagues, he is not roster-worthy.
21785.dyn: The team liked Gray enough to give him a three-year extension in 2024, but not enough to give him more than three red zone targets in all of 2025. You can hold him due to the fact that he is a backup on a team that is always a bet to make it to the Super Bowl, but know that you are expecting close to nothing from the man.

21802.blurb: The artist formerly known as “AJ Villain” is in Year 6 of the feature film production known as “Quadzilla”. While there was a ton of hype early on for this movie, the reviews are in: Dillon is better suited for the “hired muscle” role than as a featured final boss. He technically is on the Carolina roster, but could easily be cut come August with just $100,000 guaranteed in his contract.
21802.dyn: Ah, so you’ve come here for AJ Dillon dynasty wisdom. How is this guy still in the NFL? This is AJ Dillon’s profile for fantasy football. Nothing could be more serious than this man’s contribution to fantasy rosters in 2026… except for the fact that there is a real chance he doesn’t make the final 53-man roster.

21807.blurb: After five seasons of “who’s that guy” in Los Angeles, 2025 turned into “hey, I know that guy” for Colby Parkinson. He set career highs in targets (56), yards (408), and TDs (8!!). The TDs are certainly an outlier, but he was a certifiable red zone weapon, seeing 22 red zone targets inside the 20, just three shy of Puka Nacua. We are paying attention, Mr. Parkinson. The only problem is  Sean McVay loves TEs, and with a crowded room, you won’t know what weeks to start Parkinson or any of the other Rams TEs.
21807.dyn: Good ole Colby is 27 and in the last year of his deal. The Rams have made it known they have their eyes on the future, drafting Terrance Ferguson last year and Max Klare in 2026. You can hold onto him to see if he heads to a team that features him more, and if he doesn’t, there are worse offenses to be tied to.

21831.blurb: Are fantasy managers experiencing name fatigue? Hurts is coming off a season with the worst consistency metrics of his career, including averaging just 16.3 fantasy points per game from Week 9 on.
