We saw his fewest TDs inside the 5-yard line and now with AJ Brown leaving and yet another OC change, perhaps fantasy managers are scared off. While Hurts isn't a slouch as a passer, we love him in fantasy for his ability to use his legs. The overall Philly offense should return to form, making Hurts a relative value compared to where he was being drafted in the past.
21831.dyn: We are not trying to bury the recent Super Bowl MVP, but if someone in your league still views him as a locked-in top-5 QB, we are willing to listen to offers. We still view Hurts as a top-10 dynasty QB, but it is fair to wonder where this thing goes over the next 2-3 years if the Tush Push gets banned.

21841.blurb: Love's 23 passing TDs and 3300+ yards might not stand out, but efficiency has always been the name of his game. He ranked sixth in Passer Rating, seventh in completion percentage over expectation, and tied Patrick Mahomes for 12th in fantasy points per dropback.  He remains one of the more polarizing starters in the league, as we have seen some really high-end play at times, yet he hasn't put it all together for a full season. For fantasy purposes, we are viewing Love as a streamer to start the season as Green Bay begins the year favored in each of their first six matchups.
21841.dyn: Only 27 years old, Love is the type of QB in dynasty who likely costs 85 cents on the dollar compared to "brand name QBs". Over his last three seasons as a starter, he has a higher TD rate (5.5%) and Passer Rating (97.8) than Josh Allen and TD passes (80) than Patrick Mahomes. He remains a rock-solid QB to have on your dynasty roster, and he has proven he's the guy for LaFleur's team. Love signed a four-year extension recently, so he is under contract through 2028.

21952.blurb: After Chuba Hubbard was hurt in Week 5 last year, Rico essentially stole the RB1 role in Carolina; he was highly productive with his opportunities, mixing in some wild 30+ fantasy point spike weeks. Mr. "Two Pumps" Dowdle rushed for 1,076 yards this past season and ran for a career high six TDs as the leader of the committee in Carolina. Dowdle has been the lead guy for two different teams now, and while he may not be an elite talent, the guy just gets the job done. He lands in Pittsburgh reunited with former coach Mike McCarthy alongside Jaylen Warren. Consider Rico a “FLEX with benefits” to start the year.
21952.dyn: During the last two years in Dallas and Carolina, he showed he can be reliable with 200+ touches in each season. His two-year deal includes just $5 million guaranteed, and his cap hit in 2027 jumps to $8.5 million. Consider this a one-year experiment, hoping he can regain the magic he had with McCarthy in Dallas.

tags.sleeper: The Steelers are once again one of fantasy football’s ambiguous RB rooms entering 2026. After Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell both ended up being great values in drafts a year ago, we are interested in taking shots on the Steelers’ backs as long as ADPs are held in check. Warren was good last year, and it is certainly possible he wins the job, but it’s important to remember that for the first time in forever, we have a new staff in Pittsburgh. Warren comes from the Tomlin regime, while Dowdle was brought in via free agency this offseason. Back in 2024, when Dowdle played for Mike McCarthy in Dallas, he took over the RB1 job and finished as a solid RB2 for fantasy. Last season in Carolina, we saw him steal that job from Chuba Hubbard, and Dowdle has now banked back-to-back seasons with 280+ total opportunities and 4.6 yards per carry. Both Pittsburgh backs are good bets at cost, but we are leaning towards Rico, given his familiarity with McCarthy.

21961.blurb: Mooney was never more than a WR2/3 you could use in great matchups, and now he heads to New York to be pretty much the same thing for the Giants. If Malik Nabers is not ready to go at the start of the season, there is a world where he could stand a chance, target-wise, battling with Darius Slayton and Calvin Austin. Monitor training camp and Nabers, but do not expect the moon and stars.
21961.dyn: It is a one year deal for the almost 29 year old Mooney in New York. Nabers will eventually return, and with it, poof goes Mooney’s value in dynasty.

22490.blurb: 2025 was by far Lawrence’s best fantasy campaign thanks to whatever pep talk the team received during their Week 8 bye. From then on, he was the QB1 for fantasy, averaging 22.6 fantasy points per game. He joined Josh Allen as the only QBs in NFL history with 4,000+ passing yards, 29+ passing TDs, and 9+ rushing TDs in the same season. Credit goes to Liam Coen, who transformed this offense in the second half despite a WR room that dropped 8.6% of TLaw’s pass attempts, tied for the highest rate of any QB over the last four years. Lawrence is not being overdrafted based on last year’s finish, so we are still in for 1QB leagues if he is available near the double-digit rounds.
22490.dyn: It was quite the boom year for Lawrence as his rushing production spiked with his most attempts, yards, and carries inside the 5 of his career. Only 26 years old, expect the rushing TDs to regress, but the Jags look like a legit contender in the AFC. We view Lawrence as a back-end QB1 but would prefer him as a high-end QB2 in SuperFlex leagues.

tags.breakout: After wig-gate of 2026, it is time to fully consider Trevor Lawrence a thing. The fantasy community has gone back and forth during Lawrence’s tenure in the NFL, debating whether or not he was actually good at football, and some people are still not accepting it, even after his QB4 finish last year. He was one of six QBs who threw for over 4,000 yards, and his end-of-season run, fantasy-wise, was one championships were made of. Oh, and may I remind you he also runs? He managed 359 yards with his legs (10th), nine rushing TDs (tied for second most), and 39 rushing first downs (second most). We are big fans of the Jaguars offense and what Liam Coen is doing in Jacksonville, and we see a world where the Horse Child comes out of the gate galloping in 2026.

22507.blurb: Is the Muth still Luth? Unfortunately, the answer might be no with only 486 yards receiving and four TDs in 2025. The team gets back the one and only Aaron Rodgers, who had 67% of his passing yardage come after the catch, the highest rate in the NFL. With Mike Tomlin and Jonnu Smith out and Mike McCarthy and Michael Pittman Jr. in, it is up in the air how this offense will function. Look, it’s ok to just say no in fantasy.
22507.dyn: It is perfectly fine if you want nothing to do with this Pittsburgh offense, but keep in mind that this is probably the last year of Aaron Rodgers (we hope). The Mike McCarthy era has now begun. The Muth signed a four-year extension in 2024, so he will be a Steeler through 2028. He is a hold as we hope for a team makeup that lets the Muth get Luth again, as he did in 2022 and 2024.

22508.blurb: Ah, yes, the TE2 last season! As you may remember, Pitts had an incredible final third of the season with four weeks inside the top-10, including his 40-point(!) Week 15 blowout game against Tampa Bay. We are not expecting this from Pitts heading into 2026, so make sure to let your league mates reach for him come draft day. Rankings-wise, he is living in that TE6-TE10 range where players can become almost interchangeable. Aside from Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons do not have much target competition, so a world exists where he could bolster his consistency and build on his 2025 season. The QB situation and a new offensive play-caller bring more risk and uncertainty than we would
22508.dyn: Pitts signed his franchise tag, which gave the Falcons more time to work on a long-term deal with the player they took fourth overall ahead of JA’MARR CHASE! #NeverForget. The man is somehow only turning 26 this year, and while some dynasty managers were hoping he went to a new team to get a fresh start, Pitts inked a brand new three-year, $54M deal in June to stay in Atlanta. The Falcons don't really have a reliable second option in the pass game behind Drake London, so Pitts will once again ha

22526.blurb: After signing a three-year extension following a tumultuous offseason, it is clear Breece remains the Jets’ main guy in the backfield. The opportunities to score were slim in 2025 as the Jets were tied or trailing on 93% of their offensive snaps, the worst rate in the league. Zoom out a bit further, and you will see that the team ranked dead last in rush attempts inside the 5-yard line for the third year in a row. His volume and breakaway run rate can make up for the team’s shortcomings. With a 45+ reception floor, Hall can be a valuable RB2 and potentially finish as an RB1 if the TDs finally fall in his favor. Early drafters will need to be tracking Hall's health closely over the next coupl
22526.dyn: It feels like Breece has already lived nine lives in the NFL (playing for the Jets will do that), but he is still not even 25 years old. One of the most productive and efficient backs over the last three seasons, the Jets rewarded Breece with a brand new three-year deal worth just over $15 million per year. Some dynasty managers out there may have been hoping for Breece to finally be unleashed on a new team and hopefully a better offense, but this contract says he will get plenty of volume in Ne

22546.blurb: Stevenson finished the season as the RB25, thanks to the final three weeks of the season, where he scored six TDs despite averaging just 11 touches per game. He was quietly a pass-catching fiend throughout the year, leading all RBs in yards per target (9.3) and a thorn in the side of TreVeyon Henderson truthers. This regime seems more confident in Stevenson in pass protection, as we expect this to remain a 50-50 timeshare. He is a FLEX option to start the year on a Patriots team that will have a much tougher schedule in 2026.
22546.dyn: Entering his age-28 season, Stevenson remains a fixture in the New England offense after averaging 21 opportunities per game during the NFL playoffs. He is under contract for three more seasons with cap hits climbing until a cuttable final year in 2028 with a $1.6 million dead cap.

22558.blurb: One of the best fantasy stories of 2025 had to be the resurgence of Javonte Williams as Dallas' RB1. Among qualified RBs, Javonte was fourth in yards after contact per attempt while seeing 19 opportunities per game. For the first four years of his frustrating career, he had eight total TDs inside the 5-yard line; in 2025, he had 10! With no direct competition for touches, Javonte is a solid RB2 as part of a Dallas offense we love buying into for fantasy.
22558.dyn: We did it! The Javonte hive that held strong after years of disappointment had its breakthrough in dynasty.  After a bounce-back season, Dallas rewarded him with a three-year extension that includes $16 million in guaranteed money. His receiving efficiency was puzzling as he totaled a putrid 137 receiving yards on 51 targets, the fewest of any player with 50+ targets over the last 40 years! Expect at least two years of legitimate production.

tags.value: After being one of the steals of the 2025 fantasy season, Javonte’s ADP is quite palatable in 2026. He signed a three-year extension in Dallas, and the backfield competition behind him is nonexistent. Finding a workhorse RB in the fourth round coming off an RB1 season is a rare event. It would not be shocking to see him repeat 300+ opportunities and double-digit TDs.

22562.blurb: It pays to be in Aaron Rodgers' inner circle, just ask Kenny G! He signed a one-year deal last off-season after spending the first part of his career in Philly as a third-down back and kick returner. Of course, most of us were not expecting much from Gainwell given his track record and the minimal investment, but goodness gracious, he was a force in PPR formats thanks to his team-leading 73 receptions. The only backs with more catches? CMC, Bijan, and Jahmyr Gibbs. He is a valuable commodity as a FLEX option, especially if Bucky Irving fails to regain his rookie-year form.
22562.dyn: The Buccaneers signed Gainwell to a two-year deal to mix in with Irving. He will never be a workhorse in the league, but he offers an NFL franchise a valuable skill set as a pass catcher out of the backfield. Consider him a hold in dynasty and an RB who will have start-worthy weeks in 2026.

22564.blurb: Let us hit you with some hard-hitting analysis. Ja’Marr Chase is good at the game! Even with Joe Burrow missing a huge chunk of the season, the dude still finished as the WR4 with over 15 fantasy points per game. Finishing as the WR1 overall is obviously in play, especially if Burrow can finally stay healthy and have one of those elite TD seasons. He is well worth the pick early in Round 1 of fantasy drafts.
22564.dyn: In our opinion, Chase is still viewed as one of those few untouchables in dynasty formats. Despite already being in the league for five years, he is still just 26 years old and at the peak of his prime. We have him locked in as a no-brainer top-five overall asset in dynasty.

22565.blurb: Olave was buried in ADP a year ago due to concerns about the Saints' QB room and his concussion history. Fantasy drafters who took the plunge on Olave in the middle rounds last season were rewarded in a big way as Olave banked career highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yards (1,163), and TDs (9) en route to a WR6 finish. Shough for the win! After Spencer Rattler was benched, Olave went on a tear, averaging 15.8 points per game with Tyler Shough under center. The target competition will be more difficult with the addition of Jordyn Tyson, but Olave is one of the most talented WRs in the league, and we love Kellen Moore’s up-tempo scheme. We would not be shocked to see Olave post back-to
22565.dyn: Olave was able to cash in a huge payday from the Saints, signing a four-year extension that includes $90M guaranteed. Get that shmoney, Mr. Olave! This new deal gives him stability as a fringe WR1 in dynasty start-ups.

22566.blurb: The former Steeler joins the Giants, and it seems like they have a type. Seriously, can you distinguish the skillset of Austin from Darnell Mooney, Darius Slayton, Jalin Hyatt, and incoming Malachi Fields? They might all be different heights, but their main contribution to the NFL is being cast as field-stretching, nine-route guys! These guys will catch a long bomb once every 5-6 weeks, and you will go, “Should I start that guy next week?” No! Don’t do it!
22566.dyn: Austin signed a one-year contract to get in his cardio on the field. Even with Malik Nabers coming back slowly from his injury, he is barely worth a cursory look in dynasty.

22587.blurb: St. Brown is the pinnacle of consistency. He has now finished as a top-8 fantasy WR in four straight seasons, and he has banked the WR3 overall finish in three straight years as Jared Goff’s high-volume WR1. There aren’t many WRs we would want over him in redraft leagues this season, making him a rock-solid pick in Round 1 of drafts.
22587.dyn: St. Brown is locked in with the Lions through the 2028 season, and he is still just 26 years old. We expect the fantasy goodness to continue for the next two to three years at a minimum, making him one of the most valuable WRs in all of dynasty.

22597.blurb: Former Cowboys legend, Jalen Tolbert, is now in Miami in what is probably the weirdest WR room we have ever seen. It is a mix of fringe NFL caliber wide outs and rookies. Shoot, Tolbert could be the WR1 or WR5! It’s a complete guessing game as to how these targets are going to be distributed in Miami.
22597.dyn: The Dolphins signed Tolbert to a cheap one-year deal after he was relegated to the WR4 role in Dallas a year ago. Like a dingleberry, he is barely hanging on in the NFL.

22598.blurb: For the first time in his career, Jaylen Waddle is going to be wearing a different uniform as he is now in Denver after being traded before the NFL Draft. The situation is clearly much better for scoring, playing with Sean Payton and Bo Nix versus Bobby Slowik and Malik Willis. The talent remains with Waddle, so there is upside here, but be mindful that Payton historically loves to use multiple WRs, RBs, and TEs to spread things out. We would love to say Waddle will dominate targets, but the more likely scenario is that Waddle will have to have a highly efficient season to be a difference maker for fantasy.
22598.dyn: Waddle’s recent seasons have not been what we had hoped for after some excellent fantasy seasons to start his career. He has been banged up, Tua got injured and regressed in a big way, and Tyreek Hill was stealing plenty of targets in Miami. Perhaps a change of scenery will bring Waddle back to fantasy dominance, but it is also possible we have already seen the best season of his career. This time next year, he will be 28 years old, so if you are not a contender and can flip Waddle on the intrig

tags.value: In March, the Broncos traded for the soon-to-be 28-year-old WR sending a 1st rounder to Miami. Since then, Sean Payton has not stopped gushing about Waddle all off-season saying he “walks on water” with his traits. Waddle remains in his prime as his per-route metrics from 2025 (2.42 YPRR) remind you that he is still a special player. Expect a ton of easy "layup targets" as Bo Nix has led the NFL in screen attempts over the last two seasons. He is the perfect addition to this Broncos offense and yet, his draft price remains far too cheap for a player we've seen finish inside the top-20 twice in his career.

22602.blurb: After spending five years with the Rams as a field-stretching, once-in-a-blue-moon threat, Atwell signed a one-year deal with Miami, joining possibly the worst-looking WR room in the known universe. Opportunity might present itself, but remember that Atwell is averaging 1.6 receptions per game in his career. He is unlikely to be a fantasy threat in any way in 2026.
22602.dyn: Remember when Sean McVay took this guy in the second round of the NFL Draft? Hey, you can’t take away “Super Bowl Champion” from the resumè of Chataris Atwell!

22623.blurb: When you are in the last round of your draft, shoot for the moon. Shoot for a guy who hasn’t done it yet in the hopes you find a diamond in the rough. Through five years, Bateman has yet to clear nine fantasy points per game. We will be happy to snag him off the waiver wire in the event of a Zay Flowers injury, but we would prefer to take some swings on younger rookies or insurance RBs late in drafts.
22623.dyn: Somehow, Bateman keeps getting money from the Ravens. He has now signed multiple extensions, yet it has never happened for fantasy. He provides more value to the team for his ability to stretch the field, but at this point, the ship has sailed in dynasty land.

22662.blurb: Quick, name the best TE on the Carolina Panthers roster. Exactly! On paper, Tommy “High-T” Tremble looks to be the TE1, but with 249 yards receiving and two TDs in 2025, you have to look twice: he is a blocking-first TE. With Ja’Tavion Sanders and Mitchell Evans rounding out this ragtag bunch of hooligans, if you are asked at your draft which Carolina TE you should go for this season, shake your head disappointingly and respond, “None, thank you.”
22662.dyn: If you are keeping an eye on one TE in Carolina, it is probably going to be Sanders, who is 23 years old, heading into his third season. Tremble will be 26 this year, and with five seasons under his belt with no real fantasy goodness, you really do not need to worry about him, even in dynasty.

23118.blurb: Willis' time in Tennessee was pretty forgettable, to say the least. The team took him in the third round back in 2022 and moved on after just three starts in two years. However, he landed in Green Bay as Jordan Love's backup and now has a chance to revitalize his career as a starter after getting some great coaching from Matt LaFleur. We have seen other young QBs (Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, Daniel Jones, for example) take similar paths: dumped by their original organization, sit and learn for a couple of years as a backup, and then get a second chance at a starting gig elsewhere. Could Willis be next? For fantasy, the Dolphins project to be among the worst teams in the league with straight
23118.dyn: The red flags are there: Willis has never attempted more than 23 passes in a game in his six career starts, and the Dolphins could be terrible in 2026. The window to sell Willis is likely gone after Jaylen Waddle was dealt. Expecting anything more than one full year starting in the NFL might be wishful thinking.

tags.sleeper: With the ADP market getting sharper year over year, it’s getting more difficult to find late-round QB upside. As a passer, we are not sure what Malik Willis can do, especially with these weapons. However, we know rushing at the QB position is a cheat code in fantasy, and Willis has serious upside as a mobile QB. Since 2024, he’s averaging 6.6 rushing points per game, making him an intriguing QB2 with upside. It is a small sample size, but in four games where Willis took the majority of the snaps over the last two years, his rushing stat lines are 9/60/2, 10/44/0, 6/73/1, and 6/41/0.

23119.blurb: You know what’s crazy? There is a world that exists where Treylon Burks is the WR2 for the Commanders in 2026. There are rumors of a Brandon Aiyuk trade or a Stefon Diggs signing, but right now, behind Terry, it is a completely barren depth chart. You don’t need to draft him, but he is worth monitoring in training camp if you play in a deep league.
23119.dyn: What a wild ride it’s been for Treylon. From first-round bust to potentially saving his career with Washington, we are rooting for ya, Mr. Burks! Unfortunately, that doesn’t mean he will have any life in dynasty. At this point, just sticking around the league for a few more years would be considered a huge win.

23120.blurb: Flowers is coming off a highly efficient 2025 campaign, setting a career high in targets (118), receptions (86), and yards (1,211). Over the last two seasons, Zay has averaged 2.61 and 2.35 yards per route run. Those are some elite marks. The guy is good! Unfortunately, the one bug-a-boo for Zay in fantasy land has been TDs. Through three seasons, he has topped out at just five scores. In order to make the leap into being a real difference maker, he is going to need to find the painted box more often. Perhaps he can fall into an outlier TD year, but with Lamar stealing some attempts in the red zone and King Henry still here, that seems somewhat unlikely for 2026.
23120.dyn: Flowers is in his prime, productive, and tied to one of the better offenses in the league. What’s not to like?! We are in on Zay in dynasty formats, viewing him as a top-24 guy, especially after he was signed to a four-year extension that includes over $100 million guaranteed. We aren’t sure if he can truly level up to being a top-12 type of asset. The ceiling feels capped, but he is a rock-solid WR2 to have on your dyno squad.

23121.blurb: The Patriots obviously felt Boutte was not a guy to build around with a young QB as they added AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason. He was the odd man out and on the outside looking in given the depth chart in New England. As a result, the trade to Houston makes a lot of sense for both parties. Boutte actually had a few startable weeks in 2025 (four weeks in the top 20), but let’s be honest: you never knew when those weeks were, and you definitely never had underpants strong enough in your closet to make it worthwhile.  The Texans lost Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL in camp, and in a corresponding move, they traded for Boutte in late August. He figures to slide in as the WR2 on the depth c
23121.dyn: Still only 24 years old, Boutte won't be spending 2026 with New England. He was sent to Houston via trade, and while the short-term landing spot is appealing from a playing time perspective (compared to sitting on the bench behind AJB and Romeo Doubs), he still doesn't have a contract beyond this season, so we wouldn't exactly tie him to Houston beyond 2026. He gets a nice boost here in the short term for his dynasty value as he goes from a potential roster clogger to a guy you can throw in your

23122.blurb: All this dude does is earn targets at an elite level. Since 2023, G Willy’s targets per route run rates are 25%, 25%, and 26%. Simply put, he is one of the best in the game at commanding a high target share. Unfortunately, that hasn't always translated into elite fantasy seasons, but we attribute that to lackluster QB play compared to other NFL WR1s. *Geno Smith has entered the chat.* Sadly, it could be the exact same scenario for Wilson in 2026. The talent is there, and the targets will be there, but the offensive environment could hold him back for fantasy once again. Nevertheless, he is a rock-solid WR2 for your team and gets a boost in full PPR formats.
23122.dyn: If we can get this man a real QB, he could break fantasy. Until that problem is solved (maybe in 2027?!), his name will probably hold more value on your dynasty squad than the actual fantasy production. He is entering his age-26 season, and he signed a massive $130 million extension not that long ago, tying him to New York through the 2030 season.

23132.blurb: First, the good: Young led his Panthers to an NFC South title and a close loss to the Rams in the Wild Card Round of the Playoffs. He also set career-highs in completion percentage (64%), passing TDs (23), and rush attempts. Yet, he exceeded 20+ fantasy points in just three games on the season and felt impossible to get a read on week-to-week. The NFC South is a weak division, but unless we see a spike in his scramble rate and pass attempts, topping 25 passing TDs would be a small miracle. It feels tough finding routes for Young to break through as anything more than a mid-QB2 for fantasy.
23132.dyn: The Panthers picked up Young’s fifth-year option, but there is still debate about whether he is the organization’s long-term answer at QB. In 44 career starts, he has been a top-12 QB in just 23% of them. He still has a lot of life left in the NFL, but unless we get another upgrade to the pass-catchers, it will be hard seeing him will his way to anything more than a mid-to-low end QB2 in dynasty. Young seems like a prime candidate to trade away in SuperFlex leagues if he is a luxury QB3 for your

23134.blurb: All hail the ultimate cardio king! Otton ran the fourth most routes among TEs in 2025 (540!) and was on the field for the third most passing plays (625!). Obviously, he crushed it in fantasy football, right? RIGHT? Exactly. Otton finished the season with only one TD, reminding us that fantasy football and real-life football regularly do not align. On a team full of offensive weapons, including two solid pass-catching RBs, Otton’s time in the sun is almost set. But hey, if your league gets fantasy points for getting your steps in, Otton should be the first off the board.
23134.dyn: You aren’t going to get anything of value for Cade Otton if you try to trade him, so on your bench, he shall live as you dream at night of positive TD regression. If somehow that happens, ship him out the door faster than Jason cranking down the AC in July.

23135.blurb: The former Ravens TE signed a 3-year free agent deal with $17 million guaranteed to be part of Mike McDaniels' revamped Chargers offense. We expect more heavy personnel this year in Los Angeles with multiple TEs and a fullback on the field making Kolar a sneaky name to monitor. His college receiving profile at Iowa State was legit but it is more likely that he hurts Oronde Gadsden II's fantasy value more than become an asset himself.
23135.dyn: Kolar was stuck behind Mark Andrews and Isaiah Likely in Baltimore but his signing in Los Angeles was no small transaction. We expect him to potentially lead the Chargers TE room in snaps making him a worthy bench stash in deeper leagues.

23136.blurb: Big Darnell (6’7”) continues to be one of the best run blocking TEs in football, but he has very little to offer when it comes to fantasy production in redraft. You are not even looking his way without an injury to the Muth, but even then, would it be anything but cursory? It is cool to just say no, thank you, and slowly walk away.
23136.dyn: We all wanted Gigantor 2.0 to be a thing, but with only one top-10 TE finish last season, it is hard to justify Washington as anything more than a bench clogger. Feel free to cut him and hold on to someone who has slightly more ceiling potential. We advise looking for something more than the split-level mid-century one that Pittsburgh is currently offering.

23138.blurb: The offensive weapons for Dallas were a delight for fantasy managers last season, simply because the defense was nonexistent. Fergalicious took advantage, especially in Weeks 3 through 6 when CeeDee Lamb was out finishing as the TE4, TE5, TE2, and TE10 during those weeks. He set career highs in receptions (82) and TDs (8), but the contributions fell off in the second half. The trained eye will say Ferguson will be due for some TD regression. However, you can trust in the fact that the Dallas D won’t be fixed overnight, making Fergy-Ferg a late-round target who should still get a fair amount of dump-offs in this offense.
23138.dyn: Ferguson signed a four-year extension in 2025, making him a big piece of the TE room in Dallas for a hot minute. Competition-wise, the ship looks to have sailed on the Schoon-man (Luke Schoonmaker). We are uncertain if Brevyn Spann-Ford is an actual guy, and the chance of rookie Michael “Trigg Daddy” staying focused enough at practice to make the team is slim to none. All in all, Ferguson looks to be the TE1 on a high-scoring offense for several years. He has a nice and dependable floor for your

tags.bust: After gathering eight TDs and over 100 targets in 2025, you might think Ferguson is a sneaky target in 2026. We feel the exact opposite as a deeper dive into his season reveals a rough final 3 months. He failed to hit double-digit fantasy points from Week 8 on gathering just a 13% target share in that span. He is at best the 3rd target in this offense trailing CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. If you want to play the TD roulette game every week, he can have his moments. However, there are many other TE options available who should provide a better guaranteed weekly floor than Turd Ferg.

23140.blurb: Always the bridesmaid, never the bride. Mayer will be the TE2 as long as Brock Bowers is a Raider. But wait, you say…Mayer must have tons of value when Bowers is out of the lineup, right? RIGHT? He did give you one TE5 week when Bowers was sidelined last year, but during the other week, he was TE41. This former 2nd round NFL draft pick will be valuable in 12-personnel sets to the Raiders but not for fantasy.
23140.dyn: The majority of Mayer’s dynasty value went poof the moment that Bowers was drafted, and he has done nothing to build it back up. The blocking TE in Las Vegas need not be on your fantasy roster.

23141.blurb: LaPorta tried real hard to put together a season reminiscent of his astounding rookie year starting out fairly well with four top-6 finishes before being sidelined with a season-ending back injury. His 12.2 yards per reception were a career high, and his 81% catch percentage is delightful. But what happens now? New OC Drew Petzing catapulted an all-time season from Trey McBride in Arizona so we are left wondering if LaPorta will get the TMcB treatment this season. The Lions have one of the easiest schedules in the NFL, making LaPorta’s later round ADP palatable as we still consider his ceiling and TD upside enticing. However, it's worth pointing out that LaPorta is dealing with a hip injury
23141.dyn: LaPorta is heading into the final year of his rookie deal, and if he ends 2026 with a bounce back and a bang, expect the team to lock him up. His underwhelming 2025 season and back issues do present an opportunity to buy at a discount. He is a solid TE6-TE8 in dynasty startups.

tags.value: This is all about cost. Remember when LaPorta surprised every one as a rookie and was the TE1 in 2024? He was overpriced in 2025 and now it seems like the pendulum has swung back too far in the other direction. It is rare to be able to find TEs later in your draft with legit potential to finish in the double-digits in the TD department. The Lions offense could be a juggernaut and the team is favored in 14 of their first 15 games! LaPorta is circled in our drafts as a TE to target if you miss out on the elites early.

23142.blurb: Johnson was putting together a decent sophomore season in 2025, highlighted by an average of 4.9 targets a game and a budding connection with Jaxson Dart. However, he missed the final two weeks of the season with an unspecified illness, ending the year with a whimper. All was looking promising until John Harbaugh came to New York and brought Isaiah Likely with him. Now Johnson is the TE2, dropping out of the redraft conversation. What a roller coaster.
23142.dyn: It is frustrating with Johnson, as it feels like the promise of a future TE1 spot on his team was pulled out from under him with the signing of Likely. He is still young and with the Giants on his rookie deal through 2027. We can hope that Harbaugh will utilize more two-TE sets in New York, as he did in Baltimore. Consider Johnson a hold in dynasty, but his window is likely gone. (See what we did there :)

23151.blurb: Can we get this man a QB? We know London is one of the most talented WRs in the league, yet it feels like there is still so much untapped potential given what has been going on in Atlanta. Even though Tua and Penix have their warts, we are closing our eyes in drafts and betting on talent with Drake, who has been targeted on 30% of his routes over the last two seasons. In case you missed it, the Falcons are trotting out some combination of the three stooges behind London: Jahan Dotson, Zachariah Branch, and Olamide Zacchaeus. Let’s get this guy 10+ targets a game and see what happens!
23151.dyn: In dynasty, betting on young, highly drafted, and productive WRs is a winning strategy long term. That is why we will continue to bet on London even if the surrounding environment leaves a lot to be desired. Let’s hope the Falcons can find their long-term franchise QB next offseason because the Drake is here to stay. He signed a massive 4-year extension with the team in early June, making him one of the highest paid WRs in the league.

23153.blurb: George! Jason’s My Guy came through in a huge way in his first season in Dallas. His stats are a bit juiced for those games without CeeDee Lamb, but the point remains - Pickens is a super talented WR who plays in a scheme we like with a QB in Dak who can support elite fantasy seasons. The only thing to consider for fantasy is that the ADP for him is higher than it was a season ago, so we are not getting any discounts here like we were a year ago when Pickens was available in the middle rounds.
23153.dyn: Pickens’ dynasty outlook hangs in the balance after he signed the franchise tag with the Cowboys. Does he end up getting a huge extension with Dallas, or does he go chase the bag elsewhere in 2027? The upside is obviously there to be a top-12 to top-15 option, but the situation isn’t stable right now, given the contract question marks.

23155.blurb: Super Bowl champion and Eagles legend, Jahan Dotson, is now in Atlanta after signing a two-year deal in free agency. Behind Drake London, this WR room is full of some #NastyBoys, and Dotson might be the nastiest of them all. THE cardio king, Dotson has averaged an embarrasingly low 0.63 yards per route run over the last two seasons. It’s hard to put into words how bad that is…
23155.dyn: If you are still holding Jahan Dotson in your dynasty league, it is time. Set him free and never look back!

23157.blurb: If you grabbed JSN in the third round last year, you likely won your league as Smith-Njigba was incredible all year long, leading the league in receiving with almost 1,800 yards and 10 scores. His efficiency could regress after he averaged a silly 3.74 yards per route run, but he is still an easy click in the first round of fantasy drafts as one of the few guys in the league who can command a 30+% target share.
23157.dyn: Seattle just made JSN one of the highest-paid WRs in the league, and we know the talent is immense. He is an easy top-five WR moving forward and well worth a first-round selection in start up drafts.

23162.blurb: The Vikings’ offense was a train wreck last season, with that QB play being stinky, hot garbage. Of course, all pass catchers suffered as a result, including Addison, who is coming off his worst season since he entered the NFL back in 2023. The addition of Jauan Jennings does add some uncertainty to Addison’s target share behind Jefferson, but we have seen enough of him in the league to know that he is capable of posting WR2 numbers if things break his way. Ultimately, Addison’s ability to reach his fantasy potential will come down to how well Kyler plays with Kevin O’Connell.
23162.dyn: The Vikings picked up Jordan Addison’s fifth-year option, so he is under contract for two more seasons. We will see if Minnesota signs him to an extension in the next year or so, but for fantasy, he has settled into a rock-solid WR3 for your dynasty squad and is still only 24 years old.

23165.blurb: This guy is so fun to watch when he is making an explosive play, but through three years, he has played just 32% of the snaps. Darn you, Sean Payton! You tricked us thrice into thinking he could actually be something! We know now, he is pretty much just their kick returner.
23165.dyn: Mims will always be remembered in dynasty formats on the promise of “Sean Payton traded up in the second round to draft this guy.” Sadly, he’s just a part-time player who will never have any real value. Oh, what could have been!

23167.blurb: For the first time in his career, Doubs will not be playing in green and yellow; he signed a lucrative contract in free agency to join Drake Maye and the Patriots. However, the arrival of A.J. Brown puts him back in FLEX territory as a "better for the NFL than fantasy" type of WR. His receiving yards (724) and fantasy points per game (8.6) were a career-high last season but middling marks compared to the rest of fantasy WRs. He should be an every down, outside guy which pushes him to just a bench stash with some FLEX appeal.
23167.dyn: Doubs never carries a ton of value in the dynasty trade market or in startups, but when on the field, he produces WR3 numbers. Still only 26 years old, Doubs is a solid depth piece for a contender, especially after he signed a four-year deal with New England that includes $39M in guarantees.

23170.blurb: Brian Daboll is now in Tennessee, which is potentially very important for Wan’Dale’s fantasy outlook. The two were together in New York over the last few seasons, and we have seen Robinson heavily involved in Daboll’s offense, seeing 140 targets in back-to-back seasons. Carnell Tate has room to grow into the alpha, but Robinson leading the team in targets is definitely in the range of potential outcomes.
23170.dyn: Robinson is never a guy who is going to command a ton of value in the dynasty trade market, given his lack of perceived upside, and yet, he is a solid volume-based WR3 for your squad. Still just 25 years old and now quite rich thanks to a new contract in free agency, Robinson has plenty of production left in his NFL career.

23173.blurb: Before suffering a torn ACL in the divisional round against the 49ers, Charbonnet was arguably the better fantasy asset than Kenneth Walker III on the season. His 12 rushing TDs tied James Cook for fifth most among RBs, and he ranked seventh in yards after contact per attempt. It was clear the team trusted him as they entered the red zone with 17% of his carries occurring inside the 10-yard line, the second highest rate of any qualifying RB in the NFL. He will begin the regular season on PUP with the possibility that his recovery extends into October. He is buried in our rankings and someone we are happy to see get drafted by another league mate as they wait for his return.
23173.dyn: Once he does get on the field, he will need additional time to ramp up, which means he is unlikely to be fantasy relevant until November at the earliest. The most likely outcome here is that 2026 is a lost season, which is difficult timing considering he is entering the final year of his rookie contract.

23187.blurb: Tyler Shough truthers, take a bow. Entering the 2025 NFL Draft cycle, a lot was made about Shough's age, but credit to New Orleans, they seem to have found a diamond in the rough. Over his final five starts, he averaged 20 fantasy points per game, a 70% completion percentage, and 27 rushing yards per game. He unlocked Chris Olave and showed out with the best completion percentage in the intermediate area of the field (11-19 yards). We believe in Kellen Moore as a play-caller, and the addition of eighth overall pick Jordyn Tyson to the WR room gives Shough another weapon at his disposal. However, Tyson is set to miss multiple regular season games after suffering a hamstring injury in camp. Th
23187.dyn: Shough defied the ageists and became a legit fantasy threat down the stretch. Nevertheless, it seems many are pausing, calling the season a fluke. As a QB2 in SuperFlex, he could be acquired potentially with a late first-round rookie pick.

tags.sleeper: New Orleans went with Spencer Rattler to open the 2025 campaign, and to no one’s surprise, the Saints went 1-7 to open the year. From Week 9 on, the Saints were a respectable 5-4 under Shough, who banked five QB1 weekly finishes in his nine starts. Kellen Moore’s offenses are always up-tempo and ranking among the league leaders in pace of play, so Shough and the Saints offense are on the short list of teams capable of finishing inside the top-five in overall play volume. When you have a mobile QB like Shough, who is now throwing to stud Chris Olave, top-10 NFL Draft pick Jordyn Tyson, and free agent signee Travis Etienne out of the backfield, it’s not hard to see a world where Shough outperforms his ADP. The Saints also have the second-easiest strength of schedule in the NFL, and they play 10 dome games in 2026.

23189.blurb: It was a video game-like 2025 season for Bijan, totaling 2,298 yards from scrimmage, the most since CMC in 2019. He accounted for 41% of Atlanta’s total team yardage thanks to ranking first among all RBs in forced missed tackles and percentage of the team’s first-read targets. If you are splitting hairs at the top of your drafts, the only knock on Bijan might be the functionality of the Atlanta offense and how the QB position shakes out. He is all that is great in fantasy football and a true building block if you have the pleasure of drafting him.
23189.dyn: He is arguably the best offensive player in football, and now he's paid like it. The Falcons signed him to a three-year extension in early August that includes $51M in guarantees. Bijan should once again be featured in 2026 under new offensive play-callers Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees.

23190.blurb: As CMC’s backup last year in San Francisco, “BRob” totaled just 104 opportunities, including a meager eight receptions. His biggest contribution to fantasy this year could likely be when some dumb-dumb in your league accidentally drafts him in Round 1 as “B. Robinson- RB, ATL”. Tyler Allgeier vacates 160 opportunities, so expect the big-bodied back to mix in occasionally in short-yardage situations for Atlanta. Still, he should not have much standalone value behind Bijan.
23190.dyn: At 27 years old, BRob’s best fantasy football days are likely behind him. His one-year deal worth $2.5 million makes him purely an insurance back, and we know Bijan has been invincible thus far in his career.

23192.blurb: The RB2 job is up for grabs with Emanuel Wilson now in Seattle. Marshawn Lloyd looks to be the next man up, but he has just six carries to his name in the NFL, as he has dealt with injuries for two years straight. If he cannot stay healthy again, Brooks could be in line for the RB2 role for a good offense with Josh Jacobs' legal situation playing out. He is a dart throw in your drafts, knowing the team also traded for former Steelers third-round RB Kaleb Johnson.
23192.dyn: Brooks has been in the league for three years as a former UDFA, and he has never been more than a part-time role player. These profiles rarely hit for dynasty, but with Josh Jacobs' legal situation ongoing and Marshawn Lloyd a question mark in the NFL, Brooks should be rostered in deep dynasty formats in case he wins the RB2 job.

23193.blurb: There are those out there clamoring for more Tank touches as the Eagles’ backup RB averaged 5.7 yards per carry playing behind the same offensive line Saquon Barkley did in 2025. Bigsby was acquired after Week 1 and did not sniff double-digit touches in a game until Week 15. With just 11 career receptions, he remains in a niche role as an early down thumper behind one of the league’s most talented backs. You can certainly add him to your roster with one of your final picks as an insurance policy.
23193.dyn: Bigsby enters the final year of his rookie contract without much room to make noise in fantasy apart from a Saquon injury. How dare you even suggest such things!

23196.blurb: GEORGE! The Seahawks special teamer was thrust into a bigger role during the NFL playoffs after Zach Charbonnet went down with his ACL tear. He caught three passes in the NFC title game but will once again be relegated to third or fourth string on the roster. Rookie Jadarian Price should work ahead of George, with Charbonnet eventually returning from injury, but until Charbs gets healthy, Holani will have a role as a change-of-pace option.
23196.dyn: There is a small Holani hive that meets in the shadows, begging and demanding that their hero be given more opportunities on the field. They are a selective group believing the former undrafted free agent will rise from the depths and eventually take over an NFL backfield. “He’s good”, they say, referencing his Week 10 TD run against Arizona. “George is electric!” writes an anonymous group leader in their AOL group chat forum, mentioning his 24.2 yards per kick return average in 2025. “The gover

23200.blurb: Perhaps our small brains cannot comprehend this man’s greatness in fantasy football. Gibbs is a superstar, totaling the most TDs (49) in NFL history by any RB through their first three years in the NFL. After Dan Campbell took over as play-caller (Week 10), Gibbs had the seventh most receptions of any player in the NFL as David Montgomery was phased out of the offense. Gibbs should see the biggest workload of his career and is a worthy selection at 1.01 this year. Consider your opponent’s pants pee-stained every time he touches the ball.
23200.dyn: Gibbs got a bag of money thrown his way over the summer, making him the highest paid RB in the NFL. He is one of the most explosive players in the league and a surefire early first-round pick in startups. If you want to take him ahead of Bijan or one of the elite WRs, we do not blame you.

23205.blurb: “Uncle Jerome” had a brief moment filling in Cleveland a couple of years back, but at this point, he is nothing more than another camp body. Someone in the Washington backfield will get the short end of the stick after training camp and pre-season. Sorry, Jerome, but everyone is pointing at you.
23205.dyn: The former fifth-rounder was once useful on the Browns, including a surprising RB17 season in 2023. His days of fantasy relevance and taking up an NFL roster spot are likely coming to an end.

23211.blurb: The 88th overall pick in 2024 had seven total touches through two years as his body continues to betray him, but he has made it through camp without an injury (knock on wood). Seriously, can this guy make it from practice to the NFL field? So far, so good -  and now Josh Jacobs' off-the-field issues make him an intriguing play. The fact that the Packers didn't take a single RB in the NFL Draft for the second straight year suggests the team was still envisioning him for the RB2 role behind Jacobs as he becomes one of the premier insurance backs in drafts. We have docked Jacobs in projections, and depending on how long he is suspended, we consider Lloyd a plug-and-play RB2. Feel free to reach
23211.dyn: Lloyd barely played as a rookie and never saw the field in 2025, but his value skyrocketed after Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exemption list. He is a hold if you need RB help, but a potential cash-in if he is a luxury on your roster.

23212.blurb: Ever since Sean McVay gave Kyren the reins, he has been amazing for fantasy, finishing as a top-10 back in three straight seasons. He is rarely hitting big plays or flashing elite speed in the open field, but he is as dependable as they come, and McVay trusts this dude. Blake Corum is probably going to steal a few TDs and work in for a handful of touches per game, but when the game is on the line, McVay is calling Kyren’s number. In 2026, he is projected as a volume-based high-end RB2 who could bank another RB1 finish if the TDs go his way.
23212.dyn: Williams signed a three-year extension with the Rams, but fantasy managers should really treat this like a two-year window. He is already entering his age-26 season.

23214.blurb: Ken Bone! Walker was a key piece of the Seattle offense down the stretch and parlayed his Super Bowl MVP award by receiving a big old bag of money from the Chiefs. He signed a three-year deal worth just over $14M per year. He is still only 25 years old and remains one of the best home run hitters in the game, something that was severely lacking in KC's run game over the last two years. For context, over the last two years, Chiefs RBs have run for 10+ yards less than 9% of the time, 31st amongst 32 teams. Enter Walker, who was third in the league last season in rate of 10+ yard runs and #1 in forced missed tackle rate. Expect 18-20 touches per game as the team re-establishes the run game and
23214.dyn: If you have Ken Walker on your dyno squad, you have our permission to join the Hitman in removing your pants at this time. This was an incredible run out for a player who always tantalized with his per-touch ability. Only 25 years old, he is a top-10 dynasty RB in startups for us.

tags.breakout: The Kansas City Chiefs gave Ken Bone a three-year, $43 million contract for one clear reason: their RB situation in 2025 was not one that dreams were made of. A backfield made up of aging Kareem Hunt, Isiah Pacheco, and Brashard Smith managed just over 1,200 yards on the ground, pushing Mahomes to scramble (422 yards rushing) and ultimately go down to injury. The team's total yards on the ground? The eighth fewest in the league. Enter the Super Bowl MVP to save the day! Walker should get tons of opportunity; we anticipate less running from Mahomes recovering from that ACL tear, Travis Kelce is not any younger, and Rashee Rice is…who knows. The Chiefs' offensive identity could run through Walker this year, his ADP is incredibly manageable, and the depth chart is far from intimidating. Color Mike ecstatic.

23217.blurb: 'Dick White,' as he's known around TFFB HQ, is going to be donning new colors in 2026 after spending the first four years of his career in Tampa. White was the guy a couple of seasons ago, but he was relegated to a change-of-pace option with the emergence of the more efficient Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker over the last two years. For context, his opportunities per game have declined from 20.1 to 12.6 to 10.4 over the last three seasons. We know his place as a pass-catcher, and he might be going overlooked in drafts despite our projections having him as a FLEX option.
23217.dyn: Already 27 years old, White gets a short-term deal (one-year, $2 million) to join a committee in Washington where he can specialize as a pass catcher and in pass protection while playing with his former college QB, Jayden Daniels. This is nothing more than a one-year experiment.

23227.blurb: Shakir has been a great target earner in the NFL, seeing 23% and 21% target shares each of the last two seasons. However, his aDOT is nonexistent, and he is not really involved in the red zone. For fantasy, Shakir gets a small bump in full PPR, but you are never winning your league because of him, especially with DJ Moore now in town.
23227.dyn: Shakir signed a big extension with the Bills, but his role didn’t change much in 2025 as a low aDOT slot player. Now, the team went out and traded for DJ Moore. He will have value for the Bills, but the ceiling just isn’t there for a guy like Shakir. We view him as a solid FLEX/bench piece for your dynasty roster.

23232.blurb: Get that money, Mr. Pierce! After years of being a part-time role player for the Colts, Pierce showed out in 2025 with his first 1,000-yard season and cashed a huge payday with Indy. That financial commitment from the team suggests they think he can level up as a top target without Michael Pittman, but it is worth noting that he has never been a high-volume pass catcher, even going back to his college days, so it does take some projection on that front. For context, he has never had more than 52 receptions in a single season in either the pros or in college. There is some volatility with a big play threat like Pierce, so we like pairing him with more reliable high target share guys earlier i
23232.dyn: It took a few years for Pierce to develop in the NFL, so the fact that he went from a bench roster clogger to a guy who is one of the highest-paid WRs in the league is kind of wild. Nonetheless, this massive contract gives him plenty of value in dynasty formats. He is an interesting player with a wide range of outcomes, so we could see this going either direction. If you are a dynasty player who likes to play the market, it is certainly possible he has already reached peak value, so we would not

23233.blurb: Reed is a talented football player, but we are still waiting for him to put it all together for a full season. He has always popped up for big games a couple of times per year, but he has been a part-time player ever since he entered the league, making him an impossible start/sit decision weekly in redraft leagues. With Romeo Doubs in New England and Dontayvion Wicks now in Philly, perhaps that changes in 2026. If Matthew Golden can’t get it going in Year 2, and Tucker Kraft is slow to return to form off his ACL, Reed could be a sneaky late-round WR target.
23233.dyn: The Packers signed Reed to an extension earlier this offseason, so he has at least got the financial security from Green Bay. You would think the contract suggests Reed can level up and be a full-time player, but we have just never seen it, as he remains a 3WR set-only type of player. If that role expands, his dynasty value will bounce back in a big way, but if he remains a part-time guy, he will probably remain a weekly headache from a start/sit decision.

23234.blurb: You know what is fun? Jamo ripping off chunk gains thanks to some of that elite speed. Dan Campbell knows this. John Morton? Not so much. Before Guns Mahoney took over play calling, Jameson Williams’ role was frustrating for fantasy as he was used as a low-volume, high aDOT boom/bust type of guy. However, after Campbell took over the offense, Jameson Williams was one of fantasy’s most valuable WRs as he was on pace for 1,400 yards after the Week 8 bye. It is important to note that Sam LaPorta was also out for a big chunk of the season. Still, the point remains: Jamo is crucial to the Lions’ offense reaching its full potential, and he should continue to have a high upside role that is worth t
23234.dyn: Williams just signed a massive three-year extension with the Lions, so he is locked in with Detroit through 2029. It is possible he never turns into a consistent WR1 for fantasy, but he is an extremely valuable dynasty asset who can win you a week when those big plays hit.

23235.blurb: After a storybook rookie season, the Washington Commanders nosedived in Year 2 of the Jayden Daniels era as he struggled with injuries (knee, hamstring, and elbow) before being shut down in Week 15 for the season. His rushing numbers remained on par with 2024, but the cast of receivers certainly let him down as 11% of his passes were dropped, the highest rate in the NFL. Daniels can be a difference-making fantasy asset due to his legs, but drafters are not giving any sort of discount this year. In other words, you will have to pay up for what he did as a rookie and the hope that he can return to top-5 status.
23235.dyn: Jayden won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2024 and took the league by storm. Then in 2025, he recorded just ONE top-12 fantasy finish. We still view him as a top-tier fantasy QB given his elite rushing ability, but his true ceiling is at least worth questioning in the short term, given the lack of continuity at OC and barren skill group.

23237.blurb: CROD! The former Commanders RB quietly ranked fourth among all qualifying RBs in rush success rate and trailed only Bijan Robinson in yards after contact per attempt last season. If you want to connect a few dots, he played his college ball at Kentucky, where Liam Coen was the OC; in that season, he logged 238 touches as the lead ball carrier. He hasn't really done much in the NFL thus far, but the familiarity in Coen's system at least adds some threat to Bhayshul Tuten's early-down role in 2026. Consider him a solid bench stash in your drafts, hoping he finds his way to FLEX value for your teams.
23237.dyn: Besides the utter joy of his nickname, the Jaguars must like this guy as they signed him to a two-year deal with $6.2M guaranteed. It may not seem like a ton, but considering he got more guaranteed money than Rico Dowdle, the money says he could have a role in Liam Coen's offense. Beyond 2026, he is a mystery.

23239.blurb: The decline is painful to watch as Stroud went from fantasy darling as a rookie in 2023 to an afterthought and liability the last two seasons. He has averaged just 218 passing yards per game with six total top-12 finishes, the same number he totaled as a rookie. With arguably the best defense in the NFL, the Texans do not need Stroud to put up gaudy numbers to compete. He is stuck in redraft purgatory as a QB likely sitting on your waiver wire to be picked up only for plus matchups.
23239.dyn: We loved Stroud as a player coming out of Ohio State and felt justified with an awesome rookie campaign. However, he is relegated to back-end QB2 territory despite his youth. The Texans’ defense and his lack of elite rushing numbers will keep his ceiling capped. The Texans extended his fifth-year option, so expect a long-term contract to be worked out in the near future.

23241.blurb: After missing half the season with a toe injury, fantasy managers hopped on Purdy’s back in the fantasy playoffs as he finished the season as the QB5, 4, and 1. Always underappreciated in fantasy, his 6.2% career TD rate is the fourth best ever for a QB through their first 50 games. We always want to buy into the 49ers offense as long as CMC is alive and well; with the addition of Mike Evans, perhaps Purdy can find the formula to enter into top-10 territory at the position.
23241.dyn: Purdy has been one of the most efficient starting QBs in the NFL since he took over for San Fran a few years ago. Kyle Shanahan's scheme is just too good, and Purdy is a great fit for it. He signed a big-time extension last off-season, so he is locked up for the next several years.

tags.value: It feels like Purdy’s fantasy fame remains overlooked despite an unreal finish in the fantasy playoffs. He is consistently a TD outlier and adds enough on the ground to give you a weekly floor. The 49ers are double-digit home favorites in Weeks 2 and 3, where you can expect them to sport the highest implied totals. Get ahead of your league mates by either grabbing Purdy as your QB2 and waiting to plug him in for those contests.

23242.blurb: The Falcons were roasted for surprisingly taking Penix eighth overall in 2024, and the results thus far are barf-worthy. In two seasons, Penix has started 12 total games while completing less than 60% of his passes. For context, that ranks 29th among 33 QBs taken in the first round of NFL Drafts over the last decade. He suffered a torn ACL in Week 11 last year, and off-season reports suggest the team is not rushing his rehab with Tua Tagovailoa now in tow as competition.
23242.dyn: It feels like a make-or-break season for Penix entering Year 3 under a new regime with a new head coach, new GM, and new president (former QB Matt Ryan). Averaging under seven rushing yards per game in his 12 career starts, it is hard to paint a picture where Penix becomes anything more in fantasy than a bar conversation with your buddies: “Hey, remember when Atlanta paid Kirk Cousins AND drafted Michael Penix Jr.?!?!”

23245.blurb: Stop if you have heard this before: we love us some Hendo. It was a painfully slow start to his career, but he broke out in the second half as the RB8 from Week 9 on, averaging 16.7 fantasy points per game. When Rhamondre Stevenson was out for a month, he showcased bell cow capabilities, averaging 20+ opportunities per game and an 80% snap rate. We know he is explosive, but will the coaching staff trust him as the team’s main passing-downs back in 2026? He carries massive upside at his ADP, but we would recommend building out RB depth on your roster around him as you navigate the beginning of the season with Hendo.
23245.dyn: He is one of six rookie RBs to average 5+ yards per carry, sport a 50+ % rush success rate, and score 10+ TDs since 2000. Yet, we still have concerns that Rhamondre Stevenson’s contract could hold him back from truly hitting his fantasy ceiling. We have him ranked as a top-15 RB in dynasty formats, but our projections might have him end up finishing lower for 2026.

23247.blurb: After agreeing to a four-year contract extension in mid-August, James Cook punched every "TD-regression" metric in the face in 2025, leading the league in rushing yards and finishing as a top-6 fantasy back. He paced the league with 11 games of 80+ yards rushing and ranked 3rd in yards after contact. The only stain on Cook’s resume is his declining involvement in the passing game, as he averaged just 1.9 receptions per game last year. Fantasy managers can have confidence in the continuity of this Buffalo offense, the play-calling, and an offensive line that continues to maul opposing fronts. Cook remains a strong RB1 for us in 2026.
23247.dyn: Over the last two seasons, his 28 total rushing TDs rank fourth among all RBs. He is tailor-made for Joe Brady's zone scheme and is under contract until 2030. At just 26 years old and tied to Josh Allen, he remains a steady dynasty asset as a low-end RB1.

23250.blurb: Poor Tyler. After signing a two-year contract with the Cardinals, the team promptly gave him a proverbial stiff-arm, selecting rookie Jeremiyah Love third overall in the NFL Draft. The 26-year-old bruiser will still make noise inside the red zone after his seven rushing TDs inside the 20-yard line actually outpaced Bijan Robinson last year in Atlanta. However, for redraft purposes, he is nothing more than a bench stash and insurance back for Love managers.
23250.dyn: Allgeier is a solid bench RB in dynasty with a nose for the end-zone, albeit on a team that projects to have the worst record in the NFL. Holding him over the Jeremiyah Love manager might be your best course of action if you are trying to extract any semblance of value.

23251.blurb: If you were able to behold the TE season to end all TE seasons, you are probably still singing the praises of TMcB. With Jacoby Brissett at the helm, Trey McBride was unlocked, running 696(!) routes while breaking the single-season TE reception record with 126. He took advantage of various injuries among other Cardinals pass catchers to finish the year with 11 receiving TDs, a massive jump from the two he scored the year previous. We know that the TD total stands quite a chance to regress on a Cardinals team projected to win the fewest games in the NFL. Be that as it may, expect another year of massive volume, giving fantasy managers a positional advantage.
23251.dyn: What is there to say? Enjoy. McBride signed a four-year extension with the Cardinals in April 2025, so he is not going anywhere soon. McBride and Bowers will dance back and forth as TE1/TE2 for many years to come.

23253.blurb: The Eagles traded for Dontayvion Wicks and immediately signed him to a one-year extension as he has some familiarity with new OC Sean Mannion, who comes over from Green Bay. We ultimately expect him to be mixing in with Hollywood Brown on the perimeter, but unless Jalen Hurts all of a sudden becomes a prolific passer, Wicks isn’t likely to be a meaningful fantasy contributor behind Smitty and Makai Lemon.
23253.dyn: Wicks has always flashed target-earning potential (and drops), and he is just 24 years old. You could probably throw him in your starting lineup should DeVonta Smith or Makai Lemon miss some time, so if you are in a deeper league, you could certainly keep him on the end of your bench. Philly signed him to a one-year extension worth $12.5 million after trading for him earlier this spring.

23256.blurb: Remember Week 1 of the 2024 season when Likely had over 100 yards receiving and a TD, and the entire fantasy community went, wait whaaaat? Mhmm. The man is now out of Mark Andrews’ shadow and ready to live large in New York. Target-wise, the big competition is Malik Nabers, and behind him are the likes of Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, and fellow TE Theo Johnson.  We are following the money ($26 million guaranteed) and his connection with John Harbaugh in assuming that Likely will be a significant part of this offense. You don’t have to go after him early to invest in this late-round flier.
23256.dyn: Likely’s dynasty situation really couldn’t be much better. He lands on a new team with a coach who pushed for him and shares rapport with. The 25-year-old signed a three-year deal, and he has an exciting young QB in Jaxson Dart to grow with. He does have Theo Johnson sharing the room, but Harbaugh has made clear his proclivity for multiple TEs on the field. If you have Likely, hold and hope for the breakout.

tags.sleeper: After signing a 3-year deal to reunite with John Harbaugh in New York, Likely now finds himself the 4th highest paid TE in the league in terms of per year average ($13.33 million). We have seen great moments from him as he averaged 12.5 PPR fantasy points per game in nine games without Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Every trusted Giants source has echoed that Likely has been Jaxson Dart's #1 target in camp with Malik Nabers out and likely (see what we did there) will be the No. 2 when he returns. Very few TEs carry this type of upside this late in your drafts so swing away!

23310.blurb: You may have forgotten about the curly-locked, marvelous-mustached Greg D, especially since he has done close to nothing fantasy-wise during his four years so far in the NFL. The best we saw from him was a TE30 finish in his rookie season in Denver. However, Greg showed glimmers of promise at the end of last season finishing second in yards per route run among TEs from Week 9 onward. Miami desperately needs pass-catchers considering a WR core of Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert, and Tutu Atwell in South Florida. No offense to those guys, but it puts Dulcich in a great position to potentially be the target leader for new QB Malik Willis. Greg D also finished second among all TEs in YAC/catch,
23310.dyn: If Greg D takes advantage of this season in Miami fantasy-wise, you may have some trade bait on your hands. There is little chance that the Dolphins don’t look to flesh out this WR room in the upcoming drafts. If he has some spike weeks and you have other competent TEs on your roster, it is worth kicking the tires to see what you could get.

tags.sleeper: Greg D! That’s right, baby. The man with the luscious locks and mustache has made the official Sleepers list. Now, let’s not get too crazy. You do not need to be drafting Greg D in standard 10-team leagues or most 12-team leagues, but if you play in a deeper league and are looking for a guy you can snag well into the double-digit rounds if you are punting the position, Dulcich is worth a look. The Dolphins have very little talent at the WR position after cutting Tyreek Hill, trading away Jaylen Waddle, and moving on from Darren Waller. Dulcich is likely to play as an every-down TE, and he is quietly coming off an efficient 12.9 yards per reception in 2025. We obviously aren’t projecting him as a top-12 guy for the season, but it would not be surprising at all to see him bank multiple TE1 weeks thanks to his athletic ability after the catch.

23364.blurb: Mason continues to show he belongs in the NFL, averaging 5.1 yards per carry since coming into the league in 2022. For context, only De’Von Achane (5.6) and Jahmyr Gibbs (5.3) are higher in that span. After averaging 16 opportunities per game through the first six games, he eventually fell behind Aaron Jones Sr. in the RB rotation down the stretch in a lost season for the Vikings. Mason is older than you might realize (27 years old), but is only an injury away from being an every-down workhorse.
23364.dyn: Mason is a fun dynasty story to share as savvy managers read the tea leaves of the last few years and hopefully recouped value as a startable RB2/FLEX when needed. Signed in free agency last year, Mason has one more year on his deal before the void years kick in. He carries a number of rushing yardage incentives (800/900/1,000 yards) in his contract that could come into play down the stretch.

tags.sleeper: Mason might be seen as an afterthought in your drafts but he projects to be the early down thumper and goal-line back. His efficiency metrics were way better than you might remember from last year ranking 9th in rush success rate, 4th in percentage of 10+ yard runs, and 9th in forced missed tackle rate. Aaron Jones Sr. will mix in on passing downs but his injury issues and age declines have him 2nd in the pecking order of preferred Minnesota RBs. Kyler Murray at QB can hopefully restores some of the up-tempo, high-play volume we’ve been accustomed to from Kevin O'Connell offenses the previous three seasons. Mason is a late round pick likely forgotten by the rest of your leaguemates.

23368.blurb: Nailor was a solid WR3 on the Vikings, catching 10 TDs over the last two seasons. He parlayed his limited success into a multi-year deal to be a starting WR in Las Vegas. If opportunity is your thing, Nailor has an opportunity (opposite Brock Bowers) to see a 20% target share because, well, someone has to! We preach chasing talent over opportunity at the WR position, but Nailor’s draft cost suggests he is worth a flier and bench stash to start the season.
23368.dyn: He likely will be a volatile fantasy performer attached to a rookie QB, but it is nice to see the former sixth-round pick secure a bag. He signed a three-year deal worth up to $35 million and moved about five seats up on the bus from “end of bench stash” to “maybe I can FLEX him” territory.

23371.blurb: After a solid 2023 campaign, it has been all downhill since for Pacheco after suffering a brutal fibula injury in 2024 and essentially being irrelevant for fantasy in 2025. The veteran signed a one-year deal to replace David Montgomery and his 34 red zone carries. Pacheco’s efficiency numbers are downright disgusting, but opportunity is everything in fantasy. He has been left for dead in ADP, but the setup seems ideal: the clear RB2 on a good offense that can handle a three-down workload if needed. The Lions are favored in a ton of games, so it would not be surprising if Pacheco returned low-end FLEX value this year once he gets healthy. He's set to miss multiple weeks in camp because of a s
23371.dyn: Beyond 2026, we have no idea what Pacheco is for fantasy. However, he described his initial pitch from HC Dan Campbell with lots of screaming on the phone, making the pairing of these two “high-T” guys interesting for the short-term.

23395.blurb: Watson’s bug-a-boo since he entered the NFL has been injuries. When he is on the field, he is highly efficient and scores plenty of fantasy points. That was on full display last season when he returned to the lineup in Week 8 off a torn ACL and went on to average 2.67 yards per route run and 11.5 fantasy points per game. The Packers’ depth chart is thinned out entering 2026, and Matthew Golden really struggled as a rookie, giving Watson relatively weak target competition for one of the better offenses in the league. There is a shaky floor with a guy like Watson due to durability concerns, but if you are looking for a high upside WR pick in the middle rounds, Watson can be nitro to your squad
23395.dyn: The Packers gave Watson a huge 4-year, $110 million contract extension in early June. They view him as a bonafide WR1 with this type of money but we have him in the low-end WR2 territory in dynasty.

tags.breakout: If you have ever had Christian Watson on your fantasy team, you know the roller coaster ride well. Seemingly prone to injuries, you could never drop the guy, because when on the field, he was always a threat for a big play. He played ten games last season and was the WR13 or better in four of them, including a fabulous WR4 finish in Championship week against Baltimore. He finished the year fifth in yards per route run and averaged 17.5 yards per reception. It was scarier to roster Watson last season when the WR room was as packed as Costco on a Saturday afternoon, but now there is some breathing room. Romeo Doubs is in New England, Dontayvion Wicks is an Eagle, and Matthew Golden is still Matthew Golden. Target-wise, the battle looks to be between Jayden Reed, Tucker Kraft, and Watson, and even if Watson gets the short end of that stick, he is on a great offense with a solid QB, and going late enough in drafts that he could be your WR3.

23469.blurb: Tyquan can fill a role for the Chiefs as a situational deep threat, but we cannot imagine a world where he is a consistent starter in your lineup.
23469.dyn: Thornton is back in KC on a two-year deal worth $11 million. Honestly, good for you, dude! Things looked rough in New England, but he seems to have settled in nicely as KC’s field stretcher. With Rashee Rice in the news yet again and Xavier Worthy a bit of a question mark long term, there are probably worse stashes in deep leagues.

23479.blurb: Warren had a high floor throughout the season, averaging 16 opportunities per game and 12.3 fantasy points per game while receiving a “B” in our consistency metrics. While he ceded passing downs work to Kenneth Gainwell down the stretch, it was the best fantasy season of Warren’s four-year career, thanks to an increase in workload. He was rather pedestrian inside the 5-yard line, converting only four of his 14 carries. His outlook for 2026 is souring with the signing of Rico Dowdle and the arrival of a new coaching regime. He is stuck in a complicated backfield mess, profiling more as a FLEX, knowing he could take a backseat to Dowdle at some point.
23479.dyn: The former UDFA is under contract for two more seasons, although his dead cap hit in 2027 ($1.9 million) gives the team an out. He feels like an RB you are just happy has held FLEX value for a few seasons. If someone out there is willing to pay more for his services, we do not mind packaging him in a deal as he enters his age-28 season.

23489.blurb: Chig had his moments in Tennessee, flashing some YAC-ability but never quite being a consistent fantasy threat. He signed a three-year contract with the Washington Commanders, breathing new life into his fantasy prospects on a roster that desperately needs another pass-catcher opposite WR Terry McLaurin. You won’t have to pay too much to take a shot on the guy, so why not? He looks like an easy stash or waiver wire pickup early in the season. Chig is not dead for fantasy yet, we say!
23489.dyn: We saw flashes in a sub-par Tennessee offense last year with four top-12 weeks in fantasy. As the presumed TE1 in a much better offense, he saw a value boost this offseason but remains a mid-level TE2 for fantasy. If you are looking to add TE depth this off-season for a small price, Chig is your man!

tags.sleeper: The Commanders added Stefon Diggs but as it stands, the WR depth chart behind Terry McLaurin is weak with guys like Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown, and third-round rookie Antonio Williams as possible contributors. Enter Chig Okonkwo, who signed a three-year deal in free agency with almost $17M guaranteed. It is certainly possible he is the 2nd or 3rd option in the pass game, and given his athletic profile, we are willing to take shots in drafts as a late-round option.

23662.blurb: For a few weeks in 2025, “Tonges McBasketball” was the hero we didn’t know we needed. With George Kittle nursing his hamstring from Week 2 through Week 6, Tonges stepped up valiantly, giving us at least a couple start-worthy weeks. He had three weeks on the season as the TE9 or better. With Kittle battling back from his Achilles injury, there is a strong chance he won’t be ready to start the year or resemble the same old Kittle when he does. Tonges is practically free in drafts and will be the assumed TE1 on a Shanahan-led team. Consider him a low investment if you need to plug the TE position early.
23662.dyn: Tonges was rewarded for his service in 2025 with a two-year contract extension ($8 million) in March. He is the epitome of a strong TE2 with TE1 upside when thrust into the role. Brock Purdy trusts him, and the pass-catchers in San Francisco seem to drop like flies when a light breeze blows through the bay. He could be worth even more to the Kittle manager so feel free to kick the tires there.

23729.blurb: Seattle traded for Shaheed in the middle of the season last year, and he was a key piece of their Super Bowl run, particularly in the kick return game. For fantasy, things just never got going, however, as he was never a high-volume pass catcher behind JSN and Cooper Kupp. Now with a full offseason in Seattle and a big fat paycheck, perhaps that changes in 2026. We view him as a boom/bust late-round dart, but we do know that he is a fully capable WR who has produced in New Orleans when given the opportunity.
23729.dyn: Rashid Shaheed got paid this offseason, signing a brand new three-year deal worth $51 million. That investment says he will remain a key piece of the team moving forward, but his snap share could be frustrating in 2026 with Cooper Kupp still on the roster. We do not expect him to be consistent, but he is always a viable FLEX play who can put up a big score thanks to his game-breaking speed.

23880.blurb: If you are looking for the RB2 behind Javonte Williams, look no further. The former undrafted free agent has stuck around Dallas bouncing between practice squad and being buried on the depth chart the last few years before showing out in limited opportunities last year. He balled out when Javonte Williams missed Week 17 going for 103 rushing yards against the Commanders.  Consider him the insurance RB to roster for a high-powered offense.
