23880.dyn: Davis enters a contract year with just 90 total carries since coming into the league in 2022. He is an insurance back that Javonte managers could hopefully acquire now that Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah did not make the final 53-man roster cut.

24102.blurb: After his rookie season finish of TE11 in 2023, it has been downhill ever since for the guy we were hoping to become Josh Allen’s No. 1 target. His 49 targets only translated to 571 yards, five TDs, and a TE15 finish. With Joe Brady stepping in as HC, the offense should look similar, but there is no guarantee. The team added DJ Moore in the offseason to finally give Allen a WR1, and TE Dawson Knox continues to be another solid receiving option; remember, everybody eats in Buffalo. You won’t feel confident heading into this season with Kincaid as the only TE on your roster as four targets per game will not get it done in the TE fantasy streets.
24102.dyn: There was a time when we were pumped for the young TE tied to a high-powered offense and a QB with an arm who could sling it. He is under contract for two more seasons sustaining his value as a fringe TE1 for dynasty. Keep the light on for Kincaid to see how the offense is run with Brady at the helm, but make that light small. And dimmable.

24116.blurb: The Rams finally did it. They lessened the workload on Kyren Williams in 2025 after hinting at it for a couple of seasons. In 2024, when Corum was a rookie, he wasn’t a factor at all. However, in his sophomore campaign, he siphoned off 159 total opportunities for a 35% share of the carries. Kyren is obviously the lead back in this offense, but it is entirely possible Corum pushes that number closer to the 40 - 45% mark. If he does, he could have standalone value as a weekly FLEX play. Of course, should Kyren go down, Corum would project as a no-brainer weekly RB1, so he is also one of fantasy’s most valuable insurance policies while playing for one of the best offenses in the league.
24116.dyn: Corum has two more years on his rookie deal after being a third-round pick in 2024. Unfortunately, as long as Kyren is on the roster, his value will be capped as a solid depth piece. Williams signed a three-year extension not that long ago, so he is under contract through 2028.

tags.sleeper: For the last couple of seasons, the Rams have hinted at more of a committee approach to ease the workload on Kyren Williams, and down the stretch last season, we finally saw that come to fruition with Corum siphoning off 145 rush attempts to Kyren’s 259. We are still projecting Williams to maintain his RB1 role in 2026, but it is possible that the gap is tighter than it was a season ago after Corum bested his teammate in yards per carry, explosive rush rate, and missed tackles forced per attempt. If this happens to be more of an even split, Corum is a sneaky value later in drafts. Even if Kyren keeps his bell cow role, Corum is one of fantasy’s top-tier insurance backs tied to one of the best offenses in football.

24118.blurb: Kraft was on his way to a monster season in 2025, boasting two TE1 weeks and averaging close to six targets a game, until he tore his ACL in Week 9 against Carolina. He was Green Bay’s leading receiver with 32 catches for 489 yards and six TDs on 44 targets up until that point. Despite his major injury, you will still have to pay up to draft Kraft, making him a dicey draft decision. The talent is there, and the targets could be even easier to come by, but also factor in that Kraft might not be ready to go by Week 1.
24118.dyn: Of course, Kraft is ahead of schedule and reported to be back early in the regular season, targeting a Week 1 return. Shocking. 2026 marks the final year of his deal with the Packers, but GM Brian Gutekunst has made it clear that talks regarding a contract extension are underway. Both Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks have moved on, bumping Kraft up in the target pecking order, and the Green Bay offense should continue to produce at a high level with Jordan Love at the helm. Kraft is a YAC king a

24119.blurb: “Yoshi” is just running around out there having a great time as the WR3 behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. He is good enough to stick around the league and keep his role, yet he’s not going to steal targets from Chase and Higgins. So long as both studs are healthy, Andrei should remain on the waiver wire.
24119.dyn: Over the last two seasons, Iosivas has averaged less than 30 receiving yards per game. It ain’t happening, buddy!

24120.blurb: Welp! Another offseason discussing Rashee Rice and his off-the-field issues. Rice missed the first six weeks of the 2025 season while serving a suspension, and this past offseason, he violated his probation when he tested positive for marijuana. As a result, he is serving jail time in June and July. On top of that, we also got news in late May that Rice underwent a “clean up” procedure in his knee that could sideline him for roughly two months. If you recall, Rice’s 2024 season came to an end after he suffered a season-ending LCL, hamstring and posterolateral corner injury. So, to recap, we have another legal issue and a health concern. It all adds up to make Rice a highly volatile player en
24120.dyn: If you are a Rice manager in dynasty, this latest off-the-field incident feels like a complete gut punch. He is so valuable in terms of his fantasy production, but he is in a contract year and likely losing trust with the Chiefs. If they aren’t willing to pay him, and he leaves the Andy Reid and Pat Mahomes scheme, does his future production take a hit, and what happens if he is in the news again for legal troubles? His dynasty value could take a massive hit in the next 12 months.

24123.blurb: The 25-year-old enters the final year of his rookie contract stuck in no man’s land for fantasy. Tony Pollard eats up the majority of early down work, and the Titans offense routinely fails to convert long drives. In fact, Tennessee was tied or trailing on 84% of their offensive snaps in 2025, with only the Jets and Saints being worse. You would think that would translate to sweet, sweet Spears garbage time production, but the Titans RB totaled just 14 fantasy points as a third-down receiver all year long. In the deepest of PPR leagues, he makes sense as a bench stash, but he could face more competition for touches with fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton.
24123.dyn: Spears is still there for one more year as the change of pace back. His degenerative knee injury was discussed when he was drafted coming out of Tulane, and now you are seeing him slowly fade into being a typical bench RB, whom you never quite know when to start.

24143.blurb: Washington went from just a depth piece for Jacksonville to their leading receiver in 2025. Wild times, man! Following the bye week and Travis Hunter’s injury, Washington saw a 23% target share while running roughly half his routes from the slot. We are really interested in taking shots on this Jaguars’ offense, but it is nearly impossible to project the WR usage here, especially with Travis Hunter’s role up in the air. As a result of that uncertainty, expect the Jaguars guys to all be decent values in drafts. There is some downside with each individual WR here, but if you hit on the right guy, the payoff could be massive, especially at these depressed ADPs.
24143.dyn: A former sixth-round NFL Draft pick who didn’t do much early in his career, there is a good chance you were able to snag Washington off your waiver wire. If you did, that is a massive boost for your squad to add a guy who can give you WR2 or WR3 production in the right matchups. He is entering the final year of his rookie deal, so it remains to be seen if he gets an extension. The team invested a first-round pick in BTJ a couple of years back, traded up to select Travis Hunter second overall jus

tags.sleeper: If you checked out during the back half of last year, you probably missed what Parker Washington did down the stretch. From Week 9 on, Washington’s 17-game pace was 77 catches, over 1,200 yards, and 7.5 TDs. He even went 7/107/1 in the playoffs against Buffalo. The previous regime never really gave him a shot to be an every-down player, but under Liam Cohen, Washington was a key contributor down the stretch after Travis Hunter landed on IR. Looking ahead to 2026, the Jaguars’ WR room is one of the most difficult to project in the league. Brian Thomas Jr. is a wild card, Jakobi Meyers remains a serviceable NFL WR, and Travis Hunter’s role remains a complete question mark. That uncertainty will keep Washington’s ADP in check. As long as that is the case, we don’t mind taking a swing on a player who was highly efficient in this scheme over a pretty decent sample a year ago.
tags.value: If you checked out during the back half of last year, you probably missed what Parker Washington did down the stretch. From Week 9 on, Washington’s 17-game pace was 77 catches, over 1,200 yards, and 7.5 TDs. He even went 7/107/1 in the playoffs against Buffalo. The previous regime never really gave him a shot to be an every-down player, but under Liam Cohen, Washington was a key contributor down the stretch after Travis Hunter landed on IR. Looking ahead to 2026, the Jaguars’ WR room is one of the most difficult to project in the league. Brian Thomas Jr. is a wild card, Jakobi Meyers remains a serviceable NFL WR, and Travis Hunter’s role remains a complete question mark. As long as that is the case, we don’t mind taking a swing on a player who was highly efficient in this scheme over a pretty decent sample a year ago.

24145.blurb: The talent with Downs has never really been a question, but he is traditionally been a slot-only player in the NFL…until 2026? That is the million-dollar question for a guy like Downs, who could see a big uptick in playing time and targets with Michael Pitman Jr. now in Pittsburgh. Indy paid Alec Pierce big money in free agency, but behind Pierce and Downs, the WR depth chart is pretty thin, with the most notable addition here being Nick Westbrook-Ikhine. No offense to NWI, but that is not exactly scary competition to get on the field and perhaps set a career high in route participation. Give Josh Downs more routes, and generally speaking, good things are likely to happen for a guy who has b
24145.dyn: Downs has a chance to go from just a bench piece to a meaningful starter in your lineup if he is able to work his way onto the field in 2WR sets this year. Over the last couple of seasons, he has been pigeon-holed as a part-time slot player, so there is a good chance he is not highly valued in your league, but we are fans of his talent, and the opportunity is there with Pitty City gone. We do not mind the idea of trading a second round rookie pick to get a guy who is a proven producer in the NFL

tags.sleeper: The problem for Josh Downs in fantasy over the years has been a lack of playing time in 2WR sets. The talent has never been a question, but it is hard to get overly excited about a slot-only player in today’s NFL. Moving forward, Downs’ role could grow in 2026 as an every down player with Michael Pittman now in Pittsburgh. The Colts’ depth at WR is relatively weak, and when you consider that Alec Pierce has never been a high-volume WR throughout his collegiate or NFL career, Downs could really pile up volume as Indy’s top WR target earner. You can snag him as your WR4 or WR5 in drafts with next to no risk, considering his late ADP in the double-digit rounds.

24150.blurb: The Packers double-dipped in the TE in the 2023 NFL Draft, and even though Tucker Kraft has had the breakout season, it was Musgrave whom the team took earlier (second round). Musgrave had a chance to show why he was drafted earlier when Kraft went down with his ACL injury in Week 9, but he did nothing with the opportunity. He averaged just over two targets a game from Week 10 on, only marginally better than the 1.25 a week he was averaging with Kraft on the field. Either way you slice it, not great.
24150.dyn: Musgrave’s dynasty window is only slightly propped open as he enters the final year of his rookie deal. Unable to capitalize on Kraft’s missing time in 2025, it is hard to believe that he can do it while sharing time with him in 2026.

24172.blurb: Puka was dominant in 2025 with a league-leading 107 receiving yards per game and six weeks of 20+ fantasy points, the most among WRs. He was an absolute dominator on 50/50 balls, tracking down 27 contested catches, the most of any WR over the last decade. Aside from off-the-field issues, he is simply unstoppable and off-the-charts in every per-route metric we care about for fantasy. If you wanted to take Puka at the 1.01 in a full PPR league, we totally understand.
24172.dyn: Money please! That sound is the giant bag of cash coming Puka’s way after he totaled the second-most receiving yards through a WR’s first three years in the NFL behind only Justin Jefferson. We have him firmly amongst an elite three of WRs we would take at the very beginning of dynasty startups.

24173.blurb: Michael Wilson’s 2025 breakout was…nuts. We almost never see nonproductive WRs pop up for huge games the way Wilson did in 2025, but here we are. The man went nuclear without Marvin Harrison Jr. on the field, averaging seven catches and 97 receiving yards per game from Weeks 11-18. For context, that 17-game pace is 187 targets and over 1,600 yards. Fantasy drafters need to be aware that the Jacoby Brissett pass rate of last season is probably going to regress, and with Marv now healthy, we likely will not see the same target share. That said, there is a world that exists where Wilson is more productive than Marv in 2026. Pain.
24173.dyn: Wilson AKA Jerry Rice went from a dynasty roster clogger to a weekly must-start down the stretch last year. Truth be told, we are not sure what to make of Wilson’s story. He was a fine, yet uninspiring prospect, then spent 2.5 years running wind sprints before doing what he did in 2025. He is in a contract year, so the future is murky at best. If you can capitalize in the trade market in your league after his hot run to close 2025, it is probably not a bad idea. We see a wide range of outcomes m

24176.blurb: Dell missed the entire 2025 season with a catastrophic multi-ligament knee injury, and his timeline for 2026 is still unclear. It looks like he will be able to play some snaps for Houston at some point this year, but he's beginning the regular season on IR as he ramps up. As a result, he should not be on your redraft radar at this time, especially after the team traded for Kayshon Boutte in late August.
24176.dyn: Dell and Stroud had a clear connection, even for a short while. You are not getting anything for him on the open market, so a speculative (and hopeful) hold is where we are at.

24177.blurb: Is there anyone in the NFL with better cardio than Tucker? After running nearly 600 routes in 2024 (fifth most in the NFL), he followed that up with the seventh most among WRs in 2025. He had a monster Week 3 game (8/145/3) against Washington, but then faded back into oblivion, surpassing ten fantasy points just one other time the rest of the season. This Raiders WR room might be one of the worst in the league, giving him yet another year to end up on the field more than you realize. For the game we play, he likely is waiver wire fodder yet again.
24177.dyn: Tucker enters the final year of his rookie contract with a ton of snaps played but minimal fantasy impact. His agent will probably bring up the fact that he increased his targets, receptions, and receiving yards every year of his career. Oh, and maybe he will put together a PowerPoint of all the routes and snaps this dude has been on the field for the last two years.

24179.blurb: Coming off one of the most consistent fantasy seasons for an RB of all-time, hopefully, any doubts you had about Achane should be buried deep in the ground. He became one of four RBs ever to score 11+ fantasy points in every single game and ranked #1 in yards per carry (5.7) and explosive rush rate (10%) among all qualifying RBs. When you mix in his receiving work, he is a cheat code at the position. Despite Miami’s low win expectation for 2026, we are still in on his price tag at the 1/2 turn in draft as a locked-in RB1.
24179.dyn: Achane signed a four-year, $68M extension, making him one of the highest-paid RBs in the league. While the Dolphins might be going through a rebuild, his dynasty value remains stable as a top-5 RB in startups. The pass-catching cheat code that he is will help him age well in this format.

24180.blurb: Good old DeMario “Pop” Douglas never really popped (see what I did there?) and will be at the bottom of a depth chart led by AJ Brown. With 80% of his routes coming in the slot, he is a bit part player on a depth chart that has bypassed him.
24180.dyn: Sure, he will have a random big week, but any chance that he could materialize as a solid starter for dynasty has disappeared.

24194.blurb: Tucker had a few shining moments in 2025, including a monster RB1 overall performance in Buffalo in Week 11. He can flash at times and also led the team in carries (14) and rushing TDs (6) inside the 10-yard line. However, the Buccaneers backfield needs to move from a three-headed monster (Bucky, Kenny G & the Tuckmeister) to two in order for him to be started with any confidence. Expect Tucker to be floating on waiver wires after your drafts.
24194.dyn: Tucker signed a one-year deal worth $3.52 million to return as the team’s preferred goal-line back. There is a place for that on a dynasty bench, as he is better suited for standard or half-point formats.

24214.blurb: Keaton Mitchell had some moments in Baltimore as an explosive home run hitter, but he never developed into an every-down player thanks to some injuries and a random guy named Derrick Henry. Now in LA, Mitchell should be battling with Kimani Vidal for the RB2 role behind Omarion Hampton. The Chargers just invested a first-round pick in Hampton a year ago, so we are projecting him as the bell cow. That doesn’t leave much fantasy value for a guy like Mitchell in standard redraft leagues, but he could end up being one of fantasy’s premier insurance policies if he beats out Vidal for the backup role.
24214.dyn: The Chargers signed Mitchell to a two-year deal in free agency, so he is blocked by Omarion Hampton in terms of the depth chart through 2027. He needs to be rostered everywhere just in case Hampton misses time, but he is not going to bring much value to your squad outside of a Hampton injury.

24223.blurb: In his third year in the league, Strange was given the keys to the Jacksonville TE room with the departure of Evan Engram. There was a clear connection with Trevor Lawrence, as Strange had a 77% catch rate, including five weeks as TE10 or better.  Unfortunately, he was out for five weeks due to injury, and now the team double-dipped in the TE well with rookies Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol. We are fairly high on the Jags offense and the value of Trevor Lawrence this year, making Strange a potential cheap late-round pick. If you have a deeper bench, Strange might be worth a shot to see how the team looks out of the gate.
24223.dyn: Brenton Strange was about to enter 2026 in the final year of his rookie deal, but the team signed him to a three-year extension worth up to $48M. That financial backing gives him a nice boost in dynasty formats as a fringe top-12 option for the next 2-3 years.

tags.value: If you miss out on elite TEs, we preach every year, ignoring the “middle round” trap at the position. Strange presents himself as a late-round value after he commanded a 16% target share in 2025. The hyper-athletic TE is in a contract year on a team that emphasized their need to run more 2TE sets this year. Second-round pick Nate Boerkircher profiles mainly as a blocking TE, while Strange is clearly the pass-catching weapon. Consider him a solid streamer with room to develop into a weekly starter.

24226.blurb: Only five WRs collected 8+ receiving TDs in each of the last two seasons: Ja’Marr Chase, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Tee Higgins, Davante Adams, and (drumroll)… Quentin Johnston. After previously being the laughingstock of fantasy leagues, he morphed into a solid outside option for Justin Herbert. He led the team in receiving yards (789), deep targets (19), and fantasy points per game (10.4). He may not look appealing on a fantasy roster, but Johnston’s TD upside makes him a worthy second FLEX option, especially in games where the Chargers are favored. He averaged a solid six targets and 11 fantasy points per game in wins the last two seasons
24226.dyn: The Chargers picked up his fifth-year option, so Quge will be on the team for at least the next two years. He is a cheap FLEX option worth acquiring as a throw-in for trades.

tags.sleeper: The Chargers' offense should look a lot different in 2026 with new OC Mike McDaniel now calling plays. Their roster moves suggest we will see plenty of multi-TE sets, so figuring out which Charger WRs are playing in 2WR sets is going to be crucial for predicting fantasy success in this WR room. Johnston makes a lot of sense in that role given his size, speed, and ability to play on the perimeter. Since that forgettable rookie season, Johnston has improved year-over-year in fantasy points per game and yards per reception as a player who seems to be figuring it out in the NFL. With Justin Herbert under center in a scheme that could unlock plenty of efficiency, Johnston is worth a pick in the later rounds of drafts as a potential WR3/FLEX with the capability to provide your roster some ceiling performances.

24309.blurb: Wilson was quietly better than Josh Jacobs on a number of efficiency metrics. He is coming off a career high 142 total opportunities in Green Bay and flashed in a major way with his lone start in Week 12 with Jacobs sidelined. His addition to the Seattle backfield is noteworthy given Kenneth Walker’s departure and Zach Charbonnet’s ACL tear. There is a massive opportunity up for grabs in this Seahawks backfield, although first-round pick Jadarian Price will be the lead back with George Holani as the RB2. Expect Wilson to mix in here and there, but he's not on the redraft radar.
24309.dyn: The 27-year-old signed a low-risk one-year deal worth up to $2.1 million. That contract and the drafting of Jadarian Price suggest he is nothing more than a depth piece for this squad.

24347.blurb: We all assumed last year’s rookies (Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel) would steal playing time from boring vets like Xavier Hutchinson, but he was able to keep his role all season, playing 58% of the snaps. Unfortunately, he is not an efficient player and has averaged less than 13 receiving yards per game in his career (hey, don’t laugh!). After Jayden Higgins tore his ACL in camp, Hutchinson could mix in for snaps again this season, but that does not mean he will be fantasy-viable, especially after the team traded for Kayshon Boutte.
24347.dyn: Hutchinson is entering the final year of his rookie deal with Houston, so he will likely be looking for work on the open market next season as the Texans look to Jayden Higgins (in 2027) and Jaylin Noel (and maybe Tank Dell?) as their future depth pieces behind Nico Collins.

24348.blurb: We might have mentioned Tillman as a Sleeper last summer thinking he could seize opportunity as Cleveland’s WR2. Welp, nothing to see here! Move along! The team has a completely new regime and restocked the WR position with rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.
24348.dyn: Tillman had his moment and he failed to “Carpe Diem”. He can be dropped safely.

24374.blurb: It looked like Brown might end up one of 2025’s biggest fantasy busts after averaging just 8.1 fantasy points per game on 51 total yards through the first five weeks of the season. He ended up becoming a league winner en route to seeing the fourth-most targets among all RBs while averaging 100 total yards per game from Week 6 on. The only yellow flag in his profile is his lack of major success inside the 5-yard line. Cincinnati failed to bring in any other significant RB competition, making Brown yet again a candidate to finish as an RB1 for the third year in a row as part of this Joe Burrow-led offense.
24374.dyn: Brown survived yet another off-season where the Bengals failed to add a challenger in the RB room. As a PPR monster attached to a high-powered, Brown is in a sweet spot for fantasy as we consider him a fringe top-10 dynasty RB. Expect a potential off-season extension to surface this summer.

24436.blurb: Chad Ryland is a kicker for the Arizona Cardinals.

24609.blurb: Many thought Demercado was signed to fill out the KC backfield behind Kenneth Walker III, but he was cut in late August then claimed off waivers by the Cowboys after Dallas cut Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah. He did quietly have some electric moments through his first three years in the league highlighted by a robust 6.5 yards per carry. Among RBs with at least 125 carries over the last decade, that ranks #1 although the actual fantasy impact has been minimal. He will probably begin the season as the RB3 behind Javonte and Malik Davis, so there's no fantasy value here outside of injury.
24609.dyn: The former UDFA is a big play threat that lands in an offense that desperately is searching for big plays after ranking 32nd in explosive rush rate in 2025. Consider him a bench stash with no guarantee of any value beyond this year.

24923.blurb: After two seasons backing up De’Von Achane in Miami, it is clear Wright is not cut from the same cloth. He was drafted for his speed (4.38 40-time), but is averaging only 3.9 yards per carry and caught eight total passes. He is a backup RB on a team currently favored in just one of their 17 games. Translation: he is not on our redraft radar.
24923.dyn: With Mike McDaniel out the door, any semblance of hope you had for the Dolphins carrying a 1-2 punch at RB is gonezo. The curse of players coming from the University of Tennessee's college offensive system continues to plague teams that drafted them. He is rosterable but will not be usable apart from an Achane injury.

24924.blurb: Worthy had a chance in 2025 to really take a step forward to start the season while Rashee Rice was serving his suspension. Unfortunately, in the first quarter of the first game of the season, Worthy dislocated his shoulder and never looked right, playing through injury all season. You can certainly explain away some of the down production last year, but truth be told, we still do not know how good a player he is in the league. In two seasons, he is averaging 1.40 yards per route run and earning targets on 18% of his routes. As the kids say, those numbers are pretty mid. Still, we are always interested in taking shots on Mahomes’ pass catchers, and the Chiefs didn’t add any meaningful talent
24924.dyn: Worthy had promise as a first-round rookie WR, but through two seasons in the league, his metrics suggest he is unlikely to turn into a fantasy difference maker. That said, Travis Kelce is another year older, and Rashee Rice is in a contract year. If you were a Worthy truther coming out of Texas, he is probably worth a look in the trade market, but it is a make-or-break season for Worthy’s future dynasty prospects.

24927.blurb: Williams set the Bears’ all-time passing yardage mark (3,942), improved his pressure-to-sack ratio mightily, and had five games of 24+ fantasy points in Year 2. However, the erratic play still frustrates fantasy managers as he completed just 58% of his passes, a mark surpassing only Shedeur Sanders and J.J. McCarthy. He was more effective as a runner, including adding three scores on the ground. In Year 2 of the Ben Johnson system, perhaps there is room for Caleb to fly even higher and finish as a top-5 QB.
24927.dyn: We are lower than the market on Caleb, putting him inside our top-10 QBs, but firmly two tiers behind the other top-end guys. The upside is tantalizing, especially entering his age-24 season with one of the best young pass-catching corps in the league. He is a hold, considering anyone trading away Caleb wants an absolute haul.

24933.blurb: What happened here?! BTJ was amazing as a rookie, and all signs pointed to a huge breakout in Year 2. Unfortunately, Thomas’ second season in the league was plagued by inconsistency, drops, injury, and poor play overall. Ultimately, he ended up being one of fantasy’s biggest busts of 2025. Entering 2026, we are now looking at this Jags’ depth chart completely differently. Travis Hunter’s usage remains unclear, Parker Washington played so well down the stretch that you would think he has earned a role, and the team traded for Jakobi Meyers last year, then immediately signed him to an extension. Something’s gotta give in a crowded WR room. Right now, we are viewing BTJ as a potential bounce-ba
24933.dyn: There aren’t many WRs who go out and do what Brian Thomas did as a rookie. Is there cause for concern after a frustrating Year 2? Sure, but this is still a former first-round NFL WR who averaged 2.56 yards per route run as a rookie. Over the last decade, most of the guys who check both of those boxes have gone on to be fantasy difference-makers. We recognize the risk, but now that his cost is down in startups and in the trade market, it might be time to see what it takes to get him on your squad

24934.blurb: Honest question: Do you have any memory of Allen contributing in the 2025 season? If you do, you are either a “Rain Man” or a diabolical liar, as he touched the ball 20 total times before bowing out for the rest of the season to an MCL sprain. He is a man-child and an impressive physical specimen, but likely nothing more than a dart throw in your drafts.
24934.dyn: At just 22 years old, Allen remains one of the youngest RBs in the league despite having “two years” of NFL experience. You can start connecting the dots with a tin foil hat on and see a path for Allen to be a fantasy monster if Breece Hall went down.

24943.blurb: Who has two thumbs and might be the only legitimate pass-catching option on his team in 2026? This guy! Bowers followed up his incredible TE1 rookie season in 2024 with a TE8 finish in 2025, which, honestly, feels almost just as successful given the state of the QB and organization in Vegas. His targets per game dropped from 9.0 to 7.1, but he broke through with seven TDs in only 12 games played. Add in some competent QB play, either in the form of Kirk Cousins or Fernando Mendoza, and Bowers could rival Trey McBride’s 169 targets of last year. There is so little target competition in Las Vegas that he could break fantasy in 2026.
24943.dyn: With the revamping of the Las Vegas offense and Klint Kubiak’s arrival, is it possible that Brock Bowers has gained even more steam as the TE1 in dynasty? There will always be the Bowers/McBride debate, but regardless of which side you land on, Bowers can and should be the cornerstone of your dynasty squad if you are fortunate to have him.

24944.blurb: Brooks enters his age-23 season with 12 total touches over two seasons since he was taken 46th overall. We have not seen him on the football field since Week 14 of the 2024 season after he brutally re-injured his ACL. Monitor training camp news and beat reporters to see how involved he could be in 2026. Rico Dowdle vacates 51% of the carries and 10% of the team’s targets, giving credence to Brooks being a sleeper name to stash at the end of your drafts. We always loved the talent, but for now, we still have projected behind Chuba Hubbard in Carolina.
24944.dyn: He is one of the great mysteries of dynasty after he was the first RB taken in the 2024 NFL Draft and then vanished from relevance. His value is also a complete wildcard as he ranges from potentially overtaking Chuba to fading back into oblivion. If you have Brooks, he is a hold in hopes he resurrects from his fantasy grave.

tags.sleeper: Call him an international man of mystery as we have little on-field evidence through two injury-plagued seasons that Brooks can be a lead back in the NFL. However, the backfield situation in Carolina might be more up for grabs than fantasy managers realize. The slow-footed Chuba Hubbard had zero runs of 15+ yards as Rico Dowdle usurped him after the first month of the season and saw a whopping 36% of the team's total rush attempts and targets from Week 5 on. Brooks can step into a bigger role in 2026 with Rico departed and his pass-catching profile from his days at Texas should boost his upside in your mind. For now, his ADP is tame which screams sleeper material in your drafts.

24947.blurb: Sanders is recovering from a broken fibula and will be battling with Tommy Tremble for the top option at the TE position in Carolina this season. You don’t really want a TE on a team with a QB who averaged under 200 yards passing a week, do you? Do you?
24947.dyn: Inconsistent target volume makes you nervous holding onto Sanders in dynasty. The team could move on from Tremble after 2026, so you could tentatively hold onto Sanders to see how the depth chart plays out. You would really need Bryce Young to take a step forward to give you any sense of confidence in Sanders.

24953.blurb: When on the field and healthy, there aren’t many better than Malik Nabers. Unfortunately, the talk all offseason about Nabers is going to be injury, specifically his recovery from ACL and meniscus surgery. It is one of fantasy football’s biggest storylines to monitor throughout the summer. We are projecting him to be limited early in the season, so just understand that Nabers will come with risk in redraft leagues, and it is not out of the question that he could start the season on the PUP list. If and when he does get back to 100%, he is likely to provide a big impact to your team, but you might need to wait longer than you would prefer.
24953.dyn: Nabers is a young superstar. Those guys are really hard to acquire in dynasty leagues, but this injury might provide a small buying window. If you are not a contender and can take on some risk with your sights set on the future, Nabers is a great trade target, knowing you could really get a bounce-back season in 2027.

tags.bust: It stinks being down on one of the most electrifying WRs in the league, but this is all about injury with Malik Nabers. He is coming off an ACL reconstruction and a meniscus repair and required a secondary procedure in the spring to aid in his recovery. Because of this lengthy rehab, we are not expecting him to return to form until the middle of the season, so with his ADP likely to remain elevated because of the name value, he is a tough sell early in drafts where the opportunity cost is so high.

24954.blurb: AD Mitchell has always had that tantalizing upside, but he is entering Year 3 in the NFL, and it still remains to be seen if he can play as an every-down complete NFL WR. After being sent to New York via trade last year, Mitchell popped up for some big games down the stretch without Garrett Wilson, but in classic AD fashion, he disappeared for weeks at a time. He will now have a full offseason in the system, so perhaps he can put it all together in 2026. Unfortunately, the target competition is now pretty difficult with Wilson healthy, Breece Hall in the backfield, and the Jets double-dipping in the first round of the NFL Draft with Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. You do not need to be draf
24954.dyn: Mitchell’s slowly entering “You can’t cut that guy” territory. Basically, he is good enough to be on your dynasty squad, and you can always talk yourself into holding him with the hopes he develops, but you know the odds are stacked against him after two lackluster years in the league. Through two seasons, he is averaging just 3.9 targets per game and is already on his second team. Historically, that is not a recipe for long-term success in dynasty land.

24958.blurb: The signs were there in Year 1 that Maye was likely going to be a good starter in this league, but what he did in Year 2 was amazing. He was barely edged out by Matthew Stafford for league MVP, but in any other season, Maye easily could have taken home that award. He led the league in EPA per play and completion percentage while finishing inside the top-five at the position in fantasy points per drop back, which is pretty insane considering his porous offensive line and a middling pass-catching group. Add A.J. Brown to the mix and we are still bullish on the young superstar. Through 28 full games in his career, he is averaging 31 rushing yards per game, which gives him a weekly floor to fini
24958.dyn: Still only 23 years old, Maye is now firmly locked in as a top-tier dynasty QB for years to come, thanks to his fantasy-friendly skill set. He sports the fourth-highest pass success rate of any QB through their 1st 2 years in the NFL behind only Mahomes, Purdy, and Marino.

24964.blurb: With the addition of DJ Moore and the drafting of Skyler Bell, he falls further and further down the depth chart. The man can’t separate, and he shouldn’t be considered in redraft this year - even with Josh Allen throwing the ball.
24964.dyn: Any hope we had for Coleman to become the WR1 in Buffalo has pretty much disintegrated, even though apparently, GM Brandon Beane rejected four trade offers for Coleman in the offseason. If he is on your roster, feel free to accept the offer if it comes across your desk.

24967.blurb: While the majority of 2025 fantasy RBs stayed healthy, Irving dealt with foot and shoulder injuries, limiting him to just 10 games. He was extremely ineffective, ranking 51st in rush success rate and 47th in explosive rush rate among 55 qualifying RBs. The Buccaneers also failed to give him a single carry inside the 5-yard line all season! We still believe in the talent, but Irving is shaping up to be one of the bigger wildcard picks in the early rounds. Kenneth Gainwell will certainly steal passing downs work, and Sean Tucker was re-signed to be the Bucs’ red-zone hammer. If you still are bullish on Bucky, shoot your shot as your team’s RB2 in hopes the entire offense resets in 2026.
24967.dyn: From Day 3 pick to dynasty darling, Bucky’s rough 2025 campaign can be chalked up to injuries, a new play-caller, and a spell of unfortunate TD luck. We have him firmly ranked as a high-end RB2 in dynasty startups, given his age (24 years old) and the game-breaking talent he displayed as a rookie.

24971.blurb: After spending his rookie year in Denver, the one known as “Estime Lauder” found his way on the Saints roster and willed his way to two top-15 finishes in the final two weeks of the season. Before you get too excited, realize the entire Saints backfield depth chart was on injured reserve. Free agent signing Travis Etienne Jr. will be the bell-cow while Estimé occasionally mixes in for a handful of carries.
24971.dyn: He is the definition of a BBB- a big-bodied back. However, unless your dynasty roster has a specific BBB slot, you can drop the underwhelming back.

24973.blurb: Heyyyyy, it’s Franklin. If just that drop is all we ever get from Franklin in this silly game we play, we will take it. Unfortunately, that might be the case after the Broncos took Pat Bryant on Day 2 last year, then traded for Jaylen Waddle this offseason. We expect him to be part of Sean Payton’s never-ending WR committee. Aside from injuries to Sutton and Waddle, we can’t recommend putting our beloved Troy into your fantasy lineup at this time.
24973.dyn: Franklin’s short-term dynasty hopes went straight into the commode when Denver sent the 30th overall pick to Miami for Jaylen Waddle. In deep leagues, you can stash him, as he quietly earned over 100 targets in his second season for an 18% share.

24974.blurb: Alright, Marv. Listen up, buddy. It is make-up or break-up time. We have defended you on our show for a couple of seasons, and Mike even wrote a song about the pants store in your honor! Fantasy gamers were hoping for that classic Year 2 breakout a season ago, but it was anything but. Marv had another lackluster season, with this one defined by inconsistency and injuries that limited him to just 12 games. Through two seasons, he is averaging just 9.3 fantasy points per game. As the former fourth-overall pick, that is just not good enough. The QB room remains a giant question mark, and Trey McBride is the alpha here. Unfortunately, we are at a point where Marv has settled into a boom/bust fan
24974.dyn: Based on our studies, most WRs who become difference makers do so by Year 3. If you took Marv with the first overall pick in your rookie draft two seasons ago, it is important to reset your expectations. Through two years, he averaged 1.74 and 1.68 yards per route run. Those are solid efficiency marks, but they are middling for a former top-five overall pick. If Marv can’t break out this year, he is probably settling into WR3ville for fantasy.

24977.blurb: Last season was a rollercoaster for Rome Odunze. It feels like forever ago, but remember when Rome was THE WR1 in the first month of the season? The guy was on fire to open the year, but after the team’s bye, he regressed and then got injured, missing Weeks 14-18 with a foot injury. Now entering 2026, there is perhaps a buying window in fantasy as the market is hot and heavy for Luther Burden and Colston Loveland. This is still a former top-10 draft pick, and he is guaranteed to play in 2WR sets for one of the best play-callers in the league. Burden and Loveland feel like the more exciting fantasy picks in Chicago, but Rome outscoring both of those guys is in the range of outcomes.
24977.dyn: The shine on Odunze feels like it has worn off in dynasty formats. When he came out, he was selected as a top-3 rookie pick and then was a trendy Year 2 breakout candidate entering last season. It looked like he put it all together in the first month of the season, but injuries certainly derailed his 2025 season. There is a chance the manager in your league is a bit frustrated, making him an interesting trade target heading into 2026.

24978.blurb: The former fourth-round pick is two years into his NFL career, accumulating seven total receptions in 21 games played. He shockingly turned four of them into TDs, but with the arrival of rookie Ja’Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt, consider him toast.
24978.dyn: Walker is droppable in dynasty formats. That is all.

24980.blurb: After a steady rookie season backing up James Cook, Davis saw his usage curiously cut in half last year, averaging just 15% of the snaps and just four touches per game despite dressing for all 17 regular-season games. He is nothing more than an insurance policy for Cook managers as he fights for playing time alongside third-down back Ty Johnson.
24980.dyn: Entering Year 3, Davis has a tough path to carving out any fantasy relevance. His early down skillset is directly blocked by Cook and Buffalo’s true goal-line back, Josh Allen. If Cook were to miss time, we would assume Davis would be the heir apparent to being the lead back in this Buffalo rushing attack.

24985.blurb: We are a pro-Sinnott pod here, and we are holding on to a wing and a prayer. We loved the draft capital of the second round in 2024, but since joining the league, he has 18 total targets. But, hey… he caught 16 of them! The departure of Zach Ertz piqued our interest again, only to have it smushed like a bug with the signing of Chig Okonkwo. The ultra-athletic Sinnott should sadly not be anywhere near your redraft radar.
24985.dyn: All the tea leaves pointed to a potential breakout ala Trey McBride with Zach Ertz and his injury, but it never materialized. Now, with the addition of Chig, any dynasty dream we had of Sinnott being a thing is all but gone. You can cut him and collect your tears if needed.

24989.blurb: Horton got some buzz in camp last summer but ultimately missed the majority of the season because of a shin injury. After the team traded for Rashid Shaheed and then signed him to a new deal in free agency, Horton is just a part-time role player for the Super Bowl champs.
24989.dyn: Cooper Kupp is now 33 years old, and Horton was an interesting prospect coming out of Colorado State. The last time we saw him on a field, he put up 4/48/2 in Week 9 against the Commanders before groin and shin injuries cut his rookie season short. Don’t bail just yet!

24994.blurb: The Cardinals selected Beck in the third round, making him the third QB taken in the draft. His experience (43 college starts) certainly helped his cause after the team brought him in for a top-30 visit. He can get the ball out quickly on 3-step drops and hit his receivers in stride in zone coverage. His arm strength is subpar, but it should not shock anyone if Beck ends up finishing the season as the Cardinals' starting QB on a team destined for a top-5 pick.
24994.dyn: It feels like Beck has been part of the college football conversation for a while as the backup on Georgia’s two-time National Championship teams before being the starter for 2023 & 2024. The weapons surrounding him are certainly intriguing, so take a swing at Beck in the third round of your rookie drafts. He might quickly return to irrelevance if Arizona takes a QB in 2027.
24994.rb: The Cardinals selected Beck in the third round, making him the third QB taken in the draft. His experience (43 college starts) certainly helped his cause after the team brought him in for a top-30 visit. He can get the ball out quickly on 3-step drops and hit his receivers in stride in zone coverage. His arm strength is subpar, but it should not shock anyone if Beck ends up finishing the season as the Cardinals' starting QB on a team destined for a top-5 pick.

25003.blurb: Legette lost his WR2 job last year to Jalen Coker, and we are projecting that to stick in 2026. Tetairoa McMillan should dominate the target share here, and Coker is a fine WR2 option for the team. Call us crazy, but we are not drafting Bryce Young’s WR3, especially after he saw four or fewer targets in eight of his final 10 games to close 2025.
25003.dyn: This man’s accent is fun, and he is a good time. That is about where the positives end for Legette’s dynasty outlook. Through two seasons, he is averaging 1.11 YPRR. I think we all know where this is headed…

25039.blurb: Pittsburgh took Roman Wilson in the third round back in 2024, and after struggling to stay healthy in Year 1, he was just a part time player in 2025. Hey, to his credit, he did finish as the WR8 in Week 8 against the Packers, so he’s got that going for him. #NeverForget. He is likely to be a part-time player again in 2026, who is stuck behind Pitty City, Metcalf, and second-round rookie Germie Bernard.
25039.dyn: There are hundreds of players you once took in the second or third round of a rookie draft who never went on to do anything in the league. Mr. Wilson is on that list, sadly. If he is still on your dynasty squad, take some advice from Michael Jordan: “Stop it. Get some help.”

25064.blurb: Davis is an explosive backup RB who averaged 5.5 yards per carry through two seasons, albeit on just 73 total attempts. He was also electric in the passing game, but averaged just 29% of the snaps behind Breece Hall. New OC Frank Reich and HC Aaron Glenn have toiled with the idea of a committee approach, but the contract extension and talent of Hall suggest otherwise. Expect a handful of touches per game but zero fantasy relevance to start the season.
25064.dyn: The 24-year-old Davis enters Year 3 stuck behind Breece Hall, competing for bread crumbs alongside Braelon Allen. He sadly ended up on the wrong NFL team to make significant fantasy noise. For dynasty purposes, he is barely holding a bench spot, even in the deepest of leagues.

25069.blurb: Nix disappointed in a sophomore season where he led the NFL in pass attempts and the Broncos were the AFC's No. 1 seed. Apart from three monster games, he was relatively uninspiring as a fantasy starter, including six weeks scoring below 15 fantasy points. Despite having one of the best offensive lines in the business, he tied Shedeur Sanders and J.J. McCarthy for lowest yards per pass attempt when pressured. We still are in on Nix for fantasy with the arrival of Jaylen Waddle and an off season of recovering from his brutal ankle injury. Consider pairing him with another late-round QB as you see how he responds as a runner in the first month of the season.
25069.dyn: We have Nix ranked outside the top-12 of dynasty QBs, but others in your league might still think he is a top-10 guy. Only 26 years old, he is a hold but will likely settle into the low-end QB1/high-end QB2 guy, a far cry from the hoopla after last off-season.

25079.blurb: Vidal Sassoon! To this man’s credit, he went from being inactive in the first few games behind Omarion Hampton and Najee Harris to becoming one of the more valuable adds off the waiver wire in 2025. After Harris went down for the season and Hampton suffered a serious ankle injury, Vidal stepped in as the lead back and finished as a top-24 fantasy RB in five of eight games where he played 60+ percent of the snaps. It is nice to know that if the opportunity arises, he is fully capable of handling 15+ touches as a plug-and-play option. Of course, we are not projecting much workload with Omarion Hampton atop the depth chart and Keaton Mitchell joining the squad in free agency, so he is not worth
25079.dyn: Vidal is back in LA on a one-year deal as a restricted free agent, so it remains to be seen where he will play in 2027. Regardless, he is a fine player to put at the end of your bench, but you are obviously not counting on him for any production or long-term value.

25092.blurb: The former college WR was a nice story as a fifth-round pick in 2024 who certainly asserted himself as the most effective RB on a bad Giants team. Fast forward a year, and he was usurped by Cam Skattebo before his season-ending injury. From Week 7 on, Tracy saw a respectable 16.7 opportunities per game and averaged 80+ yards per game. He certainly is capable of being a fantasy-friendly asset thanks to his pass-catching abilities, but we project him to firmly be the RB2 behind Skattebo. In the later rounds of your drafts, we do not mind adding Tracy to your bench if you think they lean on him at the beginning of the year as Skatt ramps up.
25092.dyn: A tale as old as time: young RB drafted on Day 3 has a hot streak, and then dynasty managers elevate him higher than they should. Tracy was a nice story for the woeful 2024 Giants, but it is clear he was never the long-term answer for this roster or in dynasty. RBs with this type of investment at the NFL level are expendable and easily replaced.

25097.blurb: We love us some Ladd, but his sophomore season was a relative disappointment, regressing in every major statistical category compared to his WR11 finish as a rookie. He particularly struggled versus zone coverage (1.31 YPRR) as a predominantly slot WR (65% of routes) while ceding meaningful targets to old man Keenan Allen. It remains to be seen if he will be consistently on the field in 2WR sets as new OC Mike McDaniel historically adds a fullback on the field to mess with WR usage. We have Ladd ranked as a solid WR3/FLEX for fantasy and the target leader for the Chargers. However, with a ton of mouths to feed, it will be hard to return to the glory of his rookie season based on receiving ef
25097.dyn: Ladd crushed as a rookie but took a step back in terms of dynasty value this past year. Quentin Johnston and Tre’ Harris will likely see a ton of snaps for blocking purposes and potentially limit some of his red zone opportunities. He enters Year 3 as a low-end WR2 who needs more receiving volume to hit a ceiling outcome moving forward.

25098.blurb: McMillan missed the first half of the year because of a serious neck injury, but when he returned, he did have a role on this team. Now with Evans gone, McMillan is entrenched as the WR3 to start the season. For now, he is probably not on the radar in drafts, but he will be a plug-and-play option off the waiver wire should Godwin or Egbuka get injured.
25098.dyn: McMillan might be one of the sneakier trade-for candidates in dynasty right now. His name doesn’t carry a ton of weight, yet whenever he has been on the field, he has been able to produce. Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka will probably be atop the pecking order this season, but Godwin’s contract has an out after the 2026 season. It is not impossible that McMillan and Egbuka are running as the top WRs in this Bucs offense as early as 2027, assuming McMillan can hold off this year’s third-round pick,

25102.blurb: Competing with Tank Bigsby for scraps at the table, Shipley had just 23 total touches on the season for 105 total yards. To put his brief two-year career in perspective, his 27% rush success rate ranks 419th among 425 qualifying RBs since 2010. Apologies if you were coming to Will Shipley’s player profile hoping for some optimism. It ain’t here, folks!
25102.dyn: Shipley is nothing but an insurance back to dangle in front of a Saquon manager. We often overvalue these backups as the fear of “what could happen” outweighs the reality of a former Day 3 RB ever making an impact in dynasty. His capable hands make him a third-down back to stash for now.

25103.blurb: Who is the WR1 for the Dolphins? And does it matter? Man, this Miami depth chart is something else. I mean, what a crew. We honestly do not feel confident in playing time or target shares here because this is a brand-new regime with brand-new weapons and a brand-new QB. The Dolphins project to be one of the most run-heavy teams in the league under a defensive-minded head coach and run-first OC Bobby Slowik. For now, Washington looks like he will have a role as the slot WR in this offense, but we have seen enough of him in the NFL to know that a low aDOT, gadgety player isn’t going to be a difference maker for fantasy, especially in an offense that could be the worst in football.
25103.dyn: Washington comes from the previous regime, and with Miami taking multiple rookies in the NFL Draft, there is a good chance Washington is on the outside looking in when we get to the end of the season. He carries next to no value in dynasty leagues. Sorry, Malik!

25106.blurb: With Noah Fant out of the picture, the TE position was up for grabs in Seattle, and Barner did a decent job showing he should be the guy moving forward. Finishing as the TE14, he had a decent 64 targets, which turned into 519 yards and six TDs. His 18 looks in the red zone were stellar too, just two fewer than JSN. He remains too volatile in redraft, especially with fellow Seahawk Elijah Arroyo still in the mix. Barner had finishes as high as TE1 and as low as TE58 last year. It would be tough to stomach the amount of Tums we would need to ride that roller coaster.
25106.dyn: Barner carries a little more weight in dynasty. He is only 24 and will be with Seattle at least through 2027, a very well-run franchise. However, the same issues exist in dynasty as they do in redraft: four targets a game are just not enough to crack your starting lineup. His seven "TE1" finishes might lure someone into this TE trap, but as we have established on the podcast, a top-12 finish at this position is an outdated term.

25122.blurb: Coker gained some steam throughout the summer last year as a potential sleeper, but he injured his quad late in camp and then missed the first six games of the season. It took a bit for him to get going, but he did end up posting four top-24 weekly finishes in his final seven games. His 2026 fantasy value will ultimately be determined by Bryce Young’s ability to support multiple weapons and whether or not this year’s rookie, Chris Brazzell, or Xavier Legette can push him for playing time. Right now, we have him as the second option in the offense. We do not mind him as a late-round stash, especially in deeper leagues.
25122.dyn: Coker was signed to a three-year extension in mid June, giving him plenty of value in dynasty formats as the likely No. 2 option opposite Tetairoa McMillan. The former UDFA is only 24 years old and has flashed some talent, making him a solid late-round pick in dynasty start-ups and a sneaky bench stash moving forward.

25124.blurb: The clear WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, Flournoy had 11 receptions for 158 yards last season in the three games that Lamb missed. He only gets a second look if Lamb and or Pickens are injured.
25124.dyn: May I offer you an almost 27-year-old WR, drafted in the sixth round, entering his third season, who is yet to break out? No?

25198.blurb: Vele goes from WR2 on the depth chart to WR3 after the Saints took Jordyn Tyson with the eighth overall pick. He is not on the radar for fantasy in the long term, but there's short term viability in deeper leagues that have multiple FLEX spots with Tyson starting the season on IR because of his hamstring injury.
25198.dyn: If you recall, Vele entered the league as an older prospect. Now entering his third season in the league, he is already 28 years old! In other words, he’s already leaving his prime. Not great, Bob!

25201.blurb: Whittington is a McVay guy through and through. Before the team’s Week 8 bye, he averaged 62% of the snaps, but the production was minimal. We have noticed that anytime Puka Nacua or Davante Adams was off the field, McVay trusts Whittington to immediately step into their every-down role, especially as a blocker. Ignore at your drafts, but do not be surprised if we hear from Whittington at some point in 2026 if the Rams WRs have the injury bug.
25201.dyn: He likely means more to the Rams than for fantasy entering Year 3. Stash if you think he can see volume if Puka or Davante went down. Drop him if you do not.

25323.blurb: The Titans took Cam Ward first overall in the 2025 NFL Draft, and this is the perfect example of what can happen to a young, talented QB in their first year in the league. No disrespect to the good folks of Nashville, but this was set up to fail from the get-go as the Titans trailed on 72% of his dropbacks, fifth highest in the NFL. He tied Geno Smith for the most sacks taken (55!) and finished with just one top-12 finish on the year, albeit against Super Bowl Champion Seattle in Week 12. The addition of Wan’Dale Robinson and fourth overall pick Carnell Tate gives him a shot at a Year 2 breakout. However, unless he starts running more, Ward will likely be left amongst a pile of other QBs you
25323.dyn: His 5.9 yards per attempt ranks 32nd among 35 first-round QBs over the last decade. Woof. For fantasy, he ranked dead last among all QBs in fantasy points per dropback - Ward is not running enough to overcome the offense’s shortcomings. However, in dynasty leagues, he will carry QB2 value as long as he has the starting job.

25868.blurb: Let’s be clear: Jeanty checks nearly every box we want in fantasy. Jeanty was actually Jason’s ‘Bust’ pick last year on the show, relative to ADP. It is not because we all didn’t love the talent and draft capital, but it is hard to be a fantasy difference maker at the RB position when your surroundings are as bad as they were a season ago. The O-line was a disaster, Pete Carroll ran a completely unserious operation, and Geno Smith regressed massively. It led to Las Vegas ranking dead last in TDs per game. Again, it is hard to be a great fantasy RB when that’s the case. Fast forward one year, and suddenly, we are more optimistic about where the Raiders are headed. Sure, Fernando Mendoza is a
25868.dyn: The only RBs above Jeanty in our consensus start-up rankings are Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson. That tells you all you need to know about Jeanty’s future in dynasty leagues. As a prospect, he was one of those rare talents with top-10 draft capital, so you can feel pretty confident you will get multiple high-end fantasy seasons from Ashton Jeanty.

25869.blurb: Oh, Mr. Loveland. Slow clap for the managers that pounced on Loveland quickly when they saw the promise of a breakout. His Week 17 performance against San Francisco was one that fantasy championships were made of. We were nervous with the myriad of weapons in Chicago and how Ben Johnson’s offense would come together, but Loveland was the clear first read in the offense into the NFL playoffs. DJ Moore has left town, and Johnson proved that what he did in Detroit was not a fluke, so ranking Loveland in the top four seems 100% valid. We cannot wait to see the jump Loveland can make this season.
25869.dyn: Loveland had at least 15% of the team’s targets in each of the final nine games in 2025, and you know we love a TE that gets better as the season progresses. Loveland is in the second tier of dynasty TEs and is either TE3 or TE4 in start-up rankings. Congratulations if he is on your squad, and enjoy the ride with one of the youngest and most valuable players at the position.

tags.breakout: What else is there to say about Mr. Lovelaaaand? He finished the 2025 season with 82 targets and was on an upward trajectory. The final two weeks of the regular season gave us a glimpse at what he could be moving forward - 10 and 13 targets, close to 100 yards receiving each game, and each with a receiving TD. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Chicago, but Loveland proved his trustworthiness in the playoffs, as Caleb Williams went to him in the biggest moments. If Caleb can complete just a few more passes, we are looking at a bump in Loveland’s production. With TEs, we are great or late over here at Ballers HQ, and the difference in ADP between the McBride/Bowers duo and Loveland is significant enough to set him up as a potential value in a breakout season.

25870.blurb: We were uncertain about how it would all play out in the TE room with David Njoku still the de facto TE1, but Fannin came out of the gate hard in 2025. He was the bright spot in Cleveland last season, leading the team in targets (107), receptions (72), receiving yards (731), and receiving TDs (six) all as a rookie with a carousel of QBs throwing him the ball. The offense in Cleveland was abhorrent, but Fannin still managed to join Sam LaPorta as one of two rookie TEs since 2000 with 70/700/6. He now has to compete with rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston for targets, but the offense on the whole looks to have much more potential with Todd Monken driving the bus. He finished as the TE5 in
25870.dyn: Njoku was released by the Browns in March, clearing the way for Fannin to be their TE1 of the future on a team that looks poised to steadily improve. He is a top-5 dynasty TE, in the bottom of the second tier, just below Colston Loveland, and Tyler Warren. If you drafted him in your rookie drafts in 2025, congratulations on quite a value.

tags.breakout: Fannin exploded in the second half of 2025, as he was the TE12 or better in four out of the final five weeks he played - including a TE1 and a TE2 finish! Look, the QB situation in Cleveland is still murky at best, but there is even more opportunity for Fannin with the departure of David Njoku. He leaves behind 48 targets, and we know that even a bad offense can give us fantasy gold - he was targeted 12 times in the red zone, more than any WR on the team. The team did add rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, but we see a world where Fannin meets or exceeds his 21.4% target share.

25874.blurb: The beginning of the year was an utter delight for Warren as he produced just one fantasy finish outside the top-12 in the first seven weeks, thanks to the resurgence of Daniel Jones. He struggled near the end of the year, along with the rest of the Colts’ offense, but still posted 817 yards receiving and a TE7 finish on the year. The four receiving TDs felt on the lower side, but this could go up with the loss of Michael Pittman Jr. in 2026. Warren was the TE3 when it came to route participation at 83%, and we don’t see that going down any time soon. He is in that second tier of TEs in redraft that can be fantasy difference-makers even with the uncertain recovery timeline of Jones.
25874.dyn: Anyone who went all-in on Tyler Warren last year is extremely thankful and confident that they have their TE position locked up for a good while. His 21% target share should stay consistent as he will be the cornerstone of the Colts’ passing attack for seasons to come. Enjoy!

25876.blurb: Fifth-round draft pick Gadsden broke all the Chargers' rookie TE records last year as he finished with 49 receptions on 69 targets, 664 yards receiving, and three TDs. However, keep in mind that 241 of those yards came in two weeks. It was looking like the potential was high for 2026 with the addition of OC Mike McDaniel, but then the team had to go and sign David Njoku. Throw in blocking TE Charlie Kolar and FB Alec Ingold, and Gadsden’s path to fantasy relevance in redraft this year has gotten circuitous at best. Despite the alluring upside, 2026 feels like a tough route for Gadsden to be counted on in fantasy and likely someone overdrafted in your leagues.
25876.dyn: We were all certain we had hit fantasy gold in dynasty when Gadsden posted TE1 and TE4 finishes in back-to-back weeks last season. Alas, we flew too close to the sun as he dropped back to Earth faster than a paper straw in a milkshake. The team added David Njoku, but the silver lining is that he only signed a one-year deal, and it could easily be a one-and-done. Gadsden represents an intriguing buy-low opportunity for a team that won’t be depending on him for at least a year.

tags.bust: After he burst onto the scene with a monster 4-game stretch as a rookie, Oronde Gadsden II has slowly faded away from fantasy relevance. While touting a young TE can be tempting, the arrival of Mike McDaniel and multiple TEs in free agency shifted much of the optimism. On Sleeper's platform, he looks like a glaring overdraft candidate. The Chargers have reimagined their offensive philosophy and Gadsden has not been consistently working with the starters throughout camp. Let someone else in your league take a shot as there are many other young, athletic TEs we would rather bet on.

25886.blurb: With an early breakout age (20) and 25 rushing TDs over his final two seasons, he was the engine of the Huskies offense post-Michael Penix Jr. years. Coleman’s draft stock slipped after a lack of testing, but the landing spot in Denver should put him on your radar. Sean Payton loves utilizing an RB committee more than his own family, as Coleman begins the season third or fourth on the RB depth chart. Keep your head on a swivel, knowing Coleman could have a moment as a priority waiver pickup.
25886.dyn: Coleman is built low to the ground, and his receiving profile (87 career receptions) showcases the type of three-down skillset we are willing to chase for fantasy. He is a fringe first-round rookie pick, albeit in an extremely weak RB class.
25886.rb: With an early breakout age (20) and 25 rushing TDs over his final two seasons, he was the engine of the Huskies offense post-Michael Penix Jr. years. Coleman’s draft stock slipped after a lack of testing, but the landing spot in Denver should put him on your radar. Sean Payton loves utilizing an RB committee more than his own family, as Coleman begins the season third or fourth on the RB depth chart. Keep your head on a swivel, knowing Coleman could have a moment as a priority waiver pickup.

25887.blurb: How good was the Skatt man for the 10 weeks of the season? He was the RB10, averaging 14.5 fantasy points per game, including a month’s stretch where the Giants fed him the ball 22+ times a game. His gruesome ankle fracture was tough to watch, as his energy and enthusiasm made him one of our favorite players to watch in 2025. He came out saying he would be ready for Week 1, but we would expect his best football to be played in the back half of the season, as it may take time to regain his explosiveness and dynamic ability. Consider him an RB2 for your fantasy squads on a run-heavy Giants team with an improved offensive line and a new scheme.
25887.dyn: Before going down to injury, he ripped off six straight top-24 weekly finishes among RBs, so he clearly has the skillset to succeed in the game we play. That said, whenever there is a regime change, the dynasty value for Day 3 RBs is always a bit murky. For now, he is the clear best fantasy option in the backfield and a mid-RB2 in our startup rankings.

tags.value: Is he a little crazy? Sure, but we like that from our fantasy RBs and it seems like Skatt is still being punished too much for last season's injury as he looks like a great value according to our Value Scout tool. He should handle a three-down workload and operate as the clear goal-line back on a Giants team we like to take a step forward in 2026. Consider him a strong RB2 with the type of high-end ceiling to finish as a top 10 back.

25888.blurb: The sixth-round pick in 2025 barely sniffed the field for the first three months of the season behind veteran Alvin Kamara. However, he was called upon for a three-week stretch (Weeks 12-14) when he averaged 17 opportunities per game before missing the final two weeks of the season due to an injury. Perhaps he can carve out a role as the RB2 behind Etienne as the insurance back, but he is best left on waivers to start the year.
25888.dyn: Consider him the “Anthony Mackie” of Avengers actors: he’s fine, but when you give him a leading role, you are left asking why anyone greenlit this as a good idea. Neal was an all-around back at Kansas who didn’t exactly overpower people as a runner. With Etienne inked to a big free agent deal, he is relegated to being a middling backup.

25889.blurb: The second RB taken by the Browns in last year’s draft had a weird rookie campaign. Sampson surprisingly had eight receptions in Week 1 and totaled 40 targets as a change-of-pace back. Yet, he averaged just 2.7 yards per carry and failed to score on the ground. The Browns’ offense will receive a makeover in 2026 with new play-caller Todd Monken and an influx of new receivers. Once lead back Quinshon Judkins returns from his ankle injury, Sampson likely will fade to being a bench stash only in deep PPR leagues.
25889.dyn: Sampson likely does not have standalone value but is an intriguing bench stash at only 21 years old. The former SEC Offensive Player of the Year has the pass-catching skills to hang around and make noise if Judkins were to get injured again.

25892.blurb: There are talks of Sarratt moving into the ‘Big Slot’ role in Year 1 in Baltimore, which is kind of intriguing in deep formats. Sarratt is a ball winner who was frequently used in the red zone in college, giving him life as a contributor right away as a rookie in Baltimore. That said, we expect Flowers and Bateman to open the season as the top WRs on the depth chart, and the Ravens have never had a high pass rate in the Lamar Jackson era, so the path for fantasy is pretty thin out of the gate. He is not on the radar right now as a redraft target, but know the name for the waiver wire in the event Flowers or Bateman miss time due to injury.
25892.dyn: Baltimore double-dipped in the NFL Draft, taking Ja’Kobi Lane in Round 3, then Sarratt in Round 4. Even though the Ravens took Lane first, you could argue Sarratt is the better prospect for the game we play. Not only did he catch 15 TDs for the National Champion Hoosiers, but he also had a 2.56 career yards per route run rate and was second in the entire class behind only Makai Lemon in first downs per route run.
25892.rb: There are talks of Sarratt moving into the ‘Big Slot’ role in Year 1 in Baltimore, which is kind of intriguing in deep formats. Sarratt is a ball winner who was frequently used in the red zone in college, giving him life as a contributor right away as a rookie in Baltimore. That said, we expect Flowers and Bateman to open the season as the top WRs on the depth chart, and the Ravens have never had a high pass rate in the Lamar Jackson era, so the path for fantasy is pretty thin out of the gate. He is not on the radar right now as a redraft target, but know the name for the waiver wire in the event Flowers or Bateman miss time due to injury.

25894.blurb: The Bech hive was down bad last year after the Raiders took him in the second round of the NFL Draft, and he totaled just 20 receptions on the season.  He absolutely whiffed as a rookie with numbers so poor (37% snaps, 1.26 YPRR) you would bury your head in the sand if you ever publicly championed him. The Vegas WR room is begging for someone to step up alongside Brock Bowers, so perhaps he can see a jump in usage and target share in Year 2. We are rooting for Bech to make an impact, but he is nothing more than a late-round lottery ticket in redraft leagues.
25894.dyn: A dynasty favorite of ours, never let the government suppress the fact that Bech (as a freshman TE/WR) led the 2021 LSU Tigers in receptions ahead of Malik Nabers and Brian Thomas Jr. He is holding a spot at the end of dynasty benches as 2026 feels like a make-or-break year.

25898.blurb: Despite playing behind Travis Etienne Jr., the fourth-round pick finished fifth in rush success rate and 11th in forced missed tackle rate among 55 qualifying RBs. He was also much better inside the 10-yard line than Etienne, converting his eight rush attempts into five scores compared to 26 and only four. He profiled as a tackle-breaker coming out of college and now has a chance to be the lead back on an offense we like after Travis Etienne signed in New Orleans. We can see him return RB2 fantasy value on an offense we want pieces from for our rosters.
25898.dyn: Tuten was one of our “trade-for” targets all off-season, and he escaped the NFL Draft without much competition. The Jags did sign Chris Rodriguez Jr. in free agency, which does add some uncertainty here, but we are betting on Tuten to emerge as the RB1 for Liam Coen.

tags.breakout: Tuten spent the majority of 2025 bottled up behind Travis Etienne Jr., with only a 25% rushing share to Etienne’s 70%. That said, Tuten was efficient with his scoring when he got the opportunity. He turned his seven attempts inside the 5-yard line into five TDs, whereas Etienne was nowhere as successful, only cashing in twice on 12 attempts. With Etienne off to New Orleans, Tuten gets the keys to the Jag(uars), and he is getting overlooked in drafts as a potential RB1. We see the Jacksonville offense as one to target in 2026, and a team that had 22 rushing TDs in 2025 (tied for the fourth-most) will need to hand the ball off to someone. With CROD (Chris Rodriguez Jr.) and LeQuint Allen Jr. rounding out the depth chart, our money is on Tuten to be that guy.

25899.blurb: The seventh-round pick from 2025 was a trendy sleeper pick last year, as fantasy managers cited “well, Isaiah Pacheco was a seventh-round pick too!” Smith was sparingly used all season, touching the ball 79 total times despite the uninspiring play of veterans Kareem Hunt and Pacheco. With Kenneth Walker III now aboard, he is back to being a rotational back with little path forward in fantasy.
25899.dyn: Welp, there goes his window in dynasty. The former WR turned RB tantalized with his production profile and speed (4.39 40-time), but is barely holding value as a bench player. Do not feel the need to roster him apart from the deepest of PPR leagues.

25900.blurb: The former fifth-round pick is the presumed backup to Jonathan Taylor in Indy. However, we confess that his rookie season does not give us a ton of information to work from, as he touched the ball 26 total times and was active in three total games from Week 8 on. He is an explosive athlete with the opportunity to lock up the RB2 spot. For now, know the name, but the JTT manager should not feel obligated to draft him even as insurance.
25900.dyn: The size (6’0”, 212 lbs.) and speed combo (4.43 40-time) made Giddens an intriguing dynasty name a year ago. If Taylor were to go down, he could vault into being an every-down guy, but that remains mere speculation. In the words of Cosmo Kramer, “Giddy Up,” DJ!

25903.blurb: Wait, we are mentioning a former fifth-round RB who was on the field for three total offensive snaps in 2025? The San Francisco backfield annually gives us relevant fantasy backup RBs who seemingly come out of nowhere: Raheem Mostert, Jeff Wilson Jr., Eli Mitchell, and Jordan Mason ring a bell? The 49ers beat reporters seem to suggest James could enter the mix for the backup role behind Christian McCaffrey this year, despite having as many career regular-season carries as your grandmother. Know the name and be willing to draft him as CMC insurance if you want to be cautious.
25903.dyn: The former Oregon back did see some mop-up action in the 49ers’ NFC divisional blowout loss to Seattle. His final year production in college of nearly 1,500 total yards and 0.45 yards per team attempt was solid. Hopefully, you picked him up off your waiver wire earlier this offseason in hopes you have the San Fran RB2.

25912.blurb: The 3rd round pick was barely involved as a rookie and now with the arrival of A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, he looks very unlikely to be a fantasy asset in 2026. Sorry Williams truthers but a 4% target share as a rookie is not going to get it done.
25912.dyn: We kind of liked Williams as a fun prospect last year, but as things go in dynasty land, there are way more misses than hits. Unless Williams does a 180 in Year 2, it is bleak, folks. He caught just 10 passes as a rookie despite appearing in all 17 games. Ew.

25914.blurb: Houston double-dipped in the 2025 NFL Draft on Day 2, taking both Iowa State WR prospects. They grabbed Jayden Higgins in Round 2 and Noel in Round 3, and neither guy really stepped up for fantasy on a consistent basis. Noel was stuck behind Christian Kirk for the slot role last year, but with Kirk gone and Jayden Higgins out for the year, he has a chance to win that slot role.
25914.dyn: Noel is a fine stash right now until we see if he can make a jump in Year 2. It is a small sample size, but the efficiency marks aren’t terrible (1.50 YPRR, 8.3 YPT) for a former Day 2 pick.

25922.blurb: Golden’s rookie season was obviously not great. He finished with just 29 total catches and failed to haul in a single TD reception until the NFL playoffs. He now finds himself on a scary trajectory entering Year 2. Historically, WRs with poor efficiency in their rookie season who post virtually zero production have flopped more often than not in the NFL. That doesn’t mean it cannot work for Golden; probability is just not on his side. That said, the Packers are absolutely counting on him after they traded Dontayvion Wicks to the Eagles and let Romeo Doubs walk in free agency. Consider Golden a complete wild card entering 2026.
25922.dyn: After a forgettable rookie campaign, Matthew Golden’s dynasty value hangs in the balance. He had plenty of red flags in his production profile coming out of college, and then in Year 1, he averaged just 1.35 yards per route run as a part-time player. Entering his second season, odds are stacked against Golden, but the opportunity is certainly there, and the Packers invested a first-round pick in him just a year ago. If he flops again in Year 2, it is probably not going to happen, but the market

25925.blurb: The second-round pick appeared in all 17 games as a rookie but saw just a 7% target share as an afterthought in the offense. In fact, Harris failed to finish inside the top-36 WRs in a single week. His value to the Chargers might be more important to real-life football than fantasy, as this team has multiple other options commanding targets ahead of him.
