If Ladd McConkey or Quentin Johnston were to miss time, we would be interested in adding Harris as a speculative waiver wire add.
25925.dyn: It is no surprise that Cleveland Joseph Harris III was a Ballers favorite after he was taken 55th(!) overall following an unreal final season at Ole Miss. After a mostly forgetful rookie campaign, consider him dynasty bench material with a tough path forward for fantasy relevance.

25934.blurb: Tiny Tez! This guy flashed when his number was called in 2025, as Mike Evans and Chris Godwin missed a bunch of time last season. Unfortunately, unless you are an outlier, former seventh-round picks who weigh 165 pounds don’t usually go on to be fantasy stars. Tampa probably views him as a depth piece behind Egbuka, Godwin, McMillan, and Ted Hurst.
25934.dyn: Tez Johnson actually had a really solid production profile coming out of Oregon, and you saw in his rookie year that he belongs in the league. That doesn’t necessarily mean he is worth a roster spot in dynasty, as he is buried on the depth chart.

25935.blurb: The Giants traded multiple picks to land Notre Dame’s Malachi Fields, so the new staff likely has a role in mind for him. At 6’5” and 218 pounds, he is a true X receiver. Unfortunately, for fantasy, Fields looks like a guy who is more likely to help the Giants than help our fantasy teams, as he is a pretty weak prospect coming out of Notre Dame. We know Malik Nabers is the alpha when healthy, and the team paid big money to Isaiah Likely in free agency. We would be surprised if he is able to generate enough volume to matter for fantasy, but he could have some TD upside in the right matchups thanks to his power forward frame.
25935.dyn: Analytically, Fields doesn’t have a lot going for him in terms of numbers. He is an older prospect who specializes as a field stretcher and contested catch target. Generally speaking, those profiles haven’t really hit for dynasty, but with Wan’Dale Robinson gone and Darius Slayton likely not around for much longer, the landing spot says we need to keep the light on over the next 1-2 years, as he could be the second option across from Malik Nabers.
25935.rb: The Giants traded multiple picks to land Notre Dame’s Malachi Fields, so the new staff likely has a role in mind for him. At 6’5” and 218 pounds, he is a true X receiver. Unfortunately, for fantasy, Fields looks like a guy who is more likely to help the Giants than help our fantasy teams, as he is a pretty weak prospect coming out of Notre Dame. We know Malik Nabers is the alpha when healthy, and the team paid big money to Isaiah Likely in free agency. We would be surprised if he is able to generate enough volume to matter for fantasy, but he could have some TD upside in the right matchups thanks to his power forward frame.

25939.blurb: Nicknamed "the Fatman" by his mother, Allen came into Penn State as a highly regarded recruit and got to work in the gym. He checks a lot of the physical profile boxes we want at the next level, and finished his college career as Penn State's all-time leader in rush attempts and rushing yards. The question is whether his lack of flash and creativity as a runner will cap him at the next level. He likely begins third or fourth on the Washington depth chart.
25939.dyn: While playing alongside Nicholas Singleton, he certainly was able to handle a heavy workload, and his final three-game run (72 carries for 567 yards and five rushing TDs) put an exclamation point on a stellar career. His patient, no-nonsense style will win over coaches, but as an older prospect, it is tough pounding the table for him despite being in a subpar RB draft class.
25939.rb: Nicknamed "the Fatman" by his mother, Allen came into Penn State as a highly regarded recruit and got to work in the gym. He checks a lot of the physical profile boxes we want at the next level, and finished his college career as Penn State's all-time leader in rush attempts and rushing yards. The question is whether his lack of flash and creativity as a runner will cap him at the next level. He likely begins third or fourth on the Washington depth chart.

25942.blurb: After being taken in the fourth round in 2025, Marks saw 17 opportunities per game from Week 7 on. The Texans obviously were not very impressed with the efficiency (3.5 yards per carry) and forced missed tackle rate (54th out of 55 qualifying RBs), leading them to trade for veteran David Montgomery. He returns to being a backup and insurance back option only.
25942.dyn: His parents know him as Jo'Quavious Dequane Marks, but “Woody” will play for the NFL. He has a three-down skill set, but honestly, there is not much special to his game that would cause you to be bullish for dynasty purposes.

25944.blurb: It was a slow start for the second-round rookie as he averaged just 8.5 opportunities per game behind J.K. Dobbins through the first ten weeks of the season. However, after Dobbins went down with yet another season-ending injury, Harvey averaged 18.4 opportunities, 17 fantasy points per game, and finished the season with 12 total TDs. Those scores might be propping him up in fantasy managers’ minds despite the fact that his efficiency marks were less than stellar as a runner. Sean Payton seems committed to a RB committee, bringing back J.K. Dobbins while adding fourth- round pick Jonah Coleman. Harvey is in FLEX territory, but he might be maddening as a start/sit decision every week.
25944.dyn: Harvey’s value was a roller coaster this off-season after Denver’s 14-win season, his second-half performance, and then the re-signing of J.K. Dobbins. He did see 58 targets (tied for the fifth most among Day 2 RBs over the last decade), giving you hope that his value will hold in full PPR leagues. Nevertheless, he likely saw his value peak already in dynasty.

tags.bust: Harvey’s fantasy production was solid in 2025, especially for a rookie. However, most of that production was unsustainable as he was fortunate in the TD department, finding the end zone 12 times. With J.K. Dobbins back on the roster and the Broncos selecting Jonah Coleman in the NFL Draft, Harvey is likely to remain as part of a committee, which means he will need to rely on efficiency to get the job done in fantasy. That is where the concerns come in. Harvey ranked 46th out of 48 qualified backs in rushing yards over expected per attempt; he was 32nd in success rate, and he averaged a pedestrian 3.7 yards per carry despite playing behind one of the best lines in football. We would like to be optimistic about a Year 2 breakout, but the warning signs are there in a crowded offense that just added another mouth to feed in Jaylen Waddle.

25946.blurb: Judkins was everything the Browns envisioned when they selected him 34th overall in last year’s draft. Despite the team’s lack of success, he was a workhorse, averaging 18.3 touches per game and 34% of the team's total rush attempts and targets before a brutal dislocated ankle and fractured fibula ended his season in Week 16. He has a chance to be cleared for Week 1, though he will not be 100% when the season begins. Expect his production to pick up in the second half of the season, making him an awkward selection in the middle rounds of your draft.
25946.dyn: He is expected to make a full recovery for the 2026 season and should be viewed as a top-12 dynasty RB even on a bad football team. He has the size and three-down skillset to be an elite performer for the next handful of years.

25948.blurb: Travis’ little brother was a fourth-rounder out of Georgia last year who touched the ball only 23 times as a rookie. He will compete with Jonathon Brooks for touches behind Chuba Hubbard. That is fantasy football code for: he is probably irrelevant.
25948.dyn: Oh, you are looking for Trevor (“Aychane”) Etienne dynasty advice?! He was a middling prospect stuck in depth chart purgatory in Carolina. If his name were “Donald McDonaldson,” you would probably think twice, but the family name subconsciously gives him a boost that maybe he could work in fantasy football.

25949.blurb: Taken in the sixth round in 2025, there were rumblings that Brooks could win the backup job behind Chase Brown. (Narrator: but he did not.) The Day 3 pick touched the ball 17 total times as a rookie, and old man Samaje Perine is back again in 2026 as the trusted third-down back the Bengals mix in.
25949.dyn: Brooks is an end-of-bench lottery ticket that likely will be thrown in the trash very soon.

25952.blurb: The seventh-round Monangai was a revelation, tag-teaming with Swift as the Bears posted the sixth-most total rushing yards in the league. Monangai was a machine, gaining 5+ yards on 42.6% of his carries, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only Kyren Williams. He certainly has juice with the upside to see a big workload if Swift went down, as evidenced by a Week 9 game where Ben Johnson turned full sicko, feeding Monangai the ball 31(!) times. Consider Monangai a “FLEX with benefits” later in your draft.
25952.dyn: It is tough to gauge Monangai’s long-term value as his draft capital suggests this team could draft a high-end back in 2027 once Swift is a free agent. For now, he sits inside our top-36 RBs in startups, knowing there is volatility moving forward.

25953.blurb: The 6’2” bruiser saw limited work as a rookie, averaging an utterly disgusting 2.8 yards per carry on 70 total carries. Sounds bad, right? What if we told you that was the WORST per carry average of any rookie RB over the last decade? Seriously, 99 different rookie RBs since 2016 saw 70+ carries, and Ollie was the worst. It was quite the dubious distinction. Are you curious who the best rookie was in that span? (Seriously, since you are here wanting Ollie Gordon II takes, we might as well keep this thing rolling.) It was some guy named De’Von Achane who averaged five MORE yards per carry (7.8) than Ollie did. His sixth-round draft capital, Achane’s insane talent, and the Dolphins' projected
25953.dyn: Remember when Gordon was a sophomore sensation at Oklahoma State? His name value keeps him afloat, but as a backup RB on arguably the worst roster in the NFL, what are we going for here, folks? Are you sincerely hoping for an Achane injury? You sick, sick person. Leave. Now!

25956.blurb: It was a frustrating rookie season for Omarion Hampton, who missed Weeks 6-13 with a small fracture in his ankle. However, when he was on the field, you saw flashes of what he can do in fantasy. He only appeared in nine games, but in those contests, Hampton handled a 30% share of the team’s total rush attempts and targets. For context, anything at or above 30% in that metric is elite and quite rare. Now entering Year 2 in the league, there is room for that number to grow, and if it does in this Mike McDaniel scheme with a healthier offensive line, Hampton is a strong candidate to finish inside the top 10 at the position.
25956.dyn: We are not ready to put Hampton up there with guys like Bijan and Gibbs, but Hampton is a surefire RB1 in dynasty startups. He is only 23 years old and has that first-round draft capital that suggests he will have multiple seasons as LA’s bell cow. If you have him, ride this thing out for the next two to three years, knowing you have one of dynasty’s most valuable RBs.

tags.breakout: What a tease of a season we got from rookie Omarion Hampton a year ago. He had 314 yards rushing and 136 yards receiving before he went down to an ankle injury Week 5. He returned in Week 14 and gave us three out of four weeks as a top-20 RB before he sat out the final week of the season. When he was on the field, we saw the flashes that the Chargers saw when drafting Hampton 22nd overall in 2025. Now, Hampton gets a healthy offensive line, with both Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back and a new OC in Mike McDaniel, who loves to lean on a featured back when the situation presents (ahem, De’Von Achane). Behind Hampton, we are looking at Keaton Mitchell, Kimani Vidal, and FB Alec Ingold, presenting an opportunity for him to be quite the workhorse in Los Angeles.

25962.blurb: There was mixed chatter around Helm as he started his NFL career with the downtrodden Titans. He was the team's TE2 behind our pinup boy Chig (learning from the best, amirite?), and he put together a sneaky decent season. He had three TE11 finishes or better, and this was with a QB who was sacked 55 (!) times and had the third-worst 59% completion rate. Helm’s usage increased after his Week 10 bye, going from 8.7% target share to 13.1%. With Chig Okonkwo heading to the Commanders, the opportunity is there, making him an interesting prospect to keep an eye on, especially in deeper leagues.
25962.dyn: Helm is worth more in dynasty, especially with the rebuilding of the Titans. HC Robert Saleh has the reins now, and the organization splurged, taking WR Carnell Tate fourth overall, and padding the WR room with Wan’Dale Robinson. If QB Cam Ward can take a leap, there is a strong chance Helm will be along for the ride, making him an intriguing and somewhat affordable buy if you believe in the team.

25963.blurb: Meow. Would you be shocked to find out that Mason Taylor led the Jets in targets in 2025? Me. Too. The main reason was that Garrett Wilson was shut down early due to injury, and there was truly nothing else in town offensively. The second round selection in 2025 is immediately trounced by the drafting of athletic freak TE Kenyon Sadiq. Find Taylor a patch of sunshine and let him curl up. He does not belong in fantasy.
25963.dyn: The man with zero broken tackles might have a short tenure in New York as the organization seemingly drafted his replacement, Sadiq, with the 16th overall pick in 2026. You don’t need to hold onto this kitty in dynasty when a dawg is in town.

25964.blurb: Ayomanor was fine as a perimeter WR last year, but clearly the new regime is ready to relegate the former Stanford Cardinal to a role player after signing Wan’Dale in free agency then selecting Carnell Tate inside the top-five of the NFL Draft. For now, he is not on the radar for redraft leagues.
25964.dyn: Unfortunately, fourth-round NFL picks don’t usually carry much long-term value in dynasty unless they are outliers. “Epic” Ayomanor was fine as a rookie (511 yards, four TDs), but he is likely to be a secondary pass catcher in Tennessee, relegating him to a bench stash in dynasty with the hopes that he can make his way onto the field in 3WR sets over Calvin Ridley.

25970.blurb: Ferg-Daddy 2.0 is one of many TEs in Sean McVay’s crowded TE room, including the likes of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, and rookie Max Klare. We had high hopes for him in his rookie season. He didn’t deliver, running the fourth fewest routes among the team’s TEs and gaining only a 5% target share.  Ferguson did show off via the deep ball as he was the league leader among TEs in deep targets (20+ yards) with 15. Tyler Higbee and Davante Adams are not getting any younger, so perhaps we see a patented second-year breakout from the Oregon TE.
25970.dyn: A young TE tied to a prolific offense run by a guy who loves to use multiple TEs? Ferguson sounds like someone worth holding on to, at least for a couple of years, to see what he turns into. He has not played his way into weekly starter status, but hey, Colby Parkinson has definitely given us some startable weeks. Just saying.

tags.sleeper: The 2nd year TE is probably buried in your fantasy platform's ADP but his potential upside in this Rams offense should not be slept on. He led all TEs in 20+ air yard targets last year in a specialized role as the team's downfield threat. Sean McVay runs a ridiculous amount of 2 and 3-TE sets where Ferguson functions essentially as the team's slot WR. We project him as the 3rd option in this passing offense behind Davante Adams and Puka Nacua with a chance to become a sneaky TE option in 2026.

25971.blurb: There was a lot of chatter around what could have been with Oscar Delp, but looking at his numbers from college, he never really delivered. He never hit 300 receiving yards at Georgia thanks to competition with some guy named Brock Bowers basically running the offense during Delp’s first two seasons. Even with questions on the production profile, the Saints grabbed him in the third round to add youth to their TE room. He will have a tough time making an impact in redraft this year, presumably buried on the TE depth chart behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant.
25971.dyn: The athleticism is there, and Delp has the experience in a good college system. That plus draft capital should put him on your dynasty radar as a classic wait-and-see stash. Delp should be taken in your rookie drafts - probably around the TE4/TE5 - and you can sit back and wait to see what Kellen Moore can scheme for the man.
25971.rb: There was a lot of chatter around what could have been with Oscar Delp, but looking at his numbers from college, he never really delivered. He never hit 300 receiving yards at Georgia thanks to competition with some guy named Brock Bowers basically running the offense during Delp’s first two seasons. Even with questions on the production profile, the Saints grabbed him in the third round to add youth to their TE room. He will have a tough time making an impact in redraft this year, presumably buried on the TE depth chart behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant.

25975.blurb: Bryant did very little early in the season, but as the year went on, he started to pop as the team scaled back Troy Franklin’s role. Unfortunately, a concussion and hamstring injury limited his production late in the year, so entering Year 2, there are still question marks on Bryant as a player. He will have a role, but it is highly unlikely to be fantasy relevant now that Jaylen Waddle is on this roster. Consider him a potential waiver wire pickup if Waddle and/or Sutton miss time.
25975.dyn: Bryant’s dynasty value took a huge hit when the Broncos sent a first round pick for Jaylen Waddle. He’s a fun prospect who flashed at times as a rookie, so we would like to stash him if possible; It just might take a year or two for him to get a full-time role after Courtland Sutton ages out.

25976.blurb: A fourth-round pick in 2025, Lane saw limited action in a lost season for the Commanders, totaling just 16 receptions. He will be competing with incoming rookie Antonio Williams, veteran Van Jefferson, and the ghost of Treylon Burks for the WR2 job behind Terry McLaurin. Know the name, but you can ignore him to start the season.
25976.dyn: Lane is a fringe dynasty asset with the sole glimpse of light being an ambiguous WR depth chart behind Terry. He was targeted on 17% of his routes and averaged 1.24 yards per route run, both middling marks but not death sentences to his prospects. He is not a must hold, but if you want to wait-and-see what happens in Washington, be our guest.

25986.blurb: The 2025 7th round pick had 33 total touches his rookie year mixing in sparingly as a third down back. With Travis Etienne Jr. now in New Orleans, perhaps Allen carves out a bigger role alongside Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. For now, he is simply a name to know, not someone to draft even in the deepest of leagues.
25986.dyn: 7th round RBs have little shelf life even in on deep dynasty league benches. In full PPR leagues, consider him a stash if CROD continues to battle injury issues.

25987.blurb: Dike provided a ton of value for the Titans, especially in the return game. In fact, the guy set the NFL rookie record for the most all-purpose yards in a single season with 2,427 scrimmage yards in 2025. He is electric in the return game, and that is probably where he will shine as Carnell Tate, Wan’Dale Robinson, and Calvin Ridley run the most routes. He is not fantasy relevant right now, but if one of the WRs goes down to injury, we at least know he can play.
25987.dyn: Dike is a dart throw/end-of-bench stash in dynasty formats. Obviously, his outlook is capped with Carnell Tate going fourth overall and Wan’Dale signing that big contract in free agency. Perhaps he can carve out the WR3 role over time.

26032.blurb: With only a 7.7% target share and 15 catches on 26 targets, Arroyo is clearly the TE2 behind AJ Barner on the Super Bowl-winning squad. The team had the third fewest pass attempts in the NFL in 2025, so you aren’t investing in the TE2 in redraft this year.
26032.dyn: Arroyo is young and talented, and TEs often do take time to find their footing, so keeping him at the end of your deep bench is understandable. If you have a better use for that roster spot, though, no hard feelings.

26038.blurb: Blue was a hyped name last summer as a fifth-round rookie, and some claimed could take hold of the Dallas backfield. Whoops! He took a backseat to Javonte Williams while being inactive in 12 games last season. The Cowboys ultimately decided to cut Blue in late August, opening up the door for Malik Davis to take command of the RB2 role. After being cut, the Eagles signed Blue to their practice squad.
26038.dyn: Blue is a classic example of dynasty managers getting the cart before the horse. While the opportunity last off-season was there, the draft capital (149th overall pick) suggested he would likely not see the field much as a rookie. Considering he was cut by the Cowboys, his dynasty value is at an all time low.

26040.blurb: Should we just act like 2025 never happened? The Steelers drafted Johnson in the third round, and then it was all downhill from there. His kickoff blunder in Week 1 against Seattle set the stage for a train-wreck of a season where he was inactive in seven games and failed to have a single rush attempt gain 10+ yards. If there is any hope for the future, it is the fact that Mike Tomlin is gone, and Mike McCarthy could give him a clean slate. He begins the off-season as the projected RB3 in Pittsburgh.
26040.dyn: That sound you heard is the garbage truck passing your house as all your Kaleb Johnson dynasty shares are compacted into a worthless mess. He is still a hold because we all know “you can’t cut that guy”. Our studies show that Day 2 RBs who were sparingly used as a rookie (<70 total touches) often end up increasing in Year 2 with a double-digit per-game workload. Good luck!

26044.blurb: Last year’s second-round pick didn’t do much early on, but when he got his chance, he capitalized, particularly during Chicago’s playoff run. The Bears are obviously counting on Burden to take a big step forward this season after trading DJ Moore to the Bills, but it takes a lot of projection to buy into Burden’s juiced-up ADP. He is the hotness right now in Chicago’s WR room, but we need to remember he only earned 60 total targets for a 12.8% target share as a rookie. A bet on Burden is a bet on the talent profile and Ben Johnson using him to his full potential. We are viewing him as a high-upside pick who could provide big-time returns if things break right, but there is also a world that
26044.dyn: Burden entered the NFL with some question marks in his profile, but those seem to be put to bed after a highly efficient 2025 campaign. It took a while for the rookie to break out, but when he was on the field, he was highly efficient, averaging 2.69 yards per route run. Those efficiency marks signal some serious talent, but admittedly, there is still some uncertainty given the small sample size.

26054.blurb: McMillan delivered on the promise of being a top-10 NFL Draft pick a year ago, finishing with just over 1,000 yards and seven scores. The draft capital, Year 1 production, and efficiency marks suggest McMillan is poised for another step forward in his sophomore campaign. After seeing 25.4% of the target share a year ago as a rookie, T Mac is on our short list of WRs who could push for upwards of a 30% market share. With his talent, that should mean great things for fantasy.
26054.dyn: It is all there for McMillan to be one of the more valuable WRs in dynasty leagues moving forward. He broke out as a rookie, has elite draft capital, and has very little target competition on his own team. He is looking like a young building block for the foreseeable future, as we all have him inside our top-12 at the position.

tags.breakout: The reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year is coming off a WR17 season where he had just over 1,000 yards and seven TDs. There were obviously some ups and downs - fantasy finishes as low as WR108 (!) and as high as WR1 - but perhaps it is that exact roller coaster that is keeping his ADP manageable. We are ready for that patented second-year WR breakout on a team that has not changed drastically when it comes to offensive weapons. McMillan had a 25% target share in 2025, the 14th-highest among WRs, and with no massive draft-day additions beyond third-round draft pick Chris Brazzell, we anticipate the same this year. If Bryce Young improves again this year and McMillan catches a few more TDs, you will be extremely happy with your investment.

26056.blurb: Just as we were starting to see what the man could do last year, he injured his LCL and was out for the season. The WR room is now quite crowded in Jacksonville, and you still aren’t even sure that Hunter will be out there as one. High ceiling, sure, but your basement is literally a sub-level crawl space.
26056.dyn: If you took Hunter in your rookie draft last year, you are probably trying to move him. As you would only be getting pennies on the dollar, you might want to wait until he has a big game and then try to trade him. Immediately.

26079.blurb: Sanders wasn’t that bad, right? Welp, after checking the numbers, we can report back that it was hot garbage ranking dead last in catchable target rate (66.5%), completion percentage (56.6%), and Passer Rating (68.1). He did have one week for fantasy (QB2 vs. TEN in Week 14) that gave you a glimpse of the upside, but there is no guarantee for him to be the long-term solution for Cleveland. The Browns named Deshaun Watson their Week 1 starter, but we do expect Sanders to eventually make a handful of starts. In that scenario, even in SuperFlex leagues, we shy away from expecting anything out of the former fifth-round pick.
26079.dyn: Among 40 rookie QBs with 7+ starts over the last decade, Sanders ranked 38th in pass success rate and 39th in INT rate. It was barf-worthy, and a year from now, he could easily be an irrelevant name in SuperFlex leagues. Shedeur truthers like Mel Kiper Jr. must be in shambles.

26082.blurb: After the Giants traded up in the first round to take Dart, he exceeded expectations as a rookie, averaging 41 rushing yards per game in his starts, the fifth best among rookie QBs ever. He tied Drake Maye for fourth-best in fantasy points per dropback last year despite attempting three total passes to Malik Nabers before he went down. Dart’s upside is enticing despite the fact that he plays with reckless abandon. His ADP is not accounting for a Year 2 leap, making him a prime candidate to roll with as a late-round QB.
26082.dyn: There are some variables at play with a new coaching staff, offensive play-caller, and the recovery timeline for Malik Nabers. Nevertheless, Dart is a mobile QB on a young, ascending offense that seems to provide fantasy-friendly results. His playstyle might invite more risk, but in dynasty, we view him as a low-end QB1.

tags.breakout: The New York Football Giants traded up into the first round in 2025 to get their potential QB of the future in Ole Miss Rebel Jaxson Dart. And I think we can say, the gamble paid off. The first two games were questionable as he took over for Russell Wilson (remember that experiment?!), but he settled in quickly, changing the identity in New York. The QB16 on the season finished with almost 2,300 yards passing, but we all know that Dart’s rushing ability is his true calling card. He piled up 487 yards on the ground in 14 games (the third most among QBs) and nine TDs (the third most in NFL history by a rookie QB). You cannot ignore the elephant in the room - Dart runs with a kind of reckless abandon that makes you cover your eyes and cringe, consistently nervous that every rush may be his last. Be that as it may, Dart’s upside in his sophomore year is sky high, and to get that rushing upside as late as the range of QB8 to QB10 off the draft board makes him worth his weight in gold. Add in the fact that John Harbaugh is the new HC in town, and you might have a league winner on your hands with Dart, even if it takes time to get Malik Nabers back. Let’s learn to slide, though, Jaxson!

26092.blurb: Respectfully, Gronk. What the heck, dude?! Before Gronk called his man Ee-Meek-Ah Eg-Big-Boo, Egbuka was on fire, operating as the WR1 in Tampa en route to a true rookie year breakout. After Gronk’s snafu on live TV, Egbuka fell off the map, averaging just 3.2 catches and 41.1 yards per game from Week 6 on. If you zoom out, however, there are a lot of reasons for that - Egbuka played through a minor hammy injury, Baker got banged up, the O-line was injured, and Emeka’s catchable target rate was terrible. If drafts present an opportunity to buy back in on the former first-round pick, we are ready to pounce, especially with Mike Evans now in San Francisco and Chris Godwin another year older. E
26092.dyn: Despite the frustrating final two months of last year, there is still a lot to like with Egbuka. He is young, he is a former first-round pick who averaged 1.75 yards per route run, and he showed he can play in this league. Godwin may not be on this team much longer, so if there is any small buying window in your league on Egbuka, thanks to his up-and-down rookie year, we are definitely interested in seeing what it costs to get him on your dyno squad.

26101.blurb: Credit to TeSlaa. He got his own drop on the show and he scored six TDs despite seeing only 27 targets on the year. I mean, the guy knows how to score! Unfortunately, that TD rate is highly unsustainable, and he won’t see any volume with Amon-Ra, Jamo, and LaPorta all healthy.
26101.dyn: The Lions drafted TeSlaa way higher than anyone predicted a season ago, and after one year, that looks a bit silly considering his 0.81 YPRR (woof!). He is clearly just a role player, and the fact that both Amon-Ra and Jamo are signed for multiple years caps the possibility of TeSlaa turning into a fantasy star.

26102.blurb: The Raiders' fourth-round pick from 2025 was one of those “summer flings”. He gained some steam with a few camp highlights and some beat reporters lauding him to be the team’s starting X. Listen, we get it; summer is a time for being young and passionate. The dude caught ten passes on the season, including laying a goose egg in the receptions department in eight of his 15 games. Consider this a hard “No!"
26102.dyn: It was always a pipe dream thinking Thornton could turn into anything meaningful. We consistently preach this adage for incoming WRs for dynasty: if they cannot earn targets in college, why would they be able to do it in the NFL? Thornton was targeted on 13% of his routes and averaged 0.60 YPRR as a rookie, which puts him in “punt Baxter off a bridge” territory in dynasty.

26259.blurb: BILL CROSKEY!  The subject of Footballers fame burst onto the scene last summer as a seventh-round NFL draft pick and ultimately lost his starting job to Chris Rodriguez Jr. He converted just three of his 12 carries inside the 5-yard line to TDs last year and now finds more competition in the backfield with Rachaad White’s signing and rookie Kaytron Allen. While things look good on paper for Bill entering 2026, this is a buyer-beware situation. Washington is favored in just two of its first 10 games.
26259.dyn: BILL BILL BILL! He could hear sign language and dribble a bowling ball, but he could not overcome Chris Rodriguez Jr.! We have seen this story before, with NFL teams rarely handing over the keys to the backfield to unreliable Day 3 backs. For dynasty purposes, he is a hold unless someone in your league just heard their first tall tale of BILL CROSKEY and is ready to fork over some future picks.

tags.sleeper: Bill Croskey mania took over last year and it can be tough remembering where we've landed since. He profiles as the early downs back on an offense that should be in a number of shootouts to start the season. When looking at the Commanders’ RB depth chart, it features the inefficient Rachaad White, and Day 3 rookie, Kaytron Allen. White should have a receiving role as part of a committee at a minimum, but there is also a world that exists where JCM wins the RB1 job entering the season. He is the most explosive back and recent beat reports this off-season are emphasizing JCM being in on passing downs.Given that his ADP is dirt cheap, you can tack him onto the end of your bench as your RB4 with virtually zero risk.

26731.blurb: At 6’4” and 198 pounds, Brazzell has the prototypical perimeter deep threat build. He will likely compete with Xavier Legette for playing time as a rookie and be a part-time contributor, especially late in the year. We're not expecting the rookie to do much early on given that he suffered a knee injury in training camp that could sideline him for all of August. After all, are we really that excited about the third or fourth option in a Bryce Young offense? No offense, Bryce!
26731.dyn: It is always tough to project these Tennessee WRs from college to the pros, so we see a wide range of outcomes for Brazzell. He is a tall, rangy perimeter player who can win down the field, but he likely needs to develop more of a refined skillset to make it in the league. He is a fine stash, but we are not overly excited about it.
26731.rb: At 6’4” and 198 pounds, Brazzell has the prototypical perimeter deep threat build. He will likely compete with Xavier Legette for playing time as a rookie and be a part-time contributor, especially late in the year. We're not expecting the rookie to do much early on given that he suffered a knee injury in training camp that could sideline him for all of August. After all, are we really that excited about the third or fourth option in a Bryce Young offense? No offense, Bryce!

26737.blurb: Randall came to Clemson as a highly regarded WR and ended his senior year as an intriguing RB prospect after collecting 13 total TDs and 36 receptions. He was taken on Day 3, most notably as someone hand-selected by the team’s owner, which is either the best thing or the worst thing, depending on your point of view. Perhaps he can earn the RB2 role behind the Big Dog, but the most likely outcome is that he is just a role player in Year 1. Randall is beginning the season on IR because of injury.
26737.dyn: Randall is huge (6’2”, 230+ lbs.), making him a unique evaluation for the NFL. We all love a good narrative and a chance to connect the dots for fantasy. We have seen some recent success from former WRs who converted to RB in the NFL, including Antonio Gibson, Tony Pollard, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. In rookie drafts, he was one of our favorite Round 3 lottery tickets.

Perhaps he can earn the RB2 role behind the Big Dog, but the most likely outcome is that he is just a role player in Year 1. Randall is beginning the season on IR because of injury.

26740.blurb: Mendoza’s storybook college career is one of the most compelling parts of the No. 1 overall pick. From his humble beginnings as a lightly recruited three-star QB to transferring to Indiana and having a season for the ages, which ended in an undefeated national championship. He jumped in every single meaningful statistical category and became Indiana’s first-ever Heisman Trophy winner and the first in the Big Ten since 2006. The Raiders are starting fresh with play-caller Klint Kubiak at the helm. In Year 1, Mendoza will likely take some lumps. He is off the redraft radar, waiting his turn to start behind veteran Kirk Cousins.
26740.dyn: When you mix in a relatively weak draft class with Mendoza’s winning mentality, production, and precision passing, it is not hard to see why the Raiders would envision him as their heir apparent at QB. In SuperFlex, we have him in the 1.05 range behind the elite WRs. Depending on your strategy and team needs, Mendoza is not a must-target, but we can see the path of him eventually being a low-end QB1 for dynasty.

He is off the redraft radar, waiting his turn to start behind veteran Kirk Cousins.

26745.blurb: Bell was viewed in league circles as a fringe first-round NFL Draft pick before tearing his ACL in 2025. Because of the injury, he fell to the third round and landed in an intriguing spot. Unfortunately, because of the ACL recovery, we are not expecting Bell to be 100% in training camp, which, for a rookie, is not ideal when you are trying to learn the ropes of the NFL. Look for him to be more of a factor late in the season and in 2027.
26745.dyn: If it weren’t for the ACL injury, Bell would be higher in our rookie rankings and our dynasty rankings. He is the perfect type of prospect to hold if you are in a rebuild, as it could be a slow Year 1 off the injury. Moving forward into 2027, Bell could easily emerge as a top option for this team. Stash him on your taxi squad or at the end of your bench.
26745.rb: Bell was viewed in league circles as a fringe first-round NFL Draft pick before tearing his ACL in 2025. Because of the injury, he fell to the third round and landed in an intriguing spot. Unfortunately, because of the ACL recovery, we are not expecting Bell to be 100% in training camp, which, for a rookie, is not ideal when you are trying to learn the ropes of the NFL. Look for him to be more of a factor late in the season and in 2027.

26746.blurb: Lane saw a bunch of contested catches at USC, which is interesting considering his slender build. Expect him to start the season behind Flowers and Rashod Bateman in a part-time role with the chance to develop over the course of his rookie season. For now, he is not worth looking at in fantasy drafts.
26746.dyn: The production profile for Lane is pretty underwhelming, but he is an early declare prospect who played next to Makai Lemon at USC, so we will leave the light on for him in dynasty formats as a stash. This is a new coaching staff, and Rashod Bateman hasn’t exactly been a prolific weapon for the team in recent years. If he surprises as a rookie, there is a path, but it’s a pretty thin bet.

26747.blurb: Entering the 2026 season, it is possible Boston is playing behind Jerry Jeudy and KC Concepcion to start the season. For now, we view him as a name to monitor throughout the early part of the year rather than a priority redraft target. Perhaps he can come on late in the year to provide some late-season rookie upside.
26747.dyn: Many thought Big Denzel was going in the first round of the NFL Draft, but he slipped to the early part of Round 2. He will have a role as that true X receiver for the Browns, but with KC Concepcion joining the team at the same time as the more exciting prospect, Boston’s fantasy upside is probably capped until the Browns get the QB position solved.

26748.blurb: After the A.J. Brown trade to New England, rookie Makai Lemon should step into a starting role right away as a rookie across from DeVonta Smith. The 2025 Biletnikoff Award winner in college, Lemon’s production during his final season at USC was excellent, but the one question mark entering the NFL is whether or not he can play on the perimeter, as he was primarily a slot player in college. Philly’s offense should look a lot different this year with a new OC in town. If he is as talented as the production profile suggests and Jalen Hurts can bounce back as a passer, Lemon has a chance to be a meaningful difference maker for fantasy in 2026 and enter WR3 territory. That said, Lemon might get o
26748.dyn: This man’s interviews…not great. The route running and production profile? We love it! Lemon has the tools to be a great NFL receiver, and his production from college was off the charts. Philly grabbed him in the first round of the NFL Draft, and generally speaking, when you combine first-round NFL Draft capital with excellent collegiate production, good things happen in dynasty. With Philly moving on from AJ Brown, Lemon will have a big opportunity right away as a rookie.
26748.rb: After the A.J. Brown trade to New England, rookie Makai Lemon should step into a starting role right away as a rookie across from DeVonta Smith. The 2025 Biletnikoff Award winner in college, Lemon’s production during his final season at USC was excellent, but the one question mark entering the NFL is whether or not he can play on the perimeter, as he was primarily a slot player in college. Philly’s offense should look a lot different this year with a new OC in town. If he is as talented as the production profile suggests and Jalen Hurts can bounce back as a passer, Lemon has a chance to be a meaningful difference maker for fantasy in 2026 and enter WR3 territory. That said, Lemon might get off to a slower start as he's missed valuable time in both mini camp and training camp because of a hamstring injury.

26750.blurb: Germie probably needs an injury to one of DK Metcalf or Michael Pittman to be fantasy relevant this year. We are projecting him to play in the slot for Pittsburgh, and while that role could provide plenty of value for the Steelers, we are skeptical that it turns into enough fantasy points to make him a startable asset. The rookie is worth monitoring throughout camp, but for now, he is nothing more than a late-round stash.
26750.dyn: Things look crowded right now in Pittsburgh with Metcalf and Pitty City atop the depth chart. However, those veterans may not be in town for more than a couple of seasons, so perhaps Bernard’s role can grow with time. His efficiency metrics coming out of Alabama are middling, however, so we don’t view him as a surefire prospect.
26750.rb: Germie probably needs an injury to one of DK Metcalf or Michael Pittman to be fantasy relevant this year. The rookie is worth monitoring throughout camp, but for now, he is nothing more than a late-round stash.

26751.blurb: With Kellen Moore’s offense projecting to be among the league leaders in pace and play volume and the Saints not really having a reliable third option in the receiver room, we think both Olave and Tyson can eat this year. Of course, we are projecting Olave as the #1 option, especially after Tyson suffered yet another hamstring injury in training camp. He's expected to miss about two months, which means he's going to miss multiple regular season games. He's beginning the season on IR, which makes him a tough click in redraft leagues given the injury risk unless your league uses an IR spot. That said, if he can get healthy, the late-season upside is real if the Saints offense takes a leap in Y
26751.dyn: Tyson’s production profile was excellent coming out of Arizona State, and then the Saints grabbed him with the eigth overall pick in this year’s Draft. When you combine that early breakout, top-tier production, and elite draft capital, it makes Tyson a really strong long-term bet in dynasty formats.
26751.rb: With Kellen Moore’s offense projecting to be among the league leaders in pace and play volume and the Saints not really having a reliable third option in the receiver room, we think both Olave and Tyson can eat this year. Of course, we are projecting Olave as the #1 option, especially after Tyson suffered yet another hamstring injury in training camp. That said, if he can get healthy, the late-season upside is real if the Saints offense takes a leap in Year 2 of the Kellen Moore era.

26752.blurb: Tennessee surprised a lot of folks in April when they took Carnell Tate fourth overall in the NFL Draft. That type of draft capital suggests he will be on the field right away as an every-down player with the chance to lead the team in production. It can take time for rookie WRs to develop throughout the year, so even if Tate doesn’t get off to a fast start, he is a player who could really provide a boost to your squad late in the year.
26752.dyn: Tate was never really the guy in his Ohio State offense, so analytically, there are some holes in his profile. That said, he brings elite draft capital and is probably the best vertical threat in this year’s rookie class as a true perimeter receiver. We have him as a top-20 overall WR in the ranks, but his ability to hit his true ceiling over the next two to three years will depend on Cam Ward’s ability to develop as a starting QB.

tags.breakout: Welcome in the fourth overall pick to the breakout conversation. And how could you not? Tennessee made a strong statement by drafting an alpha for second-year QB Cam Ward this year, and we can assume the organization has a plan for the WR out of Ohio State. Even with the addition of Wan’Dale Robinson, the depth chart is sparse, setting up Tate to be the guy. The only concern with drafting him is whether or not Cam Ward can make the leap to make Tate’s ADP a steal. We think he can.

26753.blurb: Before transferring to Ohio State for his final year, Klare was a production monster at Purdue and showcased target-earning ability that could intrigue at the next level. Unfortunately, his first-year prospects are dim as he was selected by the Rams, who collect TEs like it is going out of style. Los Angeles has Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, and Davis Allen on the roster, making the rookie just another guy in the room. Sean McVay has shown a strong proclivity to running 13-personnel, so we know Klare will be rotated in.
26753.dyn: We think that Klare can eventually prove to be a valuable part of this McVay high-flying offense. He is a great stash in dynasty to see how he is used, but do not expect too much, too soon.

26755.blurb: Sadiq’s impressive athletic profile (remember when he broke almost every record at the NFL Combine?) catapulted him into the first round, heading to the New York Jets at pick 16. The question marks related to his usage at Oregon remain, as fantasy managers must question if a man who couldn’t top 600 receiving yards during his final year in college will be successful as a Jet with Geno Smith under center? He could end up second or third on the team in targets behind WR Garrett Wilson and RB Breece Hall, while competing with fellow rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Oh, and there is also a feline in Mason Taylor in the room that Sadiq has to overtake on the depth chart. Between you and me, a dawg always w
26755.dyn: Dynasty is another story for Sadiq, who shows strong promise looking into the future. One of the youngest at the position, only 20 years old, and drafted to an organization trying desperately to be “one QB away,” Sadiq could be one of the great TEs of the next few years. Some managers may be down to overpay, wowed by his Combine athletic performance, evidenced by him going as high as the 1.07 in rookie drafts. We have him ranked as a top-12 dynasty TE asset to start 2026.

26981.dyn: The Indiana RB was the lesser-known of their National Championship-winning backfield duo, and yet Roman Hemby went undrafted. We have a history of failed 49ers RB draft picks, but Black should be evaluated based on his profile, not their lack of success. He belongs in the mid-second round of drafts, but RB-thirsty managers might push him higher.
26981.rb: Despite a lackluster production profile, Black was a hot commodity in pre-draft visits, meeting with 10 teams before the 49ers surprisingly selected him 90th overall. Kyle Shanahan offenses always surprise us with the names that leap from obscurity, but this one was a head scratcher. CMC is coming off a season where he touched the ball 413 times, so perhaps we see Black worked into the mix. Pay attention to camp reports to see where he lands on the depth chart, competing with Jordan James and Isaac Guerendo for backup duties.

27045.blurb: The former #1 RB recruit in the nation finished his four-year career at Penn State as Penn State's all-time rushing TD leader with 45! Unfortunately, after suffering a foot injury during a Senior Bowl practice, Singleton's draft stock fell to the fifth round. If you believe in his size/speed combo, perhaps he can eventually overtake Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears and turn into a team's lead back in the back half of the season.
27045.dyn: We continually point out the fact that the stickiest stat from college to the pros is TD production, so Singleton certainly checks that box. When you add in over 100 career receptions, there is a lot to get excited about. The question is whether these stats simply make him a compiler or point to a difference-maker at the next level? The draft capital might not sound appealing (fifth round), but the context of the landing spot is what is most appealing. Pollard and Spears will be free agents in 2

It suggests they have a plan for him, and with Ricky Pearsall battling knee issues at the start of camp, he could be more than just a role player in Year 1. San Francisco did bring back Deebo on a one-year deal after Pearsall's latest knee injury, so perhaps it pours some cold water on the Stribling hype. Still, he profiles as a guy who could play on the perimeter across from Evans, and the camp reviews have been excellent. You can throw a dart late in your draft and stash him with minimal risk. We're in!
28053.dyn: From a dynasty outlook, the draft capital here is doing A LOT of the heavy lifting. Analytically, Stribling is a pretty weak prospect. He is already 23 years old after playing five collegiate seasons, and in those five years, he cleared 850 receiving yards just once. One area where he does excel is after the catch, which is usually what the 49ers look for in their WRs. He is also good in the blocking game…sure sounds like a Kyle Shanahan receiver, doesn’t it? All in all, he was probably over-dra

tags.sleeper: The 49ers unexpectedly took Stribling with the first pick of the second round and we immediately started scratching our heads: "What do they know that we don't?!" The Ole Miss product has the size/speed combination we look for at the NFL level and the drum beat this off-season has been nothing but positive for Stribling. With Ricky Pearsall out for the season with another injury, there is room for the rookie to start right away in 2WR sets alongside Mike Evans for the 49ers. Even with SF bringing back Deebo Samuel, the rookie is an intriguing flier at the end of your drafts on an offense that we desperately want pieces of in 2026. You can throw a dart late and stash him with next to no risk.
