injury_text: Injury Report Home   >   2026 Ultimate Draft Kit   >  UDK – Injury Report Recap of the health and recovery from major injuries QB RB WR TE Patrick Mahomes KC | 30 Years Old ACL + LCL Surgery Date: December 15, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Likely ready for Week 1 Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs had a disappointing 2025 season by their standards, and it all culminated in Week 15 when the All-Pro QB tore two ligaments in his left knee. Mahomes tore the ACL and the LCL (ligament on the outside of the knee) in mid-December and was placed on IR. Generally speaking, players off an isolated ACL injury wait about four weeks to have surgery in order to allow swelling to come down and restore knee range of motion, but Mahomes' procedure was performed the day after his injury in order to repair the LCL right away. This multi-ligament procedure comes with a lengthy rehab process that will extend well into the summer. However, because Mahomes is a QB and can play from the pocket, I do think he has a chance to be ready for the start of the regular season. If he were an RB, WR, or TE, he would certainly be starting on PUP. When Mahomes does get back on the field, fantasy gamers should not expect any of the rushing production we saw in 2025 when he set career highs in per-game rushing attempts, yards, and TDs. He will be a strict pocket passer for the majority of the 2026 season. Bo Nix DEN | 26 Years Old Right Ankle Fracture Surgery Date: January 20, 2026 Return Timeline: Cleared for Training Camp, Ready for Week 1 Nix injured his right ankle late in the team's win over the Bills in the Divisional Round of the playoffs and underwent surgery a few days later to address a fracture. It remains unclear whether Nix is dealing with a joint-related issue stemming from previous ankle injuries or another structural problem. Nix has a significant ankle injury history dating back to his college days, and head coach Sean Payton alluded to it when discussing Nix's recent procedure. Right now, the details of the injury aren't known, but reports from late April indicated that the Denver QB required a follow up procedure on the ankle. This isn't necessarily unusual, but it does add a layer of complexity to his injury and his injury history. Sometimes a second minor procedure is required to remove hardware, or a "clean up" procedure is used to address joint stiffness. Either way, this doesn't change his season-long outlook for 2026. Nix has been fully cleared for training camp and will be ready to go for Week 1 barring any unforeseen setbacks. Daniel Jones IND | 29 Years Old Achilles Surgery Date: December 9, 2025 Return Timeline: Cleared for Week 1 Jones and the Colts caught the league by storm in 2025 and looked like they were headed for a top seed in the AFC. Sadly, that all came to an abrupt end when Jones tore the Achilles in his right leg in Week 14 against Jacksonville. Jones underwent surgery in early December, so he spent the early part of the offseason and summer rehabbing. I do expect him to return to the field early in training camp, though he will not be 100%. He's very likely to be cleared for Week 1, but his status is worth monitoring throughout August. The reason he has a chance to return within about nine months is because of the position he plays. If he were an RB or WR, there is no chance he would be able to play in nine months, but given that he is a QB, he can play his position at less than 100%. Now, that does not mean we're going to be getting pre-injury Daniel Jones in the first chunk of the season. His mobility, especially as a runner, is going to be compromised for the vast majority of the 2026 season. Furthermore, because this is Jones' right leg, and he's a right-handed QB, his push off that right leg during dropbacks could be negatively impacted, thereby reducing his downfield velocity and accuracy. Michael Penix Jr. ATL | 26 Years Old ACL Surgery Date: Week of November 24, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Could be ready for Week 1 Coming into the NFL, Penix had a lengthy and somewhat concerning injury history. He had multiple ACL injuries in his right knee in college, and those knee concerns have not gone away in the pros. Penix missed a game in Week 8 because of a bone bruise in his knee, and then suffered a season-ending left knee injury in Week 11 when he suffered a partially torn ACL. Sometimes, players can function with a partial tear of the major ligament, but ultimately, the medical staff and team opted for a full reconstruction, suggesting the injury was more severe than just a minor sprain. With Penix's surgery taking place in late November, he will have roughly eight months of rehab before training camp and about nine months before the start of the season. Therefore, he will be doing limited work with the offense in OTAs and minicamp, but I do expect him to ramp up his participation during training camp. Given that Penix is a pure pocket passer, he does have a good chance to be ready for Week 1 in a vacuum. The reason I put it that way is that this is not a "normal situation" by any means. The QB now has a significant injury history on both knees, and the Falcons invested the 8th overall pick in him just a couple of years ago. They will surely want to give him every chance to be their long-term starter moving forward, but if they rush him back, the chances of him developing into the franchise QB could be compromised. Given his injury history, it would not be surprising to see the team take a more conservative approach, so for now, I'd consider him questionable for Week 1. Ashton Jeanty LV | 22 Years Old Right Ankle Sprain Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 Las Vegas' star RB left practice on Sunday, August 23 with a right ankle injury and did not return. Multiple local beat reports indicated that Jeanty collided with a teammate while attempting to catch a pass, and following the play, he was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was assisted off the field with trainers. Initially, there was fear Jeanty might miss a significant amount of time, but following additional testing and evaluation, it now appears this is not a long-term ankle injury with Ian Rapoport describing the injury as "more low than high." The wording here is not really a diagnosis, but clinically, this is likely a mild-to-moderate high ankle sprain that does not include the syndesmotic ligament that connects the lower leg bones. That type of high ankle sprain is generally more severe and debilitating. If this "more low than high" description is correct, Jeanty's injury likely includes an injury to the ligaments that sit just above and below the ankle joint. If this is a Grade II (moderate) injury, the recovery timeline is likely somewhere in that 2-4 week window. As a result, Jeanty should be considered Questionable for Week 1, but I do not anticipate this injury lingering beyond the first couple of regular season games. In other words, if he doesn't play Week 1, I'd expect we see him in Week 2 or Week 3. Functionally, we are likely to see a dip in Jeanty's lateral agility with cutting, so perhaps he's not as effective as he otherwise would be in his return to the field, but as the season progresses, he should be able to get back to 100%. Jeremiyah Love ARI | 21 Years Old Left High Ankle Sprain Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 The #3 overall pick in the NFL Draft is now dealing with an ankle injury after he exited the Cardinals' first preseason game on August 13. Initially, Mike LaFleur downplayed the injury, stating that Jeremiyah Love would likely return to practice in the near future, but he has since backtracked on that prognosis with the team now confirming that they will hold him out of practice the week of August 17. While the team has not confirmed the specific type of injury, video of the injury is consistent with a high ankle sprain. Furthermore, LaFleur stating that Love came into the building more sore in the days following the injury is consistent with how high ankle sprains tend to behave. Players often feel worse 24 to 48 hours following the injury once swelling and stiffness set in. Right now, fantasy managers shouldn't panic on Love's outlook, especially with four weeks of recovery prior to Week 1. However, it's realistic that the former Notre Dame RB misses multiple weeks in camp, which could affect his early-season playing time and usage. Breece Hall NYJ | 25 Years Old Groin Strain Return Timeline: Like out of practice 1-2 weeks; Questionable for Week 1 Breece Hall left practice on Monday, August 17 with a groin injury and did not return. The coaching staff and local beat reporters confirmed that Hall did receive an MRI and by their accounts, the injury is considered "minor." That could suggest a Grade I strain, which typically only carries a recovery of 1-2 weeks. While that is a reasonable prognosis, it's important to note that the groin muscles are particularly important for running backs because of the constant cutting and change of direction required of the position. Because of that, he could be limited or out of practice for longer than that 1-2 week period. For now, it's not a guarantee that Hall is available for Week 1 until we see him back on the practice field in a couple of weeks. Zach Charbonnet SEA | 25 Years Old ACL Surgery Date: February 20, 2026 Return Timeline: Could begin regular season on PUP Charbonnet tore his ACL in his left knee in the Divisional Round of the playoffs against the 49ers, which was brutal timing for multiple reasons. First, the man didn't get to chase his dreams and play in the Super Bowl, and second, his 2026 outlook is now affected in a major way. Because of this January injury, Charbonnet is going to be limited the entire offseason, including training camp. As of this writing in early February, the specifics of this ACL injury aren't known. For his 2026 return timeline, it matters whether or not this was a clean ACL tear or one that included additional damage. Either way, I expect him to begin the regular season on PUP with the possibility that his recovery extends well into October, depending on the details of the injury. Once he does get on the field, he will need additional time to ramp up, which means he's unlikely to be fantasy relevant until November at the earliest. The most likely outcome here is that 2026 is a down season, which is difficult timing for Charbs, considering he is entering the final year of his rookie contract. Cam Skattebo NYG | 24 Years Old Ankle Fracture-Dislocation Surgery Date: October 26, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited early in the offseason; Ready for Week 1 Skattebo's 2025 season came to an abrupt end in late October when he suffered a fractured and dislocated right ankle against the Eagles. Skattebo underwent surgery immediately after and was cleared to begin rehabbing a few weeks after the procedure. As of early January, Skattebo was out of his boot and off crutches, so he's progressing nicely. That said, he still has a long way to go in order to make a full recovery, which can take upwards of a year before players are back to full strength. Early on in the process, I'd anticipate Skattebo being pretty limited for OTAs and minicamp, but there is a chance he can be cleared at some point in training camp. Expect Skattebo's best football to be played in the back half of the season, as it may take time to regain his explosiveness and dynamic ability. Quinshon Judkins CLE | 22 Years Old Ankle Fracture-Dislocation Surgery Date: December 23, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Likely ready for Week 1 Judkins' impressive rookie season came to a close late in the season when he suffered a right ankle fracture and dislocation. The injury is similar to that of Cam Skattebo, but the main difference here is that Judkins' injury happened about two months later. As a result, we should expect Judkins to be limited throughout the spring and summer. He's still got a chance to be cleared for Week 1, though he won't be 100% when the season begins. Generally speaking, it takes some time for players to regain their pre-injury dynamic ability, so it's likely we see Judkins get off to a slower start in 2026. He will probably be more productive over the back half of his sophomore season. Alvin Kamara NO | 31 Years Old MCL Sprain Return Timeline: Doubtful for Week 1 Kamara suffered a sprained MCL in mid August and he's now set to miss "at least a month" per multiple local and national reporters. That reporting timeline suggests the veteran is dealing with at least a Grade II (moderate) sprain. With Kamara set to miss the remainder of the preseason and training camp, he's on the wrong side of Questionable for Week 1. If this injury pushes 4-6 weeks, he'll likely miss a couple of games to begin the 2026 season. The veteran does have a history of prior knee and ankle injuries, so at this stage of his career with Etienne atop the depth chart, expect the Saints to ease him back into action once he's fully healed. Chuba Hubbard CAR | 27 Years Old Hamstring Strain Return Timeline: Week-to-week, Likely to play Week 1 News broke on August 13 that Chuba Hubbard is dealing with a hamstring injury that is considered "week-to-week" according to Dave Canales. That week-to-week prognosis does not provide much detail regarding the severity, but as we have seen across the league, hamstring injuries can linger for multiple weeks as players try to ramp up their activity level and intensity in camp. For now, I would tentatively expect Chuba to miss at least a week of practice, but it is possible he is not available until later in August. For what it's worth, Canales noted that the team does expect Chuba to be available for Week 1. Kyle Monangai CHI | 24 Years Old Hyperextended Right Knee Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 Chicago's RB2 left practice early on August 16 with a right knee injury and did not return. It's now being reported that Monangai suffered a hyperextension of his right knee. The expectation with this type of injury, which can include sprained ligament(s) and/or a bone bruise, is that Monangai will miss "multiple weeks." The exact details of Monangai's injury are not known, but if there is a bone bruise component to the injury, this hyperextension injury could affect his Week 1 availability. If the injury is only a mild sprain, he could get back to practice at some point in late August. Regardless of whether or not he plays in Week 1, we can expect his workload to be managed early in the season, especially after he missed time early in camp with a soft tissue injury. Isiah Pacheco DET | 27 Years Old MCL Sprain, Back Injury Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 Dan Campbell announced on August 10 that Pacheco is expected to miss multiple weeks while recovering from a sprained MCL. He also noted that the team does expect Pacheco to return for Week 1. Assuming that is accurate, it suggests this is a mild to moderate (Grade I or Grade II) sprain, and these lower-grade MCL sprains heal well because of their great blood supply. At the time of injury, Pacheco will have roughly one month to rehab ahead of Week 1, which should be enough time for him to get back to 100% ahead of Week 1. However, in late August, Dan Campbell shared that Pacheco is now also dealing with a back injury. It remains to be seen how serious this new back injury is, but the fact that the team brought in Kareem Hunt for a visit suggests the former Chief is in danger of missing Week 1. Josh Jacobs GB | 28 Years Old Groin Strain Return Timeline: 2-3 Weeks Josh Jacobs began missing practice on August 6 with a groin injury, and as of this writing, he has yet to return to the practice field. Multiple beat reporters have suggested that the injury is not believed to be serious or long-term, but on August 11, Matt LaFleur confirmed that Jacobs is expected to miss at least one more week of practice. For now, this is a soft tissue injury that is worth monitoring, but Jacobs' Week 1 availability is not in doubt. Green Bay has historically been conservative when it comes to managing injuries, so Jacobs will likely be limited initially when he does return to the field. Bucky Irving TB | 24 Years Old Labrum Repair Surgery Date: February 2026 Return Timeline: Cleared for Week 1 Bucky Irving dealt with foot and shoulder injuries in 2025, limiting him to just 10 games. His foot injury healed without requiring surgery, but his shoulder injury did require a stabilization procedure. Reports from last year suggest that Irving's shoulder injury was a subluxation (AKA partial dislocation). These injuries require surgery in football players given the nature of the contact sport. That procedure is usually a labrum repair to help stabilize the joint. This recovery is generally straight forward, but it takes multiple months before players are cleared for contact. He didn't participate fully in OTAs or mini-camp, but he should be fully cleared for Week 1. J.K. Dobbins DEN | 27 Years Old Lisfranc Surgery Surgery Date: November 2025 Return Timeline: Limited in OTAs and Mini Camp, Cleared for Week 1 JK Dobbins suffered yet another season-ending injury in 2025. In Week 10 against the Raiders, Dobbins suffered a left mid-foot injury, likely a Lisfranc injury. Generally speaking, these injuries can be difficult for skill players in the NFL because the ligaments involved at these joints are crucial for stability in the foot during sprinting, cutting and change of direction. Initially, there was hope that Dobbins could rehab the foot without surgery and potentially return later in the season, which tells us that the injury was on the more mild side of the spectrum when it comes to Lisfranc injuries. These types of injuries range from a mild sprain (partial ligament tear) to a full dislocation of the joint with associated fracture. For Dobbins, the good news is that because his injury was on the more modest side of that spectrum, he's far more likely to return to form than a player who had suffered a more severe injury. Regardless, research does show that players coming off this procedure in Year 1 do tend to have less efficiency and reduced explosiveness upon return to play. With Dobbins having 10 months to be cleared for Week 1, I do anticipate he'll be able to enter Week 1 with minimal limitations, but he could require some time to regain his explosiveness and dynamic cutting ability. Dobbins was already participating in individual drills at OTAs, which is obviously a great sign, and he's been a full participant in training camp. RJ Harvey DEN | 25 Years Old Shoulder Labrum Repair Surgery Date: Late January/Early February 2026 Return Timeline: Training Camp News broke in mid June during OTAs that last year's rookie RB, RJ Harvey, tore the labrum in his shoulder against the Patriots in the AFC Championship game. He required surgery to repair the labrum, but the exact date of that procedure isn't known as of this writing. If we assume he had surgery shortly after the injury happened, he'll have roughly seven months before the start of Week 1. The recovery timeline here in contact sports is generally longer in an effort to protect the repair and reduce risk of re-injury. Because of that, Harvey was limited to individual drills early in training camp, but drafters can expect him to be fully cleared towards the back half of the camp and be ready for Week 1. Chris Rodriguez Jr. JAX | 25 Years Old Foot Surgery Surgery Date: Spring 2026 Return Timeline: Training Camp The Jaguars signed Chris Rodriquez Jr. in free agency, but he did not participate in OTAs or Mini Camp because of an unspecified foot injury. The injury reportedly required a procedure, but like the injury, the details of the surgery are not available as of early June. Rodriguez has been participating in individual drills in training camp as of late July/early August, and in mid August, he began participating in 11-on-11 team drills. That's a great first step in his return to the field, but it's still going to take some time for him to ramp up throughout the rest of August. Barring any setbacks, I do expect him to be ready for Week 1. Joe Mixon FA | 30 Years Old Right Ankle and Foot Injuries Surgery Date: Unknown Return Timeline: TBD Joe Mixon missed time in 2024 due to a high ankle sprain in his left leg, then missed the entire 2025 season due to an unspecified right ankle/foot injury that he suffered while training in the spring away from the facility. Speaking after the conclusion of the season, Texans GM Nick Caserio said, “It was a freak thing. Honestly, I’ve never seen it, the condition.” Caserio also added that there is nothing irresponsible that Mixon did, and that it was a medical situation that didn’t improve. Obviously, this is a murky situation and nearly impossible to speak to without knowing the specifics. Entering the 2026 offseason, it remains to be seen if the RB stays with Houston. If the team performs a physical and decides to move on, it could tell us that his foot is not in a place where the team feels comfortable to continue with him on the roster. The veteran back turned 30 in July, and after missing an entire season because of injury, it obviously brings into question Mixon's future in the NFL. Given this chronic injury, it's possible Mixon never returns to his pre-injury level of play or returns to the NFL at all. This remains an ongoing situation to monitor throughout the offseason. Najee Harris NYG | 28 Years Old Achilles Surgery Date: Late September 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Cleared for Week 1 It feels like forever ago at this point, but Harris was in the news almost daily throughout August as we awaited his return to the field following a fireworks eye injury sustained on the 4th of July. Once he was finally able to ramp up and contribute to the Chargers' offense, it looked like we were heading for a potential split with then-rookie Omarion Hampton. Unfortunately, Najee's 2025 quickly went from bad to worse in Week 3 when he tore the Achilles in his left leg against the Broncos. Harris underwent surgery the week of September 22 to repair the torn tendon. When the NFL season kicks off, he will be just under one year removed from surgery, which means he will have a good chance to be cleared for the start of the season. That said, he's unlikely to be 100% right away coming off this injury. On top of the injury recovery, Najee didn't sign until late in the season, so he didn't have a traditional NFL offseason/training camp. It'll take time for him to ramp up early in the season as he mixes in behind Cam Skattebo and/or Tyrone Tracy. Jordyn Tyson NO | 22 Years Old Hamstring Strain Return Timeline: Likely to miss 3+ regular season games; Could begin season on IR Jordyn Tyson entered the NFL with a history of hamstring injuries, and unfortunately, that trend has continued in training camp. Tyson missed games during his final year in college because of recurring hamstring problems, and the Saints tried to limit his reps in the spring in order to mitigate short term risk. While Tyson did enter camp without restrictions, he injured his hamstring again in joint practices on August 13. The Saints have said the newest injury is not related to his previous injury, yet at the same time, it's been confirmed that the rookie is seeking multiple opinions, which is not the norm for the vast majority of hamstring injuries. This suggests the injury severe enough for New Orleans to consult multiple medical professionals. When speaking about the injury, head coach Kellen Moore said "I think my understanding of this one, any player that was put in his situation where your foot slips and you get shoved from behind...Any player in that situation probably has the same diagnosis coming out of this." With Moore suggesting Tyson's foot slipped and he was shoved from behind, it's likely that this hamstring injury is located higher up towards the attachment at the hip. These proximal hamstring injuries that include the hamstring tendon do take longer to heal than most injuries in the middle of the muscle. If this is in fact what's happening with Tyson, he's going to miss multiple regular season games. Expect New Orleans to be ultra conservative with their top-10 pick after he's dealt with recurring hamstring problems for the better part of the last calendar year. He could begin the season on the IR and miss the first month of the season. Puka Nacua LAR | 25 Years Old Hip Flexor Strain Return Timeline: Likely to play Week 1 Puka Nacua has been battling a hip flexor injury in training camp since August 11, but he appears to be making progress in his recovery. As of August 25, Puka was not participating in team drills, but he was working on the side with the rehab staff and doing some speed work, indicating he's nearing a return to the field. The hip flexor is a primary muscle used for generating power during the sprint motion, so the fact that Nacua is doing this with about two weeks out from the start of the season is a great sign for his Week 1 availability. Of course, soft tissue injuries should always be tracked closely given the high recurrence rate, but barring a setback, I do anticipate Nacua being on the field for the regular season opener. Mike Evans SF | 33 Years Old Groin Strain Return Timeline: Likely to play Week 1 Mike Evans has been battling multiple injuries since he arrived in San Francisco (insert Substation joke here). He dealt with a quad injury early on, and at one point, he was seen with a wrap and ice on his foot and ankle. Most recently, as of August 25, Evans is now sitting out practice with a groin injury. The team is hopeful the veteran WR will return to practice the week of August 31, but that remains to be seen. Given Evans' injury history, it would not be surprising to see San Francisco play it safe with the 33-year-old in the final two weeks of camp. As of now, he is likely to play in Week 1, but this is a situation that should be closely monitored over the next two weeks ahead of the regular season opener. Malik Nabers NYG | 23 Years Old ACL + Meniscus Surgery Date: October 28, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited in Training Camp, Questionable for Week 1 Nabers suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 against the Chargers, tearing the ACL in his right knee. It was later revealed that the talented WR also suffered additional damage to the meniscus, which has implications for his short-term recovery. In the long run, getting that structure repaired is beneficial for the health of the knee, but it will make his recovery in 2026 more cumbersome. Nabers underwent surgery in late October, just before Halloween, giving him less than one year of rehab before the start of the regular season. Generally speaking, most elite athletes recovering from an isolated ACL injury can return to the field in roughly 9-10 months. With the extra rehab time required to account for the meniscus, that timeline is usually pushed back 6-8 weeks. Because of that, Nabers is uncertain for Week 1, and there is an outside chance he could begin the regular season on PUP, especially after he required a second "clean up" procedure in the spring. He will be limited throughout the majority of training camp, but the good news is that Nabers was participating in individual drills in late July. Look for Nabers to ramp up slowly throughout August as he regains confidence in the knee. If the Giants believe he can play before Week 4, he's likely to avoid beginning the season on PUP. Look for Nabers to return closer to his pre-injury level of play in the back half of 2026 and really bounce back in a big way in 2027. Rashee Rice KC | 26 Years Old Right Knee "Clean up" Procedure Surgery Date: May 2026 Return Timeline: Likely limited to begin Training Camp; Cleared for Week 1 Rashee Rice's 2024 season came to an early end when he suffered a season-ending right knee injury. That injury included a torn lateral collateral ligament (LCL) and damage to the postero-lateral corner (PLC) and hamstring tendon. After rehabbing throughout the 2025 offseason, Rice returned to full strength last year and was productive when on the field. However, news broke in mid-May that Rice required a "clean up" procedure on his surgically repaired right knee in order to remove "loose debris." While this isolated procedure doesn't require a lengthy rehab, it does add some volatility to Rice's short and long-term outlook. PLC injuries can be complex, and it is not uncommon for these types of injuries to also include some sort of cartilage damage. The fact that Rice required a second follow-up procedure to remove loose bodies suggests this is probably the case for the Kansas City WR. I do ultimately expect him to be limited to begin training camp, but he should be cleared for Week 1. The key here is whether or not this secondary procedure helps relieve the knee irritation that had been bothering him recently. There is also a second layer to this whole story in that Rice rehabbed while in jail as he served a 30-day sentence shortly after having this second procedure. All in all, Rice is likely to be okay for the 2026 season, but the cartilage injury makes it possible that this isn't the last time we hear about knee problems in the future. Alec Pierce IND | 26 Years Old Left Ankle Surgery Surgery Date: Spring 2026 (Exact date unknown) Return Timeline: Limited to begin camp; Likely ready for Week 1 Alec Pierce is coming off a career year in 2025 and is back with the Colts after signing a massive deal in free agency. Indy is certainly counting on him to take a step forward as the leader of the offense with Michael Pittman Jr. now in Pittsburgh. While it is still possible for Pierce to regain his form this season, it wouldn't be surprising to see him get off to a slower start as he's recovering from an ankle procedure in the spring. As of this writing, the specifics of that surgery aren't known, but Pierce was seen at Colts OTAs with a sleeve on his left calf while observing practice. In that video, his left calf appears to be atrophied, and his ankle range of motion appears limited. With this new information available, Pierce will be limited to being training camp as he regains full strength and explosiveness off that left leg. Given that Pierce's offseason participation will be cut short, he could get off to a slower start in 2026, especially with his QB recovering from Achilles surgery. On July 27, the Colts placed Pierce on the PUP list to begin camp and as of August 10, he is yet to return to practice. Emeka Egbuka TB | 23 Years Old Turf Toe Return Timeline: Situation to Monitor; Questionable for Week 1 Emeka Egbuka left practice on Wednesday, August 12, with what is being described as a toe sprain after getting rolled up on at joint practices. The exact details of the injury aren't known, but the most likely outcome here is a turf toe type of injury, with multiple local beat reporters suggesting the WR will have an MRI to further evaluate the injury. For now, we will await more details on imaging for Tampa's WR1. If this is on the more mild side, Egbuka could return in 1-2 weeks. A moderate sprain could sideline him for multiple weeks and limit him into late August/early September and put his Week 1 status in jeopardy. Regardless, expect the Bucs to be conservative here in an effort to avoid this injury lingering into the regular season. Makai Lemon PHI | 22 Years Old Hamstring Strain Return Timeline: Limited throughout Training Camp, Questionable for Week 1 The Eagles' first round pick, Makai Lemon, originally injured his hamstring in the spring, forcing him to miss a portion of the team's offseason program. Unfortunately, he's dealing with a second hamstring injury in training camp, which has forced him to miss the majority of team practices through the first two weeks. The team has not provided specific details on the severity of the injury, but given his hamstring injury from spring, I'd expect the team to be cautious throughout camp and the preseason. There's no indication from the team that he'll miss regular season games, but it's reasonable to expect the rookie to get off to a slow start. He returned to practice on August 20. Luther Burden III CHI | 22 Years Old Groin Strain Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 Luther Burden left Bears' practice on Saturday, August 8 with a groin injury and did not return. Upon further testing, he is expected to miss the entirety of the preseason, but multiple reports indicate that the team is hopeful he's available for Week 1. Based on that timeline, this is likely a Grade II muscle strain, which carries a recovery timeline of about 4-6 weeks. With Burden missing the majority of training camp, he could be eased into regular season action, but barring a setback, this injury isn't likely to linger beyond September. For now, Burden should be considered Questionable for Week 1. Chris Bell MIA | 22 Years Old ACL Surgery Date: December 2025 Return Timeline: Limited in Training Camp; Could be cleared for Week 1 Chris Bell is a rookie WR out of Louisville who was taken by the Miami Dolphins in the NFL Draft. Some draft analysts suggested that Bell was a late Round 1 talent, but he fell a bit in the draft due to his recovery from a torn ACL. During his final year in school, Bell tore the ACL in his left knee in late November of 2025 and underwent surgery in December. Reportedly, his injury was a clean ACL tear, so the recovery process here should be somewhat straightforward, with Bell likely returning to the field in roughly nine months. That gives him a chance to be cleared for the start of the season, but it is important to understand that Bell will be limited throughout the entirety of the offseason, including training camp after he was placed on the NFI list in late July. Bell was activated off NFI on August 17 and returned to practice on August 24. Even so, for a rookie looking to make the jump from college to the pros, that recovery adds an extra layer to his projection for the 2026 season. Because of the timeline and jump in level of competition, it would be surprising for Bell to make a big impact early in the season. For dynasty managers, the most likely scenario here is that Bell is more of a factor in Year 2 when he is a full season removed from his injury. Ricky Pearsall SF | 25 Years Old PCL Reconstruction Surgery Date: August 2026 Return Timeline: Will miss entire 2026 season Ricky Pearsall will undergo season-ending knee surgery. In the early days of training camp this year, he dealt with swelling in his knee related to his 2025 PCL injury. Pearsall injured his right knee in Week 4 of last year and went on to miss Weeks 5-10 because of a sprained PCL. Videos surfaced of Pearsall working out this summer with a compression sleeve on that right knee, so it is possible that Pearsall has been managing this for some time. These PCL injuries (depending on the severity) do tend to linger, and while most can be rehabbed, some do end up requiring surgery if the athlete continues to experience swelling, pain and/or instability. That PCL reconstruction surgery usually carries a 9-12 month recovery. Given that Pearsall will have his procedure in early August, he should enter 2027 with minimal restrictions, but dynasty managers can expect him to be limited in the early portion of next year's offseason program. Chris Brazzell II CAR | 22 Years Old LCL Sprain Surgery Date: Early August 2026 Return Timeline: Out for the year Carolina's rookie WR, Chris Brazzell, injured his knee in the first few days of training camp. On July 29, he suffered an LCL injury that was initially described as a "moderate" injury that could force him to be sidelined for 6-8 weeks. However, after further tests and evaluation, the team opted to shut him down for the year. He'll undergo surgery on his LCL and be out for the season. It's obviously not ideal to miss his entire rookie season, but this early surgery will allow him to be ready for next year's off-season program. For those with Brazzell in dynasty formats, the recovery here is generally pretty straightforward with good post-surgical results, so he should be able to enter 2027 without limitations. Tyreek Hill FA | 32 Years Old Partial Knee Dislocation Surgery Date: September 30, 2025 Return Timeline: May not play in 2026 Hill's 2025 season came to an abrupt end in Week 4 against the Jets when he suffered a serious left knee injury. During the play, Hill suffered damage to multiple ligaments, cartilage, and surrounding tissues. Unfortunately, this is a 'Tank Dell' type of injury that is going to require at least a year of rehab and recovery, if not longer. One additional concern with this type of dislocation is potential damage to the nerve that wraps around the outside of the knee. All in all, Hill is highly unlikely to be fantasy-relevant at any point in the 2026 season and may not play at all, depending on how his recovery goes. Now 32 years old, Hill's NFL future hangs in the balance, as this injury has the potential to be career-threatening. Travis Hunter JAX | 23 Years Old LCL Surgery Date: November 11, 2025 Return Timeline: Cleared for Training Camp Hunter's rookie season was cut short due to an unfortunate season-ending knee injury that he actually suffered in practice coming out of the bye week. The Swiss-Army Knife CB/WR tore his LCL (ligament on the outside of the knee) and required a procedure to repair the injury. The typical recovery timeline for this type of injury is roughly six months, so Hunter wasn't 100% throughout the early part of the offseason, but he will be cleared for training camp and enter Week 1 healthy. His role moving forward remains to be seen, but his injury is not a concern entering the 2026 regular season. Sam LaPorta DET | 25 Years Old Low Back Surgery / Hip Injury Surgery Date: November 2025 Return Timeline: Likely to play Week 1 Sam LaPorta's 2025 season came to an early end after he required a procedure on his lower back. At the time of the injury, the specifics were unknown, but it's now known that LaPorta's injury is related to a disc issue in his lumbar spine. Generally speaking, the recovery process for this type of injury in the short term is favorable, so I do expect LaPorta to be cleared for training camp, though he is likely to be limited throughout the spring. Moving forward, this injury and surgery now becomes a factor to consider with LaPorta throughout his career. NFL football is a violent sport that puts a lot of stress on the body. Because of the demands of playing in the NFL, it's possible this isn't the last time we hear about LaPorta's back injury during his time in the league. Spine injuries (and specifically disc injuries) can be tricky, and the recurrence rate is decently high, even after a procedure like this. All in all, I expect LaPorta to participate fully in camp and be ready for the 2026 season, but his injury now makes him a slightly more volatile player moving forward. Think of it like this - There's a range of outcomes here with Detroit's TE1. He could play the entire season with zero issues, but it's also possible this flares up again, and depending on the severity, that could cause him to miss time. In addition to monitoring LaPorta's back issue, fantasy gamers will need to track LaPorta's recent hip injury from the week of August 17. The injury appears to be some sort of contusion after he took a hard hit in practice. Fortunately, he returned to practice on August 25, so he should be out there in Week 1. George Kittle SF | 32 Years Old Achilles Surgery Date: January 14, 2026 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Questionable for Week 1 San Francisco's All-Pro TE suffered a torn Achilles in his right leg during the Wild Card Round of the playoffs against Philadelphia. Speaking after his procedure, Kittle shared some insights on his injury, stating, "Surgery went really, really good. [ElAttrache] said best-case scenario when you tear an Achilles is that you tear it up high by your soleus, which is what I did. I had a clean tear. They didn't have to drill into my heel. And where the repair was there's more blood flow. And so it takes some time off of the recovery time... It's not as bad as other ones." Kittle is referencing Dr. Neil ElAttrache, one of the best orthopedic docs in the country, who has performed surgeries on other well-known NFL players over the years. I could go on and on about the specifics of what Kittle shared, but basically, the TLDR for fantasy managers is that Kittle suffered a mid-tendon injury, closer to where the tendon meets the muscle tissue of the calf. That is overall good news, as the outcomes do tend to be more favorable with this type of injury compared to those that involve the insertion of the tendon at the heel bone. Now, that doesn't mean Kittle will miraculously be 100% for Week 1, but it does give him a chance to contribute to the 49ers at some point early in the regular season. From a fantasy perspective, Kittle is a long shot to be on our radar as a top option, the way he has been for the last decade. This is still a mid-January injury, he's 33 years old (younger is better for this injury), and the recovery for this procedure is still going to be 9+ months. From there, he will need additional time to ramp up, which means he's unlikely to be 100% (pre-injury level of play) at any point in the first half of the 2026 season. The Niners activated Kittle off PUP on August 23, signaling that he's very likely to avoid the PUP list to begin the season. He remains Questionable for Week 1. Tucker Kraft GB | 25 Years Old ACL Surgery Date: November 2025 Return Timeline: Limited in Training Camp, Likely cleared for Week 1 Kraft tore his ACL in his right knee in Week 9 against the Panthers, ending an impressive 2025 campaign. Following the season, he spoke with reporters and confirmed his injury did include slight damage to the LCL (ligament on the outside of the knee) and the meniscus, but neither structure needed to be repaired. As a result, we can largely treat this injury as an isolated ACL reconstruction, which means his recovery will likely take somewhere between 9-10 months. Given that Kraft's surgery took place in November, he will have roughly 10 months until the start of the season to rehab. That at least gives him a chance to be cleared for Week 1, though he'll be limited throughout training camp. Fantasy managers should expect Kraft to get off to a slower start, but he should be able to regain his pre-injury level of play as the season progresses. Kenyon Sadiq NYJ | 21 Years Old Core Muscle Repair Surgery Date: Spring 2026 Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 The Jets' rookie TE and first round pick missed most of the spring while recovering from a sports hernia surgery. Generally speaking, these procedures are reliable when it comes to healing and recovery, but at times, athletes can deal with groin or abdominal soreness when ramping up activity. At the start of camp, head coach Aaron Glenn noted that Sadiq had a "setback" and would likely miss a few weeks, though he did express optimism over his Week 1 availability. All in all, I'm not overly worried about Sadiq's ability to get healthy and contribute as a rookie, but he'll have missed almost the entirety of the team's offseason program, so it's fair to question his conditioning and readiness to contribute right away. Expect a bit of a slower start as he's eased into NFL action.

notes.free_agency: Free Agency Review Home   >   2026 Ultimate Draft Kit   >  UDK – Free Agency Review Fantasy implications for the biggest offseason moves QB RB WR TE Free Agents re-signed Daniel Jones Re-signed | 29 Years Old IND | 2 years, $88 million Danny Dimes went to Indy last year to challenge Anthony Richardson for the starting gig, and not only did he win that job in camp, he had his team headed towards a top seed in the AFC until...Week 14. Unfortunately, the Colts' season went south real quick after Jones tore his Achilles. When he was the starter in Weeks 1-13, the Colts were 8-4, and Jones was the QB7 in fantasy. Talk about a late-round value, especially in SuperFlex leagues! Entering 2026, Jones is back in Indy after the Colts used the transition tag on him then re-signed him to a new two-year deal worth up to $100 million. For fantasy, with much of his value tied to his ability to contribute with his legs, it remains to be seen if 2026 will be as successful for Jones given his Achilles injury. The front office and coaching staff is essentially betting their jobs and Jones returning to form. We'll see! signed Malik Willis Signed | 27 Years Old MIA | 3 years, $67.5 million Willis' time in Tennessee was pretty forgettable to say the least. The team took him in the third round back in 2022 and moved on after just three starts in two years. However, he landed in Green Bay as Jordan Love's backup and now has a chance to revitalize his career as a starter after getting some great coaching from Matt LaFleur. We've seen other young QBs (Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, Daniel Jones, for example) take similar paths: Dumped by their original organization, sit and learn for a couple of years as a backup, and then get a second chance at a starting gig elsewhere. Could Willis be next? He lands in Miami with new head coach Jeff Hafley, who comes over from the Packers, so this signing makes a lot of sense. For fantasy, the Dolphins project to be among the worst teams in the league, but we know what works at the QB position for the game we play - elite rushing upside, and Willis certainly has the wheels to put up fantasy friendly numbers on the ground. signed Kyler Murray Signed | 29 Years Old MIN | 1 year, $1.3 million The Kyler Murray era in Arizona is officially coming to a close with the Cardinals set to move on. Still just 28 years old, Kyler will look to get his career back on track in Minnesota, perhaps following the path of guys like Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold. This move makes all the sense in the world for Kevin O'Connell's team. They're short on cash this year in terms of cap space, and with Arizona picking up the vast majority of is salary this year, they were able to sign him for the vet minimum. Expect the team to frame this as a QB competition throughout the summer, but if you watched JJ "Nine" McCarthy play NFL football in 2025, you likely know where this is headed in terms of the Week 1 starter. signed Tua Tagovailoa Signed | 28 Years Old ATL | 1 year The Dolphins and Mike McDaniel had some nice seasons there in Miami, but they couldn't get over the hump, and as a result, the franchise is undergoing a facelift this offseason with a brand new GM and head coach. The previous regime gave Tua a four-year, $212 million deal a couple of years back, and now the Tua era is officially over as the team is designating him as a post-June 1 cut. It's going to hurt, but Miami is going the Russell Wilson route and eating a ton of dead money as they look to rest the franchise. In fact, they're eating an NFL record $99M in dead money over the next two seasons. Looking for some insurance for Michael Penix coming off a torn ACL, the Falcons signed another lefty to a cheap one-year deal with the Dolphins paying the vast majority of his salary. signed Kirk Cousins Signed | 38 Years Old LV | 1 year, $11.3 million Kirko Chainz' agent is the GOAT. This man just keeps getting fully guaranteed deals and cashing those checks. He's made over $320 million in his career...sheesh! Good for you, Kirk. The Raiders signed Cousins to what is essentially a one-year deal worth about $20 million given that the Falcons are picking up some of the salary for 2026. He'll mentor Fernando Mendoza and potentially even start for part of the season while the Raiders groom there eventual franchise QB. For fantasy, Cousins is obviously not the prolific passer he used to be, but hopefully he can keep the offense on track to ensure Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty deliver for our fantasy rosters. re-signed Aaron Rodgers Re-signed | 42 Years Old PIT | 1 year, up to $25 million Rodgers spent the majority of last offseason pondering his NFL future before landing in Pittsburgh on a one-year deal with Mike Tomlin. In classic Steelers fashion, Rodgers did enough to help them stay competitive and make the playoffs, but they ultimately fell short in the Wild Card Round. At this point in his career, the vet isn't really on the radar for fantasy outside of 2QB formats. Now 42 years old, Rodgers and the Steelers seemed like a one-year fling, but they hired his old coach, Mike McCarthy, to replace Tomlin, so they'll reunite one last time while Pittsburgh. We're not expecting Rodgers to suddenly turn back the clock and support multiple high-end fantasy options, but he's certainly a better option than guys like Drew Allar or Will Howard. re-signed Marcus Mariota Re-signed | 32 Years Old WAS | 1 year, $7 million The former Oregon Duck has spent the last two seasons in Washington as Jayden Daniels' backup, and when Daniels has missed time because of injury, Mariota has filled in admirably. Washington re-signed him to a one-year deal in free agency to keep some continuity in the QB room. For fantasy, we've seen him continue to post usable numbers when he's been under center, thanks mainly to his ability to run. In seven full stars last year with the Commanders, Mariota averaged 17.2 fantasy points per game, giving him life as a streamer if and when his number gets called. Russell Wilson Unsigned | 37 Years Old Russ was named the starter in New York coming out of camp, but we all knew it was a matter of when, not if, Jaxson Dart would take over. The most cringe QB in the league only lasted three games before the rook got his shot and ran away with the job. This is probably where the road ends for Mr. Unliiiiimited. He says he believes he can still be a starter in the league, but after bouncing around from Denver to Pittsburgh to New York the last three years, it sure feels like the NFL says otherwise. Free Agents re-signed Breece Hall Re-Signed | 25 Years Old NYJ | 3 years, $45.8 million It feels like Breece has already lived nine lives in the NFL (playing for the Jets will do that), but he's still not even 25 years old. One of the most productive and efficient backs over the last three seasons, the Jets rewarded Breece with a brand new three-year deal worth just over $15 million per year. Some dynasty managers out there may have been hoping for Breece to finally be unleashed on a new team and hopefully better offense, but this contract says he'll get plenty of volume in New York. We're not all that optimistic about the team in 2026, but if they can land a stud QB in next year's draft, perhaps New York can finally get it going and unlock Breece's full potential. signed Kenneth Walker Signed | 25 Years Old KC | 3 years, up to $45 million Ken Bone! Walker was a key piece of the Seattle offense on their Super Bowl run, and now that Zach Charbonnet is coming off a January ACL injury, the Seahawks have a major need at RB with Walker hitting free agency. Usually, in situations like this, where the team has so much success, they look to bring back key contributors, but Walker hit the open market and got a big old bag of money from the Chiefs, signing a 3-year deal worth just over $14M per year. He's still only 25 years old and remains one of the best home run hitters in the game, something that was severely lacking in KC's run game over the last two years. For context, over the last two years Chiefs RBs have run for 10+ yards less than 9% of the time, 31st amongst 32 teams. Enter Walker, who was third in the league last season in rate of 10+ yard runs. He'll bring stability to the backfield and should be heavily featured, especially with Mahomes coming off the ACL. signed Travis Etienne Jr. Signed | 27 Years Old NO | 4 yrs, up to $52 million Etienne bounced back from a disappointing 2024 season and was one of the biggest values in 2025 drafts, given the uncertainty around his role and standing on the depth chart with the new staff under Liam Cohen. Despite being drafted outside of the top-24 RBs, Etienne finished as the RB10 thanks to his workhorse volume. He was one of just 13 backs a year ago with 300+ total opportunities, and after that bounce-back season, he was rewarded in free agency with a multi-year deal with the Saints. re-signed Javonte Williams Re-Signed | 26 Years Old DAL | 3 years, $24 million One of the best fantasy stories in 2025 has to be the resurgence of Javonte Williams as Dallas' RB1. His career got derailed by that complex ACL injury in his second season as a Bronco, but the talent was never the question. Now healthy, we saw what made Javonte such an exciting prospect coming out of UNC. Among qualified RBs, Javonte was fourth in yards after contact per attempt, and he was one of just 10 NFL backs with double-digit rushing scores. After a bounce-back season, Dallas rewarded him with a 3-year extension that includes $16 million in guaranteed money. He'll be the Cowboys' bell cow for the next couple of seasons after averaging almost 19 total opportunities per game last year. re-signed J.K. Dobbins Re-signed | 27 Years Old DEN | 2 years, up to $20 million What a fun story Dobbins was in 2024 and then again in 2025. After tearing his Achilles in Week 1 of 2023, he signed a league minimum deal with the Chargers that included just $50K in guarantees, yet played a 63% of the snaps in 2024. The long-term durability is still a big concern, especially considering he missed four weeks with a sprained MCL in his surgically reconstructed knee in 2024 then spent the final two months on IR with a season-ending foot injury in 2025. Dobbins proved these last two years that he can at function in a timeshare. He's back with Sean Payton and Denver on a two-year deal, forming a committee with last year's second-rounder RJ Harvey. While we still expect Harvey to see high-value looks in the pass game, Dobbins should have FLEX-worthy weeks in the right matchup while running behind one of, if not the, best offensive lines in football. signed Rico Dowdle Signed | 28 Years Old PIT | 2 yrs, up to $12 million After Chuba got hurt last year, Rico essentially stole the RB1 role in Carolina, and he was productive with his opportunities. Mr. "Two Pumps" Dowdle rushed for 1,076 yards this past season and ran for a career high six TDs as the leader of the committee in Carolina. Dowdle has been the lead guy for two different teams now, and while he may not be an elite talent, the guy just gets the job done. During the last two years in Dallas and Carolina, he's shown he can be reliable with 200+ touches in a season. He lands in Pittsburgh reunited with Mike McCarthy teamming up with Jaylen Warren. signed Kenny Gainwell Signed | 27 Years Old TB | 2 years, up to $14 million It pays to be in Aaron Rodgers' inner circle, just ask Kenny G! He signed a one-year deal worth just under $2M last offseason after spending the first part of his career in Philly as a third-down back and kick returner. Of course, most of us weren't expecting much from Gainwell given his track record and the minimal investment, but goodness gracious, he was a force in PPR formats thanks to his team-leading 73 receptions. The only backs with more catches? CMC, Bijan, and Jahmyr Gibbs. The Buccaneers signed Gainwell to a 2-year deal to mix in with Bucky Irving. He will never be a workhorse in the league, but he offers an NFL franchise a valuable skill set as a pass catcher out of the backfield. signed Tyler Allgeier Signed | 26 Years Old ARI | 2 yrs, $12 million Allgeier has spent the last couple of seasons as the 'thunder' to Bijan Robinson's 'lightning' in Atlanta. A dependable early-down runner who's been productive at the goal line, Allgeier was going to mix in a Arizona backfield alongside Trey Benson and James Conner. However, the Cardinals threw a curve ball and drafted Jeremiyah Love 3rd overall. Sorry Tyler! For fantasy, he probably remains a rosterable FLEX with benefits, similar to what we saw over the last couple of years with the Falcons. signed Chris Rodriguez Jr. Signed | 25 Years Old JAX | 2 years, $10 million CROD! Rodriguez landed a nice two-year deal with the Jaguars in free agency, signing for $6.2M guaranteed. It may not seem like a ton, but considering he got more guaranteed money than Rico Dowdle, the money says he could have a role in Liam Coen's offense. He played his college ball at Kentucky when Liam Coen was on the staff, and in that season, he logged 238 touches. He hasn't really done much in the NFL thus far, but the familiarity in Coen's system and guaranteed money at least adds some threat to Bhayshul Tuten's early-down role in 2026. signed Emanuel Wilson Signed | 27 Years Old SEA | 1 year, $2.1 million After losing Ken Walker in free agency and Zach Charbonnet to a torn ACL in mid January during their Super Bowl run, there's a massive opportunity up for grabs in this Seahawks backfield. The team spent a late 1st on Jadarian Price who should eventually be the lead back. Wilson, who's 26 years old, is coming off a career high 142 total opportunities as Josh Jacobs' backup last season in Green Bay and flashed in a major way with his lone start in Week 12 with Jacobs sidelined. signed Keaton Mitchell Signed | 24 Years Old LAC | 2 years, $9.25 million After flashing off and on over the last couple of years in Baltimore behind Derrick Henry, Keaton Mitchell lands in LA on a two-year deal with $5M guaranteed. He brings a speed element to Mike McDaniel's scheme and is a great fit in the offense given his burst and big play ability on the edge. He's likely to slide in as the RB2 behind Omarion Hampton and could be one of fantasy's top insurance backs for an offense that should win plenty of games. signed Rachaad White Signed | 27 Years Old WAS | 1 year, $2 million 'Dick White,' as he's known around TFFB HQ, is going to be donning new colors in 2026 after spending the first four years of his career in Tampa. White was the guy a couple of seasons ago, but he was relegated to a change-of-pace option with the emergence of the more efficient Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker over the last two years. For context, his opportunities per game have declined from 20.1 to 12.6 to 10.4 over the last three seasons. Already 27 years old, White gets a short-term deal to join a committee in Washington where he can specialize as a pass catcher and in pass protection while playing with his former college QB in Jayden Daniels. signed Isiah Pacheco Signed | 27 Years Old DET | 1 year He burned too bright! Pacheco is the perfect example of what can happen to a Day 3 back in the NFL. Despite being the workhorse for Andy Reid during the back half of his rookie year and during his second season, Pacheco was never the same after he fractured his fibula in 2024, and ultimately, he ended up in a time share with Kareem Hunt. Given that the former seventh-rounder is coming off yet another injury-plagued and inefficient season, his future for fantasy is murky at best. He lands in Detroit on a one-year deal to backup Jahmyr Gibbs. signed Brian Robinson Signed | 27 Years Old ATL | 1 year, $2.5 million B Rob was the early down back in Washington in 2023 and 2024, but the team moved off him in favor of BILL CROSKEY, sending him to San Francisco via trade just before the start of the season. With CMC seeing a million opportunities and staying healthy all year (#Blessed), Robinson was nothing more than a backup in 2025 as he appeared on just 17% of the offensive snaps. He was an older prospect coming out of Bama, so he's already entering his age-27 season. The market wasn't hot and heavy for Robinson, so he landed in Atlanta on a cheap one-year deal. Obviously, this is the Bijan show (don't click the wrong B Rob in your draft!), but with Tyler Allgeier vacating almost 160 opportunities, Brian could have a role behind Bijan. We don't anticipate much consistent production as long as Bijan is healthy, but Brian becomes of the few high priority backups late in drafts. Joe Mixon Unsigned | 30 Years Old Congratulate yourself for scoring as many fantasy points as Joe Mixon in 2025. The Texans cut the veteran for only $2 million and save themselves a solid $8 million against the cap. He will be entering his ninth year in the league at age 30 and coming off a mysterious foot injury, which is not ideal for a free agent RB. After the team traded for David Montgomery, Mixon's NFL future hangs in the balance. Kareem Hunt Unsigned | 31 Years Old Kareem Hunt is like those three-day-old leftovers in the back of your fridge. Will it get the job done for dinner if you are hungry? Sure. Are you going to impress your guests after popping that Tupperware in the microwave? Of course not. If your NFL team needs a 30-year-old back who can pile up touches en route to 3.5 yards per carry and a cloud of dust, Hunt is your guy. Nick Chubb Unsigned | 30 Years Old What's the saying? "Don't cry because it's over, smile because it happened." Let's remember the good times for Mr. Chubb. One of the most dominant runners in the league over the last decade, the wily old veteran is now entering the final stage of his NFL career. After Joe Mixon's mysterious foot injury caused him to miss the entire season, Houston signed him to a one-year deal last year, and ultimately, he was phased out as the year went on. If you're a fan of Nick Chubb, it was at least awesome to see him play a full season one more time after he suffered that nasty second knee injury in 2023, then broke his foot in 2024. Perhaps he lands a one-year deal for an NFL team shopping on the value menu, but it wouldn't be surprising for him to be a guy who signs late in the process as he weighs his NFL future. Free Agents franchise George Pickens Franchise Tag | 25 Years Old DAL | 1 year, $27.3 million Back up the Brinks truck. George made himself a pile of cash this year, showcasing the type of weekly boom potential and alpha status teams dream of at the WR position. Pickens had five weeks inside the top 10 and led the league in receiving yards off slant routes. He is a game breaker, and we expect Jerry Jones to work out a long-term deal. They used the franchise tag on George as a place holder, but expect something in the neighborhood of $30+ million if he strikes a multi-year contract. signed Mike Evans Signed | 33 Years Old SF | 3 years, up to $60.4 million As they, "All good things must come to an end." It's going to be really weird seeing the future Hall-of-Famer where a different jersey in 2026, but Mike Evans is officially headed for San Francisco. The 32-year-old vet only played in eight games last year due to multiple injuries (hamstring, broken collarbone, and concussion), so this signing does come with some risk, but he's still one of the top X receivers in the game. Fantasy Implications for Coaching Moves This Offseason Head Coach Mike LaFleur, ARI The younger LaFleur brother comes to the desert after years soaking up knowledge in the McVay and Shanahan coaching systems. The Cardinals averaged 40 pass attempts per game in Jacoby Brissett starts last year and project to be among the worst teams in the NFL, currently sitting at 4.5 for their win total. We expect that passing volume to slightly come down as he integrates third overall pick Jeremiyah Love into the offense. Head Coach Kevin Stefanski, ATL The former two-time NFL Coach of the Year was let go in Cleveland and now finds a home in Atlanta. Good luck, Kevin! The Falcons have not had a winning season since 2017, the second-longest streak in the NFL. His offenses consistently were among the best at running the football, ranking top 10 in rush attempts every year from 2019 to 2023. All-Pro RB Bijan Robinson is the centerpiece, but the question remains if you have two QBs (Tua & Penix), do you truly have none? Head Coach Jesse Minter, BAL The former Chargers defensive coordinator takes over for long-time legend John Harbaugh. He looks to bring the same intensity on the defensive side of the ball; hopefully, with a full season from QB Lamar Jackson and one last run from fantasy legend Derrick Henry. The Ravens are the favorites in a tough AFC North projected for 10.5 wins. Head Coach Joe Brady, BUF Apparently, sporting a 12-5 record was not good enough for Bills ownership, as long-time HC Sean McDermott was axed and Brady was promoted from offensive coordinator. The Bills led the NFL in rush attempts inside the red zone as Josh Allen and James Cook formed an incredible duo. The question will be if the acquisition of DJ Moore helps the WR room progress forward, and the Bills finally break through in the AFC playoffs. Head Coach Todd Monken, CLE At 60 years old, this is Monken’s first head-coaching gig in the NFL after being an offensive coordinator for Baltimore the last two years and numerous other stops. The data is not kind to old head coaches: among eight first-time head coaches over the last 25 years that were 55+ years old, they averaged 6.4 wins in Year 1, and only two of those coaches lasted more than three years. Monken is inheriting a team of brown-stained pants that punted the ball (93 times) more than any other team in the NFL and averaged just 5.0 yards per attempt. Woof. The QB play is a massive question mark moving forward. Head Coach Klint Kubiak, LV Kubes! After leading the Seahawks offense to a Super Bowl title, Kubiak was the prized coaching hire of the off-season. He will need to fix a Raiders offense that was dead last in points and yards per game last season. In fact, the team had five total rushing TDs on the season! Expect No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza to slowly be integrated as he holds the clipboard behind Kirk Cousins. Oh, and expect Brock Bowers to see 10+ targets a game. Head Coach Jeff Hafley, MIA After two seasons as the Green Bay defensive coordinator, Hafley takes over in Miami for a team that clearly is rebuilding. The Dolphins' defense is a project after allowing the third-highest completion percentage (72%) in NFL history last year. After drafting offensive line and defensive pieces early in the draft, fantasy managers will need to have patience as everyone but De’Von Achane is a mystery to us. Head Coach John Harbaugh, NYG Depending on who you talk to, Harbaugh is either a living legend (most road playoff wins in NFL history) or someone who fell short of expectations (just one Super Bowl). Regardless, he represents a major culture change in New York for a team with an exciting core of offensive players (Dart-Skattebo-Nabers) and a nasty pass rush on defense. Depending on the recovery timeline for their offensive stars, the Giants are on our short list of teams that could surprise in 2026. Head Coach Mike McCarthy, PIT Haven’t we seen this movie before? Mike McCarthy, former Green Bay and Dallas head coach, ventures to another storied NFL franchise, potentially reuniting with his buddy Aaron Rodgers. It will be strange to see a non-Mike Tomlin coach on the sidelines as the Steelers routinely outperformed expectations. For 2026, keep in mind Pittsburgh has a “first-place schedule” adding games against Denver and road games in New England and Philadelphia. Woof. Head Coach Robert Saleh, TEN After piecing together a broken 49ers defense last year, Saleh was hired in Tennessee to right the ship for an organization desperate to regain their edge. The Titans' offense was tied or trailing on 84% of their offensive snaps in a mostly abysmal season for No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward. The Titans find themselves in a highly competitive AFC South, albeit with the arrow pointing up on their potential. Offensive Coordinator Nathaniel Hackett, ARI Do not ask us how this man continues to be employed in the NFL. The former OC and one-year failed head coach experiment in Denver was a “defensive analyst” last year in Green Bay. This is LaFleur’s ship, and Hackett is aboard simply to provide his offensive “expertise”, whatever that means. Offensive Coordinator Tommy Rees, ATL The former Notre Dame QB follows Kevin Stefanski from Cleveland and will be calling plays for the Falcons. The offensive play-makers between Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts are certainly top-tier, but the Falcons’ success will ultimately come down to the QB play. Both Stefanski and Rees have mentioned establishing a “wide zone” run scheme throughout their press conferences. Offensive Coordinator Declan Doyle, BAL After a year as Ben Johnson’s offensive coordinator in Chicago, the 30-year-old Doyle will be calling plays in Baltimore. The Ravens ran the ball on 55% of their “early downs” (the highest rate in the NFL) as the Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry combo remains the heartbeat of the offense. Baltimore does have to replace a number of key pieces on the offensive line, fullback Patrick Ricard, and two TEs, so perhaps we see some innovation in 3-wide sets for 2026. Offensive Coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr., BUF The former long-time Saints offensive coordinator latches on to Buffalo serving under Joe Brady, someone who was Carmichael’s offensive assistant back in New Orleans. This is Brady’s offense so Pete is OC in title only. Offensive Coordinator Press Taylor, CHI Zac Taylor’s younger brother will have the esteemed privilege of being Ben Johnson’s “yes man” in Chicago. He is being promoted from passing game coordinator to OC but play-calling duties remain with Johnson. The Bears jumped from 28th in points per game (18.2) to 9th (25.9) in 2025; that is the 6th largest year-to-year jump (7.7 ppg) over the last decade. Offensive Coordinator Travis Switzer, CLE The former Baltimore run-game coordinator follows Todd Monken to Cleveland in hopes of fixing an offense that completed just 57.9% of their passes last year. That putrid passing mark ranks 305th out of 320 NFL teams over the last decade. The Browns did add several high-end WRs in the draft, hoping to give the team more pass-catching threats than just TE Harold Fannin Jr. and the WR formerly known as Jerry Jeudy. Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb, DEN The 31-year-old Webb was a hot commodity this offseason, interviewing with multiple teams for the head coaching positions. Instead, he remains in Denver and gets elevated to OC. Sean Payton declared that Webb will be taking over play-calling duties, trying to restore some of the passing efficiency numbers for Bo Nix. Offensive Coordinator Drew Petzing, DET Affectionately known as the “Blob Fish” on our podcast, Petzing parlayed a couple of years in the Arizona desert to another OC job alongside Dan Campbell. The Lions had a massive drop in rushing efficiency last year after Ben Johnson left town. Petzing’s goal will be to “restore the roar” of a top-5 scoring offense and take advantage of their “fourth place schedule”. Trey McBride came out after the hire and said Petzing’s scheme could mean great things for Sam LaPorta in Detroit. Offensive Coordinator Eric Bieniemy, KC The longtime KC offensive coordinator in the early Patrick Mahomes era (2018-2022) returns after three different jobs in three years. This offense needs a facelift after Kansas City had four total offensive plays of 20+ yards that resulted in a TD last year, tied for the fewest in the NFL. The running game was also pitiful, producing just one total 20+ yard run on the season. The arrival of Kenneth Walker III should help, but the Chiefs' overall offensive ceiling depends on Mahomes’ return from a major injury. Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel, LAC Love him or hate him, McDaniel is a lightning rod for fantasy production. The former Dolphins head coach will have tons of weapons at his disposal and hopefully a full, healthy offensive line. The Chargers will not want Justin Herbert to repeat last year when he led all QBs in rushing yards via scrambles, and led the league in % of pressured dropbacks (43%). Expect even ancillary speed threats like Keaton Mitchell and rookie Brenen Thompson to be worked in alongside main fantasy options of Omarion Hampton and Ladd McConkey. This offense is going to be one of our favorites to keep an eye on in training camp and pre-season. Offensive Coordinator Nate Scheelhaase, LAR The Rams' offensive coordinator position is an honorary title, as Sean McVay is the one who rules the roost. However, keep in mind the running list of current head coaches in the league who have recently held this position: Mike LaFleur, Liam Coen, Kevin O’Connell, Matt LaFleur… Scheelhaase has rave reviews from many throughout the league, so do not be surprised if he is on the short list of potential head coaches in 2027. Offensive Coordinator Andrew Janocko, LV Janocko (pronounced juh-NO-co) is a Klint Kubiak buddy who was with him in their last couple of stops in Seattle, New Orleans, and Minnesota. He follows him to Las Vegas to try to fix an offense that averaged just 11.5 points per game on the road last year, by far the worst in the NFL. Janocko’s reputation as QB whisperer will come in handy in developing No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza and keeping Kirk Cousins flush with Kohl’s Cash. Offensive Coordinator Bobby Slowik, MIA Slowik was a hot commodity in coaching circles after guiding C.J. Stroud to a breakout rookie season in 2023. However, things headed south the following year, and he was let go. After spending a year as Miami’s senior passing game coordinator, he was promoted to offensive coordinator and play-caller under this new Dolphins regime. Bobby will have his work cut out for him connecting new QB Malik Willis with a group of barf-worthy pass-catching options. Seriously, stop what you are doing right now and go look at the Dolphins' WR depth chart. Apologies for what you are about to see. Offensive Coordinator Matt Nagy, NYG He’s back! The man known as the “Budget Magician” on our podcast moves from offensive coordinator in Kansas City to play-caller in New York. The Giants have some exciting young pieces, as the offense was competitive in almost every Jaxson Dart start last year. The team quietly ranked top half in points per game and yards per game, and with a bit of injury luck, you can see a path forward for this team being in the mix in the NFC East. Offensive Coordinator Frank Reich, NYJ Reich wins the title of oldest offensive coordinator (64 years young) in the league, which is wild considering the average age of the other 31 OCs is 41 years. We are not quite sure if Aaron Glenn and the Jets front office had an updated resume for Reich, as he was out of the NFL for the last two years. We would put the odds quite low that he remains in this position for 2027. Offensive Coordinator Sean Mannion, PHI The Eagles are a funny bunch as they have ping-ponged from Super Bowl years (2022 & 2024) to playoff disappointments (2023 & 2025) recently. Part of the equation was the offensive coordinator position changing every single year. Mannion is an up-and-coming name from the Packers coaching tree. He will be bent on restoring Saquon Barkley and the Eagles' big-play rushing offense, alongside a bevy of new pass-catchers in the mix. He will be taking over play-calling duties as Nick Sirianni remains in his “CEO-coaching” style. Offensive Coordinator Brian Angelichio, PIT The former Vikings passing game coordinator joins Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh. One quote from a front office executive caught our eye: "I've been around football for 40 years, and I've never met a guy [Angelichio] who is more obsessed with football." Breaking news: Guy who works in football ... likes football! This is earth-shattering stuff! Offensive Coordinator Brian Fleury, SEA After years working as the TEs coach for Kyle Shanahan in San Francisco, Fleury joins an NFC West division rival, inheriting the big shoes of Klint Kubiak. It does help that Fleury worked with Sam Darnold when he was a 49er in 2023, and this might be one of the most well-run organizations in football. Keep in mind, Seattle was incredibly healthy all year long with the third fewest “games lost” due to injury in the NFL. Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson, TB After two years calling plays in Atlanta, Robinson linked up with division rival Tampa Bay, becoming Baker Mayfield’s fifth different offensive coordinator over the last five years. The Buccaneers suffered multiple injuries on offense last year, and Baker averaged the lowest yards per attempt (4.99) versus man coverage in the league. Nevertheless, in a weak NFC South division, the Buccaneers can still make noise with some of their young offensive playmakers. Offensive Coordinator Brian Daboll, TEN The Titans were straight diaper gravy on offense last year, ranking 30th in points per game and 31st in yards per game. Daboll’s success as a play-caller should make Cam Ward a great bet for a sophomore step forward. Over the last decade, QBs drafted in the top 10 averaged 2.6 more fantasy points per game in Year 2. Expect a higher pass rate and a chance for multiple pass-catchers to enter the fantasy conversation, something we could not say last year in Tennessee. Offensive Coordinator David Blough, WAS At just 30 years old, Blough is the second youngest OC in the NFL considering he was a backup QB in the league as recently as 2023! He steps into an incredible spot as Jayden Daniels’ play-caller after being the team's QB coach under Kliff Kingsbury. After Daniels and Terry McLaurin appeared in just three total games together in 2025, we can expect better luck in 2026. Washington quietly has been effective running the ball the last few years, so the key factors in the offense will be the emergence of another pass-catcher opposite Terry. Will that be free agent signee Chig Okonkwo or third-round rookie Antonio Williams?
